events.label: Royal Commission on Reorganisation of Indian Army appointed — the Peel Commission (Major-General Jonathan Peel, also Secretary of State for War 1858-59; younger brother of Sir Robert Peel who created modern London police); goal: design 'coup-proof' colonial army

Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1 November 1858 — (i) Crown sovereign of India; (ii) religious tolerance promised; (iii) governance per India's own traditions + customs; (iv) socio-religious reforms + promotion of Christianity shelved; GOI Act 1858 enacted: (a) EIC rule replaced by direct Crown rule; (b) Secretary of State for India (full Cabinet member) replaces President of Board of Control; (c) Mughal sovereignty legally ended; Zafar37-57 exiled to Rangoon Burma (dies 1862)
Peel Commission submits report — recommendations implemented through combination of legislation + executive military orders

European Forces (India) Act 1860 — abolishes EIC's separate European army; merges those soldiers into regular British Crown Army; triggers 'White Mutiny' among EIC European soldiers (resisted transfer without financial bounty)

Fixed ratios: Bengal Army (mutiny was worst) = 1 British : 2 Indian; Madras + Bombay Armies = 1:3; Indians ENTIRELY BARRED from artillery (control of artillery = control of decisive firepower = structural check on any future offensive)

Divide + Rule regiments: deliberate mix of castes, religions + ethnicities within each regiment; no single group can dominate; inter-regional interaction actively discouraged (pan-India unity among regiments was British nightmare in 1857)

Martial Races theory: Jats, Rajputs, Sikhs, Gurkhas described as naturally loyal + good fighters but incapable of independent leadership (ideal soldiers, never officers); regions that stayed loyal in 1857 heavily favoured; minimum or no Indians in senior military positions; army actively deployed against INM activities + peasant revolts

Police Act 1861 (passed March 1861) — 1st Police Commission 1860 under Canning56-62 (M.H. Court heads it); Police Raj created from 1857: Indians excluded from all senior positions; proper provincial police structure: IG -> SP (district level, reports to DC/DM) -> SI (thana level, reports to SP)

Civil Services: CS exam (Charter Act 1853) NOT held simultaneously in India; maximum age deliberately set at 19-23 (low enough to effectively bar most Indian candidates who finish education later than British counterparts)

Statutory Civil Service (1870, implemented by Lytton76-80 in 1878): Indians nominated to certain posts previously reserved for CCS officers — only loyal, hand-picked elites chosen (co-option, not inclusion)

Royal Titles Act 1876 — empowers Queen Victoria to take title Kaiser-i-Hind (Empress of India); Delhi Durbar 1877 under Lytton76-80 where Victoria formally coronated; she had used title informally since 1858

WEMC frustration = seed of modern nationalism: WEMC educated in British institutions + believed in British liberalism; wanted share in governance; now shut out post-1857 by racism + authoritarianism; this frustration + alienation becomes foundation of the INM that develops in 2nd half of 19th century

remark relates to the REVOLT OF 1857 (NOT Champaran Satyagraha 1917 / NOT Khilafat + NCM 1919-22 / NOT August
Movement 1942). Significance: Hindu-Muslim unity in 1857 was what made the revolt so dangerous — and why divide-and-rule
became CENTRAL to post-1857 British policy.
n Prelims Alert (1998) — WEMC and 1857: The educated middle class (WEMC) OPPOSED the revolt of 1857 (NOT supported /
NOT neutral). Reason: believed in benevolence of British rule; directly benefited from new economy + jobs + status British rule
created. This is why the WEMC produced modern nationalism LATER (INC 1885 onward) rather than joining 1857.
Peel Commission Key Facts: Royal Commission on Reorganisation of Indian Army, July 1858. Head: Major-General Jonathan
Peel (also Secretary of State for War 1858-59; younger brother of Sir Robert Peel who created modern London police). Report:
March 1859. Key outcomes: (1) European Forces Act 1860 (merges EIC's European army into Crown Army; triggers 'White
Mutiny'); (2) Fixed ratios (Bengal 1:2; Madras+Bombay 1:3); (3) Indians entirely barred from artillery; (4) Divide+Rule regiments; (5)
Martial Races theory; (6) Minimum Indians in senior military positions.

sections.title: A Thread Running Through All These Revolts

events.label: EIC begins promoting Indigo cultivation in Bengal — gives loans to 10 European planters (could have given to local zamindars but chose Europeans; preferential treatment from day one)

PS1793 — zamindars become large landowners; land becomes commodity (sold, rented, leased, mortgaged); planters shift from Nij System (buy land + cultivate directly = expensive + complicated) to Ryoti System: planter leases land from zamindar -> signs contracts with tenant ryots; 3 conditions: (i) ryot must grow Indigo on at least 25% of land he occupies; (ii) planter gives low-interest loans + sells Indigo seeds + seed drills to ryot; (iii) planter then PURCHASES cultivated Indigo from ryot at price far below market rate; trap: debt keeps ryot permanently tied to Indigo even without force

Charter Act 1853 — creates post of Lieutenant Governor of Bengal in 1854 to reduce GG's workload; sympathetic LG later directs DCs to take side of ryots (forced cultivation against spirit of capitalism + free market)

Indigo destroys soil fertility -> productivity for food crops falls; low price paid for Indigo + low soil fertility = ryot perpetually in debt; to repay one loan ryot must take another; planter = de-facto zamindar during lease period; global indigo prices fall (financial crisis on Stock Exchange -> general British economic slowdown -> demand falls); planters offer even less for cultivated Indigo; squeeze becomes unbearable
Rent Act of 1859 — occupancy right for ryots who cultivated same plot continuously >12 years; ryots USE this Act to fight planters' eviction attempts in court

Indigo Revolt — ryots' multi-pronged campaign: (i) REFUSE to accept new loans + refuse to cultivate Indigo; (ii) social BOYCOTT of Indian agents of planters (= Non-Cooperation before Gandhi); (iii) NO-RENT campaign when planters go to court to enforce contracts; (iv) fight planters' eviction attempts in court using occupancy rights under Rent Act 1859 Neel Darpan (Blue Mirror) — play by DeenBandhu Mitra depicting ryot oppression by Indigo planters; enormous public awareness; Michael Madhusudhan Datta (Bengali poet) translates into English; Christian missionary James Long publishes it; planters file libel case against Long; Long convicted, fined Rs 1,000 (paid by Kaliprasanna Sinha), sentenced to 1 month imprisonment; Hindu Patriot (English) + Somprakash (Bengali) publish strong editorials for ryots; British Indian Association (1851, educated zamindars) supports ryots (partly self-interest: resent dominance of European planters)
Indigo Commission (1860) — rules: ryots must honour existing contracts but FREE to refuse future ones

By 1863: Indigo cultivation largely shifts from Bengal to Bihar — operates there as Tinkathia System (ryot forced to grow Indigo on 3/20th = three-twentieths of land occupied; essentially same as Ryoti System)

BASF (German company) develops synthetic Indigo (1897) — cheaper + more consistent than natural product; synthetic Indigo floods global markets; demand for natural Indigo collapses; destroys whatever economic logic remained in plantation system; Prelims 2020: indigo cultivation declined because of new inventions / unprofitability in world market (NOT peasant resistance / NOT national leaders' opposition / NOT govt control over planters)
Gandhi launches Champaran Satyagraha (1917) — Bihar chapter of Indigo story; leads to Champaran Agrarian Act 1918 which ends Tinkathia System

Rent Act 1859 — grants occupancy rights to ryots who cultivated same plot continuously >12 years (cannot be arbitrarily evicted); zamindars routinely VIOLATE these rights; rents raised illegally; illegal abwabs (extra cesses) collected

Pabna Agrarian Leagues (1873) — ryots of Pabna district, Bengal organise into Agrarian Leagues (formal structure of collective action); pool money to fight cases in court; leader Ishan Chandra Roy replicates movement in neighbouring districts; two new features of post-1857 revolts on clear display: organisation + legal awareness

WEMC divided on Pabna: (i) Hindu Patriot (English) + Amrita Bazar Patrika (Bengali + English) SUPPORT zamindars; (ii) Bengalee (English) edited by Surendranath Banerjea (SNB) SUPPORTS ryots; (iii) Anglo-Indian press sides with ryots (here = Indian landlord under attack, not peasant defying European)
Ripon80-84 sets up Rent Commission 1880 — to address Pabna + broader zamindari-ryot conflict

Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 (Act III of 1885) — properly implemented; occupancy rights to ryots who cultivated different plots in same village continuously >12 years; finally brings genuine relief to Bengal's ryots

phases.label: MAHARASHTRA — NO-TAX CAMPAIGNS + BOMBAY DECCAN RIOTS (1873–1897)

events.label: Limitation Law of 1859 (Bombay) — interest on a loan applicable only for 3 years regardless of when ryot repays; moneylenders' workaround: make ryot sign FRESH debt bond after 3 years with accumulated interest added to principal; debt can never truly be paid down

Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) — associated with M.G. Ranade; collects 17,000 signatures on powers-of-attorney to represent ryots; successfully convinces govt: confiscation of land = last resort in recovering LR arrears; moneylenders retaliate by REFUSING further loans -> ryots unable to pay LR -> violence breaks out

No-Tax Campaign, Maharashtra (1873-74) — ryots launch organised no-tax campaign against hike in LR; direct, organised resistance to colonial fiscal policy Bombay Deccan Riots 1875 — grievances: high LR under Ryotwari system + oppression by moneylenders + loss of land; ryots do NOT attack moneylenders' lives; they BURN DEBT BONDS (awareness of the instrument of oppression, not just its wielder)
Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act 1879 — protects against loss of land due to indebtedness; regulates interest rates
No-Tax Campaign 1896-97, Maharashtra — outbreak because govt refuses to grant any remission (one-time reduction) in LR despite widespread crop failure

phases.label: PUNJAB — KUKA REVOLT + CANAL COLONY AGITATIONS (1871–1907)

events.label: Kuka Revolt — leader: Baba Ram Singh, head of Namdhari Sect; Namdharis = reformist Sikh sect: believe in living Guru + Guru Granth Sahib; strict equality of status for women; reject rituals (rely only on chanting of mantras -> name 'Kuka' = reciter); anti-priestly + strongly pro-cow protection; revolt begins as violence against cow slaughterers + priests -> turns against British; Baba Ram Singh exiled to Burma 1872 Singh Sabha founded 1873 — among 3 organisations that mobilise peasantry in Punjab Canal Colony agitations 1907
Arya Samaj founded 1875 — among 3 organisations that mobilise peasantry in Punjab Canal Colony agitations 1907
Lahore Indian Association founded 1877 — among 3 organisations that mobilise peasantry in Punjab Canal Colony agitations 1907

Punjab Canal Colony Agitations 1907 — British introduce bill: (i) govt can control inheritance of land in canal colonies; (ii) increase water rates; (iii) increase fines for violations of canal colony regulations; 3 organisations mobilise peasantry: Lahore Indian Association 1877 + Arya Samaj 1875 + Singh Sabha 1873; no-tax campaign begins -> escalates into riots; British response: REPRESSION + quiet WITHDRAWAL of bill; withdrawal calculation: post-1857 Indian Army heavily recruited from Punjab particularly Sikh community; disaffection among Punjab's peasantry could spread to army = risk British cannot afford

anchors: Key Pattern — Two New Features of Post-1857 Revolts: (1) Legal awareness: ryots file court cases using Rent Act 1859
occupancy rights; fight planters + zamindars in courts instead of only with weapons. (2) WEMC involvement: lawyers, journalists,
reformers (SNB's Bengalee, Neel Darpan, Hindu Patriot, Amrita Bazar Patrika) speak for ryots in courts, newspapers + public
associations. These revolts = REHEARSAL for the INM: non-cooperation, no-tax, boycott, legal challenge — all methods peasants
discovered through trial + error in these decades; Gandhi later perfects them.
Indigo System — Nij vs Ryoti: Nij System: planter buys land directly + cultivates indigo himself (expensive + complicated ->
abandoned). Ryoti System: planter leases land from zamindar -> contracts with tenant ryots; 3 conditions: (i) 25% of ryot's land for
indigo; (ii) low-interest loan + seeds/drills from planter; (iii) planter buys cultivated indigo below market rate. Bihar variant =
Tinkathia System: 3/20th (three-twentieths) of land for indigo (= same trap, smaller fraction). Indigo destroys soil fertility -> food
crop productivity falls -> ryot perpetually in debt -> trap closes.
n Prelims Alert (2020) — Decline of Indigo cultivation: Indigo cultivation declined by beginning of 20th century BECAUSE OF:
new inventions / unprofitability in world market (BASF Germany develops synthetic indigo 1897; cheaper + more consistent; floods
global markets; natural indigo demand collapses). NOT peasant resistance / NOT national leaders' opposition / NOT govt control
over planters.
Anglo-Indian vs Eurasian — Terminology Trap: BEFORE 1911 Census: 'Anglo-Indian' = European living in India; 'Eurasian' =
person of mixed British-Indian descent. AFTER 1911 Census: FLIPPED — 'Anglo-Indian' = person of mixed descent; 'Eurasian' fell
out of use entirely. When chapter says 'Anglo-Indian press sides with ryots' (Pabna 1873) = European-owned press; NOT
mixed-descent community.

chapters.title: Pre-INC Organisations and the Early Indian National Movement

sections.title: How the Indian National Movement Began

phases.label: FIRST ASSOCIATIONS + RACIALLY PROVOCATIVE COLONIAL ACTS (1838–1870)

events.label: Charter Act 1833 — promises racial equality ('no person to be deprived of chance to enter EIC service on grounds of religion, race, birth or colour'); 'Black Acts' of 1850 attempt to act on this promise -> Europeans protest vigorously ('white rebellion')
Landholders' Society, Calcutta — Dwarkanath Tagore; included many non-official Anglo-Indians (= Europeans settled in India, pre-1911 usage); precursor to BrIA1851

Black Acts (Bethune's Bills) 1850 — attempt to end European racial privilege in courts: before 1850, European charged with crime in mofussil (rural areas outside Presidency Towns) could ONLY be tried by Supreme Court in a Presidency Town (Calcutta/Bombay/Madras) — bypassing local Company courts where Indian judges presided; made justice for ordinary Indians nearly impossible (witnesses + complainants had to travel to Presidency Town at great cost); Black Acts would bring Europeans in mofussil under criminal jurisdiction of ordinary district courts where Indians served as judges; Europeans protest so vigorously in press = called 'white rebellion'; Acts suspended; same principle resurrected 1883 as Ilbert Bill

Lex Loci Act 1850 (Removal of Religious/Caste Disabilities Act) — grants right of inheritance to converts from any religion to any other; passed despite Indian opposition; widely seen as tool to promote conversion to Christianity

British Indian Association (BrIA1851) — set up @ Calcutta; 1st major voluntary organisation in India; Radhakanta Deb = 1st President; membership: educated men of LANDED class; 1st all-Indian organisation in character
events.full: British Indian Association (BrIA1851) — set up @ Calcutta; 1st major voluntary organisation in India; Radhakanta Deb = 1st President; membership: educated men of LANDED class; 1st all-Indian organisation in character (Prelims 2017: Radhakanta Deb = 1st President of BrIA1851 = CORRECT; SNB = founder of Indian Association 1876 = CORRECT; Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty = founder of Madras Mahajan Sabha = WRONG — correct founders: M. Veeraraghavachariar + G. Subramania Iyer + P. Anandacharlu)

events.label: Bombay Association (1852) + Madras Native Association (1852) — formed same year as BrIA1851; all three = educated, landed, conservative; immediate reason: British Parliament deliberating Charter Act of 1853 -> Indian elites want to present demands; sent SEPARATE petitions (not joint = not thinking as single national fraternity; three regional lobbies); common grievances: high taxes, expensive + incompetent administration, neglect of education + public works; elite personal interests: opposition to salt + opium monopolies; framing: 'un-British' rule (not colonialism itself = wrong)
Charter Act 1853 — mandates Civil Services Exam (1st held 1855 in London only; simultaneous exam in India only under GOI Act 1919; 1st India-based exam 1922)
ICS exam established — 1st held 1855 in London; Satyendranath Tagore (Rabindranath's brother) = 1st Indian to clear ICS exam (1864)
Income Tax 1st introduced 1860 — withdrawn under press pressure; re-introduced 1868; WEMC slogan: 'No Taxation Without Representation'; famines sweep different parts of India through 1860s-70s
Madras Native Association closes 1861 — political activity in Madras goes into lull until Madras Mahajan Sabha 1884
Indian Councils Act 1861 — sets up Legislative Councils; WEMC later demands Indian representation there
Satyendranath Tagore clears ICS exam (1864) — 1st Indian to do so
Income Tax re-introduced 1868 despite famines across India; Great Madras Famine 1876-78: ~1 crore Indians die from 2 consecutive years of drought

Education cuts in Bengal 1870 — Anglo-Indian press calls WEMC 'seditious'; colonial response: cut higher education spending in Bengal (not engage with criticism); military expenditure + high taxes continue as before

Surendranath Banerjee (SNB) — passes ICS exam but NOT selected due to age dispute (differences between English calendar + Hindu calendar; personal injustice -> political fuel; eventually dismissed from ICS; Prelims 1999: Indian leader dismissed from ICS = Surendranath Banerjee, NOT Satyendranath Tagore / R.C. Dutt / S.C. Bose)

phases.label: RISE OF WEMC ORGANISATIONS + LYTTON YEARS (1870–1880)

events.label: Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) — M.G. Ranade sets up; members: K.T. Telang, P.M. Mehta, later G.K. Gokhale + Bal Gangadhar Tilak; aim: represent interests of ALL sections of society (significant departure from landlord focus of earlier bodies); 1875: sends petition to British House of Commons demanding direct Indian representation (one of earliest such demands addressed to Imperial Parliament itself; Prelims 2002: which submitted petition to HoC demanding direct Indian representation 1875 = Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, NOT Deccan Association / NOT Indian Association / NOT Madras Mahajan Sabha)

By 1875: India has over 400 newspapers in English + vernacular languages; combined readership >1.5 lakh; press = primary tool of WEMC; builds inter-regional awareness; spreads nationalist ideas; helps regional leaders grow into national ones

Arya Samaj 1875 (Dayananda) + Swami Vivekananda + Bankim Chandra Chatterjee — cultural nationalism of this period; extremist leaders Lal-Bal-Pal later use this cultural nationalism to strengthen political nationalism

SNB founds Indian Association (1876) Bengal — explicit goal: 'representing the people'; SNB had passed ICS exam but age dispute arose (English vs Hindu calendar difference) -> not selected; eventually dismissed from ICS; Indian Association = major WEMC-led political organisation in Bengal
Bombay Association of 1852 briefly revived 1876 when Dadabhai Naoroji + Naoroji Ferdunji return from London; younger generation not satisfied with its conservative outlook
ICS age limit CUT from 21 to 19 by Lytton76-80 — exam only in London; change makes it near-impossible for Indians to compete; demand for exam centre in India rejected outright

Delhi Durbar 1877 by Lytton76-80 — enormous + expensive imperial spectacle; Queen Victoria crowned Kaesar-i-Hind (Empress of Hindustan); held while Great Madras Famine 1876-78 killing people across south India; WEMC press scathing; 3-year press campaign 1877-80 by WEMC demanding Indianisation of Civil Services — Durbar only adds fuel
Lahore Indian Association (1877) — set up in Punjab by Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia (when SNB toured Punjab); prominent leaders (not founders): Lala Lajpat Rai + Ajit Singh

Press campaign demanding Indianisation of Civil Services (1877-80) Vernacular Press Act (VPA) / Gagging Act 1878 by Lytton76-80 — targets vernacular press (grown sharply critical of British policy); printers + publishers must deposit security bond (forfeited if publish anything 'objectionable' = anti-British); British Liberal MP Gladstone publicly criticises Act from London; Amrita Bazar Patrika converts overnight from Bengali to English to escape VPA's reach
Arms Act 1878 by Lytton76-80 — Indians require licence to own arms; Europeans + Eurasians EXEMPT (openly discriminatory); B.C. Pal launches press campaigns against it

Statutory Civil Services Act 1878 by Lytton76-80 (implemented as policy from 1878) — new service category but entry by NOMINATION not examination; only loyalists nominated (= colonial 'lateral entry'; looks inclusive, ensures loyalists get in)

2nd Anglo-Afghan War 1878-80 by Lytton76-80 — driven by fear of Russian influence in Afghanistan; expensive campaign when Indian treasury already stretched by famine relief; treaty shapes modern borders of Afghanistan; 1st Anglo-Afghan War 1838-42 was for same reason + was expensive disaster
Gladstone's Liberal Party wins 1880 British elections; sends reformist Viceroy Ripon80-84 to India; stark contrast with Lytton
Ripon sets up Rent Commission 1880 — eventually leads to Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 (pressure from Pabna Agrarian Leagues 1873)

Factories Act 1881 — child labour banned for children under 7; working hours capped for children under 12; 4 monthly holidays mandated; moderate Indian leaders OPPOSE this Act (hurts Indian capitalists already struggling against British manufactured goods competition)
VPA repealed by Ripon80-84 (1882)
Arms Act amended by Ripon80-84 (1882) — now everyone including Europeans needs licence (Ripon amended NOT repealed; reformer but still colonial ruler)
ICS age limit raised back to 21 by Ripon80-84 (1882); Ripon also pushes for simultaneous exam in India -> strongly opposed by Europeans in India -> proposal fails

Local Self-Government Resolution/Act 1882 by Ripon80-84 — stated goal: train Indians in self-governance; KEY CHANGES: (i) rural: elected District Boards set up across British India; members elected by LR payers + rent payers (not nominated by officials); (ii) urban: municipalities strengthened: minimum 2/3 members must be elected; chairperson must be non-official member; (iii) local bodies given charge of health, education, sanitation, roads + communications with day-to-day autonomy; govt retains power to inspect + dissolve; colonial seedling -> 73rd + 74th Constitutional Amendments 1992 make it constitutional tree (Part IX = Panchayati Raj; Part IX-A = Municipalities)

Hunter Education Commission (1882-83) — follows Ripon's Local Self-Govt Act; recommends: transfer education to local bodies; focus on mass vernacular education; strengthen female education; implementation remains poor Ilbert Bill 1883 — drafted by Law Member C.P. Ilbert; proposed: extend jurisdiction of Indian district judges to try cases involving Britons in mofussil (rural areas); would end privilege by which Briton in rural India could NOT be tried before Indian judge; European community in India reacts with immediate + furious organised opposition: lobby + protest -> bill WITHDRAWN + amended; final version requires mixed jury in any case involving a Briton; SAME PRINCIPLE as Black Acts 1850 (both attempts to end racial privilege in courts)

Ilbert Bill Controversy 1883-84 — for WEMC: settles any remaining doubt; British will NOT treat Indians as equals in courts / civil services / political life; triggers massive press campaigns across country; major milestone in growth of Indian political consciousness; Prelims 2013: Ilbert Bill = removal of disqualifications imposed on Indian magistrates with regard to trial of Europeans (NOT restrictions on arms / NOT press restrictions / NOT cotton duty); Prelims 2003: what Ilbert Bill sought = bring Indians + Europeans on par as far as criminal jurisdiction of courts was concerned Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884) — M. Veeraraghavachariar + G. Subramania Iyer (nationalist journalist + founder of The Hindu newspaper) + P. Anandacharlu; revives Madras political activity after Madras Native Association closed 1862; Prelims 2017: Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty NOT correctly matched as founder of Madras Mahajan Sabha = WRONG pair
INC founded 1885 (substantive home -> CH 24) — emerges from soil of: Western education + free press + racial provocation + organised WEMC associations + railways + telegraphs
Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 — from Ripon's Rent Commission 1880; properly implemented; brings genuine relief to Bengal's ryots

Indian Councils Act 1892 (ICA1892) — allows more Indians as members of Legislative Councils; WEMC associations begin using Legislative Councils as platforms for criticising British policies from within the system

Key English Figures Behind the INC

events.label: British India Association (BrIA1851) attempts to open branches in Bombay + Madras specifically to submit joint petition to London during Charter renewal of 1853 — earliest attempt at all-India coordination
A.O. Hume serves as Secretary of Dept of Revenue, Agriculture + Commerce under Viceroy Mayo69-72 — works to improve agricultural yields; reformist orientation established

Campaigns against Afghan War (1878-80) + Vernacular Press Act (1878) Hume supports Ripon80-84's reforms especially Local Self-Govt Resolution 1882

Hume publishes direct appeal to British voters to elect pro-Indian candidates to Parliament (1885)

Indian National Conference (1883/1885) merges into INC in 1886 — natural rather than forced (both running on nearly identical tracks by 1885); Indian Association itself continues to exist as separate body
Indian National Conference 1885 merges into INC (1886)
Badruddin Tyabji — 1st Muslim INC President @ Madras Session 1887; Prelims 1998: Tyabji NOT connected to Muslim League (Muslim League founded Dec 1906 @ Dacca; Tyabji died Aug 1906 before ML founded)

George Yule — 1st non-Indian / British INC President @ Allahabad Session 1888; merchant + businessman; founder of Agency House 'Andrew Yule & Company' @ Calcutta; President of Indian Chamber of Commerce; Prelims 2000: 1st British INC President = George Yule, NOT Hume (Hume was never INC President; Hume = General Secretary)

William Wedderburn — 2nd non-Indian INC President (1889 + again 1910); retired civil servant; ex-Secretary to Bombay Govt; co-founder of INC 1885; denied judgeship at Bombay HC for pro-Indian positions; later as MP in Britain actively supported INC demands in partnership with Gokhale; favoured Cooperative Banks for cheap loans to farmers

William Wedderburn + W.S. Caine set up Indian Parliamentary Committee in British Parliament (1893) — Prelims 2011: purpose = to agitate for Indian political reforms in House of Commons (NOT entry of Indians into Imperial Judiciary / NOT facilitate discussion on Independence / NOT entry of Indians into British Parliament)

Alfred Webb — 3rd non-Indian INC President @ Madras Session 1894; Irish politician + MP in 1890s; personally invited by Dadabhai Naoroji; strongly opposed to racism (supported Britain's 1st anti-racist journal); opposed opium trade into China; Irish background shaped sympathy for people living under imperial rule

Indian Councils Act 1892 (ICA1892) — allows more Indians as members of Legislative Councils; WEMC associations begin using Legislative Councils as platforms for criticising British policy from within the system
Wedderburn serves as INC President 2nd time (1910)

Wedderburn writes biography of Hume (published 1913) — describes Safety Valve Theory: in 1878 Hume came across 7 volumes of secret reports by religious gurus describing conspiracy by lower classes to overthrow British rule; Hume then met Dufferin84-88 + together formed INC as 'safety valve'; WHY THEORY IS WRONG: (i) 7 volumes never found in any archive; no reference except Wedderburn's biography = single unverifiable source by close personal friend; (ii) Dufferin did NOT take Hume seriously; called Moderates 'microscopic minority of Babus working for self-interest'; (iii) Dufferin did NOT welcome INC; quietly asked Governor of Bombay to be alert about it; feared INC would grow like Irish Home Rule League (Charles Parnell 1870s-80s = powerful political force that consistently embarrassed British govt)

Agency Houses — What Were They? British trading + financial firms in colonial India = cross between NBFC + private equity firm

enterprises (tea plantations, jute mills, coal mines, shipping). Today's equivalent: NBFC + private equity firm + holding company.

sections.title: Evolution of the Viceroy's Executive Council (VEC)
True Federalism — Just a Small Beginning

events.label: Charter Act 1793 — VEC composition: GG + 3 Ordinary Members + CIC (extraordinary member appointed by CoD); CIC = extraordinary (not ordinary) member; Law Member added as extraordinary for legislative meetings; VEC structure established

Charter Act 1833 — GG(Bengal) -> GG(India); Law Member added for legislative meetings only; Executive Meetings: GG + 3 Ordinary Members + CIC (extraordinary); Legislative Meetings: VEC + 1 Law Member (Macaulay); 1st grain of separation between executive + legislative

Charter Act 1853 — Law Member of 1833 elevated to full ordinary executive member; 6 more Legal Members added for legislative sessions; Executive Meetings: GG + 3 Ordinary Members + CIC (extraordinary) + 1 Law Member (now ordinary); Legislative Meetings: VEC + 6 Legal Members = 12 persons total
GOI Act 1858 — EIC abolished; GG becomes Viceroy + GG; reports to SoS for India in London; CIC now appointed by SoS (not CoD); same powers

Portfolio System introduced by Canning56-62 in 1859 — specific departments (ministries) allocated to individual VEC members; their decisions on portfolios final subject to Viceroy's veto; cabinet-style administration at centre; James Wilson introduced as Finance Member 1859 (income tax introduced 1860; Wilson dies 1860); ICA 1861 gives this system legal recognition
James Wilson dies (1860); Income Tax introduced 1860 (Wilson's last act); Income Tax withdrawn under WEMC pressure; re-introduced 1868

ICA 1861 — complete restructuring of British Indian State; simultaneously: Indian High Courts Act 1861 restructures Judiciary; two laws, one year, complete State machinery overhauled; Charles Wood (SoS for India): 'Government of India must be a despotism controlled from home' = fundamental principle of British Indian governance until 1947

ICA 1861: VEC formally constituted as: GG + 5 Ordinary Members + CIC (extraordinary member appointed by SoS); Portfolio System given legal recognition; 5 Ordinary Members = Home + Revenue + Finance + Law + Military (Administrative Military Member runs office; CIC runs battlefield — two separate roles; Crown does not want one man wearing both hats); Finance Member (5th Ordinary Member) added constitutionally 1861 (practice started 1859 with Wilson)

ICA 1861: ILC = VEC + 6 to 12 Additional Members (half must be non-officials); ILC = same council with two hats: (i) day-to-day executive work = VEC; (ii) law-making = ILC (= VEC + Additional Members); every VEC member automatically part of ILC; design guarantees official majority in every legislative vote; expanded-council model continues until GOI 1919 replaces it with fully bicameral Central Legislature (Council of State + Central Legislative Assembly)

Indian High Courts Act 1861 — establishes High Courts in Madras, Bombay + Calcutta; HCs begin functioning from 1862; Calcutta HC = merger of Sadar Diwani Adalat + Sadar Nizamat Adalat + Supreme Court @ Calcutta; ends dual-track system

1st Indians nominated to ILC (1862): Raja of Banaras + Maharaja of Patiala + Dinkar Rao of Gwalior (knighted 1877 as Sir Dinkar Rao); all elites; some from Princely States; British logic: elite Indians stayed loyal during 1857 -> reward + secure their cooperation; by ICA 1892: only 45 Indians nominated in total (mainly Zamindars + moneylenders from BrIA1851 + British businessmen + some Princely State rulers = deliberate selection of loyalists)

Bengal PLC established (1862) — Bengal's provincial council had evolved into GG(India)'s Council by 1833, became Viceroy's Council in 1858, then rebranded as ILC + VEC in 1861 -> Bengal needed fresh PLC of its own
Income Tax re-introduced 1868

6th Ordinary Member added to VEC in 1874 — massive investment in railways, canals + infrastructure requires dedicated portfolio; portfolio = Public Works; updated VEC: 6 Ordinary Members = Home + Revenue + Finance + Law + Military + Public Works

NWP PLC established (1886) — NWP = half of Awadh annexed as permanent payment of subsidiary alliance subsidy in 1801; Mahalwari 1st applied here in 1822; given province status 1836 but without legislature + under LG; delay: memories of 1857 still raw; British cautious about loosening executive grip in epicentre of 1857 revolt
ICA 1892 — requirement for Viceroy's sanction on provincial nominations ended; more genuine power shifts to Governors; by ICA 1892: only 45 Indians nominated to ILC in total since 1862
Punjab PLC established (1897) — Punjab annexed 1849; delay: frontier province; British preferred strong executive control rather than slower deliberation of a legislative body
ICA 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) — outer ring of additional members gradually grows + gains marginal new powers; expanded-council model still continues

GOI Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) — abolishes expanded-council model; replaces with fully bicameral Central Legislature: Council of State (CoS) + Central Legislative Assembly (CLA); structurally DISTINCT from VEC; also: provincial budget separated from central budget for 1st time; legislative powers restored to provinces

1st Muslim INC President (Tyabji); 1892-1905: Hindus = 90% of members; Muslims = only 6.5%; Brahmins alone = ~40% of Hindu membership; INC composition: ~20% landlords + 40% lawyers + 15% traders (mostly from landed families)

anchors: Moderates' Ideological Framework — 4 layers: (1) Utilitarianism + Liberalism = twin foundations (greatest good for greatest
number + individual rights + rule of law). (2) Constitutionalism = Responsible Government + Rule of Law (today: reflected in
Preamble + Basic Structure doctrine + DPSPs). (3) Constitutional Methods = use only institutions + mechanisms the State itself
provides (today: elections + legislature + judiciary + RTI + CPGRAMS + Citizen Charters + petitions). (4) Providence of British Rule
= British, if sufficiently pressurised, can be made to modernise India; goal = Limited Self-Government within British rule; ultimate
vision = Dominion Status like Canada/Australia (NOT independence).
Lancashire Lobby Logic — Why Moderates Opposed Factory Acts: British textile manufacturers in Lancashire lobby for Indian
factory regulations -> raise Indian production costs -> reduce competitiveness of Indian textiles in global markets. Moderates
understand this game: oppose regulations not out of indifference to workers but to protect infant Indian industries from premature
regulatory burden. Their argument: India needs room to industrialise; heavy regulations now = India stays permanently as raw
material supplier for British manufacturing. BUT consequence: Indian workers (including children) continue to labour under harsh
conditions for longer than necessary. Moderates support Assam Tea Garden workers (European owners) but oppose same labour
reforms for Indian-owned factories = class inconsistency within principled argument.
Defence of Moderates (Gokhale 1913): British would never have allowed all-India organisation under Indian leadership -> Hume
= protective cover. Culture of direct confrontation with colonial government had not yet developed. INC 1885 = beginning of
something, not the end. A movement that begins with petition + prayer is not necessarily weak — it is building the institutions +
culture of politics for a country that had NEVER had a national political organisation before. Moderates created: vocabulary of
Indian politics; culture of annual national conference; demand structure (civil services + legislative reform + economic exploitation);
press culture; national leadership class. Extremists and Gandhi later built on this foundation, not from scratch.

events.label: INC 1st session @ Bombay — declared goal: 'building national unity'; India in 1885 = land of regions, languages, castes + religions; no pre-existing single Indian political community; Moderates understand: building such a community is 1st task, even before demanding rights from British; deliberate choice: focus ONLY on issues common to all Indians (Indians vs British; NOT Hindu vs Muslim / UC vs LC / men vs women / workers vs capitalists / ryots vs landlords)
Dadabhai Naoroji lays down informal INC rule (1886): Congress will take up ONLY political questions, NOT social or class questions — social issues could divide Indians against each other

INC decision 1888: NO resolution would be passed if majority of Hindu OR Muslim members disagree with it — structural protection of minority community within INC; Prelims context: 1889 Minority Clause = INC (NOT Muslim League) that FIRST formally demanded minority representation in legislative councils

INC Minority Clause 1889: INC demands British govt reserve seats in ILC + PLCs for religious minorities in proportion to their share of population; NOTE: it was the INC itself, not the Muslim League (1906), that first formally demanded minority representation

INC sessions held in different parts of country each year; President specifically NOT from host region (e.g. Marathi leader presiding in Calcutta builds inter-regional bonds; Bengali delegate listening to Marathi president on Bombay peasant problems starts seeing that leader as national leader); nation-building through simple structural design

INC sessions modelled on parliamentary practice — President functions like Speaker; members speak + debate + vote on resolutions; for India = new; roots of modern Indian parliamentary culture; Lok Sabha procedures today trace back to INC session culture from 1885
ICA 1892 — bitter disappointment; fails to deliver meaningful reform; this failure gives Drain Theory particular prominence as intellectual weapon

events.label: Absence of Protective Tariffs (1813-WW1 1914-19) — no import duty on British goods entering India; British goods flood Indian markets; Indian manufacturers cannot compete; only after WW1 (1914-19) were protective tariffs applied for 1st time
Exchange Rate Manipulation — rupee-to-pound exchange rate managed to benefit British businesses; kept British exports competitive in India

Council Bills (CBs) mechanism post-1833 — SoS for India holds India's foreign exchange (forex) in London; foreign importer buys Council Bills from India Council in London (pays forex to London); uses CBs in India to purchase Indian goods; GOI accepts CBs + gives Indian rupees to importer; result: India never gets forex for its exports (forex stays in London); Indian taxpayer money finances this trade (forex for Indian exports stays in London)

Railways — introduced by Dalhousie48-56 in 1853: original purpose = faster movement of British army; railways connect Indian markets + raw material sources to PORTS (not to Indian manufacturers); technology transfer very limited; British capitalists receive GUARANTEED 5% annual interest on invested capital paid in pound sterling in London from Day 1 of FDI (= effectively FD with simple interest); if railway fails to earn 5% profit in any year, GOI makes up deficit; right to sell back to GOI at exact total FDI amount at any point before 99 years; wasteful construction (profits private; losses public); same money could have invested in irrigation for food security; byproduct: railways covered 78% of India by 1947; feeder roads allowed Indian businesses to eventually use network; increased people-to-people contact -> strengthened national unity + INM inter-regional bonds

Suez Canal built 1859-69 — cuts sea distance between India + Britain by 4,500 miles; combined with steam-powered railways, steam-fitted ships, paved roads + modern ports = cheaper + faster to extract raw materials from India + ship finished goods back = drain worse, not better Strachey Famine Commission 1880 — appointed to review recurring famines; recommendations rarely implemented seriously

used phrase 'Un-British' (Prelims 2008). (2) R.C. Dutt: Economic History of India (Vol 1: 1901, Vol 2: 1903); data-driven historical
depth + empirical backbone; former ICS officer. (3) M.G. Ranade: Father of Indian Economics. Prelims 2015: ALL THREE (Naoroji
+ G. Subramania Iyer + R.C. Dutt) = economic critics of colonialism. Drain Theory's structural claim: without Swaraj (self-rule), the
drain could never be stopped -> economic critique inseparable from political demand.
Council Bills Mechanism — How India Lost Its Export Forex: Foreign importer wants to buy Indian goods -> goes to India
Council in London -> buys Council Bills (CBs) with his forex -> forex STAYS IN LONDON -> importer goes to India with CBs -> GOI
accepts CBs + gives Indian RUPEES -> importer buys Indian goods. India received: its own rupees (its own currency). India did
NOT receive: forex for its exports (forex stayed in London). Where did India's rupees come from? Indian taxpayers. Net result:
India's export earnings (forex) never returned to India; Indian taxpayer money financed trade that benefitted British importers +
British India Council in London.
n Prelims Cluster — Drain Theory (1996 + 2008 + 2011 + 2013 + 2015 + 2018 + 2020): 1996: did NOT believe in Drain Theory =
Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (NOT Tilak / R.C. Dutt / Ranade). 2008: used 'Un-British' = Dadabhai Naoroji (NOT Anandmohan Bose /
Tyabji / Pherozeshah Mehta). 2008: rejected Knighthood + refused Council of SoS for India = G.K. Gokhale (NOT Motilal Nehru /
Ranade / Tilak). 2011: Home Charges = funds 1 (India office in London) + 2 (salaries/pensions of British personnel) + 3 (waging
wars outside India) = ALL THREE = answer 1, 2 and 3. 2013: Naoroji's most effective contribution = exposed economic exploitation
of India by British (Only 1). 2015: economic critics of colonialism = Naoroji + G. Subramania Iyer + R.C. Dutt = 1, 2 and 3. 2018:
economic result of British rule in 19th century = commercialisation of agriculture. 2020: Industrial Revolution's impact on India in 1st
half of 19th century = Indian handicrafts were ruined.
n Prelims Alert (1997) — AINLF: M.C. Setalvad + B.N. Rau + Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer = All India National Liberal Federation
(AINLF, 1918). NOT Swarajist Party (Motilal Nehru + C.R. Das, formed 1922). NOT Communist Party of India. NOT Indian Civil
Service. AINLF = Moderates who left INC after Surat Split 1907; founded 1918; leaders: SNB + Tej Bahadur Sapru. All three
named figures = eminent jurists who later served in constitutional/legal roles in independent India.
n Prelims Alert (1999) — No independent development of industries under British rule: Because of = ABSENCE OF HEAVY
INDUSTRIES. NOT scarcity of foreign capital (FDI did come in but for British-owned enterprises). NOT scarcity of natural
resources (India had abundant natural resources). NOT preference of the rich to invest in land (partial truth but not the primary
reason). Core: without heavy industries (steel mills, machine tool factories, heavy engineering) no self-sustaining industrialisation is
possible.

chapters.title: Indian Councils Act of 1892 (ICA 1892 or Lord Cross Act)

sections.title: The "Indirect Election" That Wasn't Called an Election
The Viceroy's Executive Council (VEC) — No Change
A Separate Administrative Reform of the Same Era

events.label: Canada gets Dominion Status (1867) — self-governance within British Empire without breaking from it; Moderates later use this as benchmark for their demand: if white-settler Canada can self-govern, why not a civilisation far older?
INC founded Dec 1885 @ Bombay — Moderate era begins; 1885-1905 = 20 years of prayers + petitions = zero demands met

Aitchison Commission (1886-88) — recommends civil service reforms; implemented as administrative orders by Lansdowne88-94 NOT as provisions of ICA 1892 (classic exam trap); changes: (i) Covenanted Civil Services (CCS) -> renamed Imperial Civil Services (ICS); (ii) Uncovenanted Civil Services (UCS) -> renamed Provincial Civil Services (PCS); (iii) Statutory Civil Services (created 1878) -> ABOLISHED; ICS-PCS split has federal logic: centre + province as two levels each with own service cadre George Yule — 1st non-Indian INC President @ Allahabad session 1888

ICA 1892 (Indian Councils Act 1892 / Lord Cross Act) — SoS: Lord Cross; Viceroy: Lansdowne88-94; simultaneously: result of Moderates' struggle + proof of its failure; gave just enough to show British had listened + little enough to show no intention of conceding power

ICA 1892 — INDIRECT NOMINATION (NOT election): most significant feature = indirectly nominated members in ILC + PLCs; word 'ELECTION' deliberately omitted from text of Act; legal mechanism = 'nomination on the basis of recommendation' = selection, NOT election

ICA 1892 — HOW RECOMMENDATION WORKS: (i) For PLCs: Governors nominate non-official members based on recommendations from District Boards, Municipalities, Universities, Trade Associations + Zamindars; (ii) For ILC: Viceroy nominates non-officials based on recommendations from non-official members of PLCs + Bengal Chamber of Commerce (NOT directly from local bodies); EXAM TRAP: 'Members of ILC under ICA 1892 were directly recommended by Municipalities' = FALSE; Municipalities -> PLCs -> ILC (two separate tiers); direct recommendation to ILC only from PLCs + Bengal Chamber of Commerce

ICA 1892 — SIZE OF COUNCILS: ILC = VEC + 10 to 16 additional members (up from 6-12 of ICA 1861); at least half can be non-officials; but official majority ALWAYS guaranteed (VEC + official additional members always comfortably outnumber non-official Indians = mathematically guaranteed by structure of Act)
ICA 1892 — VEC: NO CHANGE from ICA 1861 + 1874; still: GG + 6 Ordinary Members (Home, Revenue/Agriculture, Law, Military, Finance, Public Works) + CIC (extraordinary); all nominated by British Crown

ICA 1892 — NEW POWER: QUESTIONS: for 1st time non-official members can ASK QUESTIONS to executive; but strict conditions: (i) 6 days prior notice required; (ii) no discussion of answers given; (iii) no supplementary questions allowed; can ask, cannot follow up
ICA 1892 — NO POWER: RESOLUTIONS: opposition members (non-official, non-officer members) CANNOT bring any resolution before council; CANNOT demand vote on govt resolution

ICA 1892 — BUDGET: Budget CAN be discussed for 1st time — another genuine new right; but members can NEITHER vote on it NOR amend it; 'Taxation Without Representation' (TWR) = slogan of American Revolution 1776; Indians can watch Budget + speak to it; zero power to change it

ICA 1892 — LEGISLATION: official majority means Indian non-official members outvoted on every single bill; presence = advisory, not decisive; legislative function = recommendatory, not mandatory; Viceroy's absolute veto + official majority = why recommendatory, NOT new ordinance bypass; ordinance power unchanged from ICA 1861 (6-month emergency instrument)

ICA 1892 — FEDERALISM: ONE SMALL STEP: Governor NO LONGER needs Viceroy's approval to nominate Non-Officers to PLC; all other Viceroy powers over provinces unchanged: rule-making powers + prior approval for certain bills + single unified budget (no separate provincial budget until GOI 1919) + power to create new provinces + appoint LGs
Notable Indians in councils under ICA 1892 framework: Gokhale + Pherozeshah Mehta (names dominating Moderate politics for next two decades)

ICA 1892 — SCORECARD (what Moderates won): Indianisation of CS + Military = NO; non-official majority = NO; elected majority = NO; proper indirect election = NO (only nomination on recommendation); expansion of ILC + PLCs = YES (but dissatisfactory); powerful legislatures = NO; Constitutionalism = NO; word 'election' did not even make it into text of Act
Australia gets Dominion Status (1901) — both Australia + Canada = majority white-settler colonies; Moderates' demand: if those colonies can self-govern, why not India?

INC Calcutta session 1906 — Swaraj officially becomes goal of INC: Self-Government within the Empire (Dominion model = Home Rule); Moderates raise ceiling of demand after ICA 1892 disappointment; Drain Theory becomes twin pillar of Moderate politics alongside political demand for Swaraj

INC Surat Split 1907 — disillusionment seeded by ICA 1892 (hollow Act: expanded councils with no real power + budget discussion with no vote + questions with no follow-up) is the soil in which Extremism took root; Moderates vs Extremists
ICA 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) — next significant change; introduces separate Muslim electorates; non-binding resolutions allowed; ILC outer ring grows further

anchors: Indirect Nomination Chain — ICA 1892 (two tiers, not one): TIER 1 (feeding PLCs): District Boards + Municipalities +
Universities + Trade Associations + Zamindars -> recommend names to Governor -> Governor nominates non-official PLC
members. TIER 2 (feeding ILC): Non-official PLC members + Bengal Chamber of Commerce -> recommend names to Viceroy ->
Viceroy nominates non-official ILC members. EXAM TRAP: 'Municipalities directly recommended to ILC' = FALSE. Municipalities
-> PLCs; PLCs -> ILC. Direct recommendation to ILC = only PLCs + Bengal Chamber of Commerce. In a PROPER indirect
election: voters elect local body -> local body elects MLAs -> MLAs elect MPs; choice of voters is final. Under ICA 1892:
recommending bodies only sent shortlist; final pick was Viceroy's or Governor's. Not an election — a managed shortlist.
Aitchison Commission Reforms — NOT a provision of ICA 1892 (exam trap): Aitchison Commission (1886-88)
recommendations implemented by Lansdowne88-94 as ADMINISTRATIVE ORDERS (not as provisions of ICA 1892). Changes:
(1) CCS renamed ICS (Imperial Civil Service); (2) UCS renamed PCS (Provincial Civil Service); (3) Statutory Civil Services (1878)
abolished. ICS-PCS split has federal logic: centre + province as two levels each with own service cadre. If exam question asks
'which of the following were provisions of ICA 1892' and lists civil service changes = answer: NOT a provision of the Act.
ICA 1892 as Catalyst for Extremism: Moderates played by every British rule + used every permissible channel + mustered every
rational argument for 7+ years (1885-1892). What they got: hollow Act — expanded councils with no real power + budget
discussion with no vote + questions with no follow-up + word 'election' not even in text. This was the moment belief in British
benevolence began to crack. If 'prayers + petitions' could produce only this, then the method itself was bankrupt. Disillusionment
seeded by ICA 1892 = soil in which Extremism (Lal-Bal-Pal) took root in the decade that followed -> Surat Split 1907.

events.label: EIC obtains Diwani of Bengal Suba (Bengal + Orissa + Bihar); 1775: Benaras annexed + administered as part of Bengal Presidency

Half of Awadh formally ceded to British (Treaty of Lucknow 1801) + added to Bengal Presidency as 'Ceded Provinces'; Scindhia territory conquered in 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05) added -> renamed 'Ceded and Conquered Provinces' under Bengal Presidency
British get practical control of Orissa by defeating Bhonsle of Nagpur in 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (while Diwani of 'Orissa' held since 1765, it practically only covered Midnapore region until now)
Assam annexed in Treaty of Yandabo 1826 after 1st Anglo-Burma War (1824-26) + added to Bengal Presidency
'Ceded and Conquered Provinces' separated from Bengal Presidency -> North West Provinces (NWP1836) created
Assam carved out + made separate Chief Commissioner Province (= Union Territory equivalent; directly under central administration)
Bengal Presidency = Bengal + Orissa + Bihar; Assam = separate CC Province
Bande Mataram composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in novel AnandaMath (1882) -> anthem of INM during Swadeshi Movement
Tilak organises Ganapati Festival 1893 in Maharashtra — not just religious event but platform for political mobilisation; turning cultural identity into nationalist consciousness
Tilak organises Shivaji Festival 1896 in Maharashtra — same political mobilisation strategy

Calcutta Municipal Corporation Amendment Act 1899 (Curzon99-05) — reduces number of elected members in municipalities; rolls back whatever limited representative participation Indians had achieved in local governance; 1st of 3 chain-of-failure laws

ShantiNiketan Ashram 1901 (Rabindranath Tagore) — most notable example of Constructive Swadeshi + mobilisation at village level (pre-Partition); Moderates led by SNB + C.R. Das run press campaigns against Partition

Risley Papers 1903 (Risley = Home Secretary) — officially published in Gazette of India; Curzon99-05's Minute on Territorial Re-distribution laying out Partition plan in detail; Indians come to know of scheme in 1903 itself

Moderate Phase: Press + Constructive Swadeshi — newspapers: Bengalee (SNB), Sanjibani, Hitabadi campaign against Partition Desher Katha (1904) by Sakharam Ganesh Deuskar — documents economic exploitation of India under British rule; uses 'Desh' to refer to ENTIRE Indian subcontinent (not just Bengal) = conscious attempt to build pan-Indian economic consciousness against colonial drain; Prelims 2020: warned against hypnotic conquest of mind + inspired Swadeshi plays = 1 and 2 correct (NOT statement 3: 'Desh' context was all of India, NOT just Bengal); widely read in Bengal; contributes to intellectual climate for Swadeshi Movement

Indian Universities Act 1904 (Curzon99-05) — brings universities under direct govt control; Curzon calls Indian universities 'factories of sedition' = centres producing politically aware graduates who question British authority; clamps down; 2nd of 3 chain-of-failure laws

Indian Official Secrets Amendment Act 1904 (Curzon99-05) — significantly reduces press freedom; govt can censor + confiscate any publication that hurts interests of British Empire; broad definition of 'official secret' (any information relating to affairs of state or any matter specially notified by govt); remains in force until Indian Official Secrets Act 1923 (even more strict); 3rd of 3 chain-of-failure laws

Bengal Partition ANNOUNCED July 1905 — British justification: administrative (undivided Bengal = most populous province, too large; 3 benefits: (i) Assam grows + gets own CS cadre; (ii) Assam-Bengal Railways under unified EBA admin; (iii) Assam's tea gardens get cheaper maritime outlet via Chittagong port); REAL REASON: Divide + Rule = weaken INM in Bengal; creates two provinces along Hindu-Muslim demographic fault line; Bengal Bhadralok (UC Hindu educated professionals = backbone of organised political activity) become minority in both new provinces simultaneously

Bengal Partition EFFECTED 16 October 1905 — West Bengal (= WB + Bihar + Orissa) + new province of East Bengal & Assam (EBA = EB + Assam); EBA designed as Muslim Majority Province (MMP); Nawab Salimullah of Dacca + elite Muslim leadership welcome Partition; Prelims 2009: 16 October 1905 = Partition of Bengal took effect (NOT proclamation of Swadeshi Movement at Calcutta Town Hall / NOT Naoroji declared Swaraj / NOT Tilak started Swadeshi Movement in Poona); Prelims 2014: Partition lasted until King George V abrogated Curzon's Act at Royal Durbar in Delhi 1911

Boycott Resolution passed @ Calcutta Town Hall — Moderates including SNB, K.K. Mitra, Anand Mohan Bose + P.C. Ray pass resolution for boycott of British goods + institutions in response to Partition announcement; Moderates themselves cross a line; Swadeshi Movement begins; Prelims 2023: 7 August = National Handloom Day BECAUSE Swadeshi Movement launched on same day in 1905 (Both statements correct, II explains I)
Swadesh Bandhab Samiti (1905) of Ashwini Kumar Dutt in Barisal — notable Samiti; conducts Constructive Work specifically among Muslim ryots; organises Barisal Conference 1906

Extremists take over movement: add goal of Swaraj (self-rule) to demand for annulment of Bengal Partition; add Passive Resistance (PR) = NC + CD + threat of violent agitation if British respond with repression; take movement out of Bengal + spread nationally
Movement leaders: Bengal = C.R. Das + B.C. Pal; Bombay = Tilak; Delhi = Syed Haidar Raza; Punjab = Lala Lajpat Rai (L.L. Rai) + Ajit Singh; Madras = V.O. Chidambaram Pillai

Muslim League (ML1906) founded — actively supports Partition; works with Ulamas who control Muslim masses; deepens communal lines; reduces possibility of joint Hindu-Muslim resistance to Partition; ML1906 + Nawab Salimullah of Dacca + Ulamas = triple obstacle to Muslim participation in Swadeshi Movement
Barisal Conference — SNB + Aurobindo Ghosh distribute badges of Bande Mataram; police repress procession before it can even begin

INC Calcutta session 1906 — Dadabhai Naoroji as President (respected by both factions); Extremists get 4 resolutions passed: (i) Swaraj as goal; (ii) Boycott as method; (iii) Swadeshi as method; (iv) National Education as method; Bengal Partition separately condemned; Tilak sets up Extremist/Nationalist party within INC to convert INC from within; Prelims 2010: 4 resolutions passed at Calcutta session 1906 = Swaraj + Boycott + Swadeshi + National Education; the resolution NOT among them = Annulment of partition of Bengal (condemned separately, not one of the 4 resolutions)

Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company (1906) — founded by V.O. Chidambaram Pillai in Tuticorin; Indian-owned shipping line competing directly with British India Steam Navigation Company; most ambitious example of economic nationalism; Swadeshi applied to maritime trade
Tata Iron & Steel Company (TISCO) — conceived by Jamsetji Tata; established by son Dorabji Tata in 1907

INC Surat Split — planned for Poona or Nagpur (Extremist strongholds); Moderates shift venue to Surat (they have more control); flashpoint: fight over presidency (L.L. Rai vs Rash Behari Ghosh); L.L. Rai withdraws to prevent split but Extremists refuse compromise unless 4 Calcutta resolutions re-adopted; session collapses; shoes hurled, chairs broken; Extremists expelled from INC; Prelims 2016: main reason for Surat Split = Extremists' lack of faith in capacity of Moderates to negotiate with British Govt (NOT communalism by Lord Minto / NOT foundation of Muslim League / NOT Aurobindo unable to be elected President)
Punjab Canal Colony Agitations 1907 — L.L. Rai + Ajit Singh lead; L.L. Rai arrested + deported; Lahore Indian Association (1877) mobilises peasantry alongside Arya Samaj + Singh Sabha
Tilak deported to Mandalay, Burma (1908-14); Aurobindo retires from active politics; B.C. Pal retires temporarily
Allahabad Convention (Mehta Congress) 1908 — senior INC leaders' small meeting; declares: 'we are loyal to the Raj'; 1908 INC Annual Session @ Madras with Rash Behari Ghosh as President

Rise of Revolutionaries (1908-11) — Extremist mass politics has run out of steam with leaderless movement; those who concluded even Extremist methods failed -> more radical tendencies; failure of one approach -> more radical successor Bengal Partition ANNULLED + Capital shifted to Delhi from Calcutta — announced at Delhi Durbar December 1911 during coronation of King George V + Queen Mary as Emperor + Empress of India; Bengal = WB + EB reunited; Assam + Bihar & Orissa become separate; 1936: Bihar + Orissa also made full separate provinces

L.L. Rai goes abroad (1914-20) — London then United States; sets up 'Indian Home Rule League of America' Annie Besant + Tilak launch Home Rule Leagues (1915-17) Extremists RE-ENTER INC 1916 (Lucknow session; Lucknow Pact between INC + ML1906); but re-entry NOT same as agreement on methods; differences persist until Gandhi
Gandhi unites Moderates + Extremists (Nagpur session 1920) — INC divided from 1907 to 1920 = 13 years; Gandhi's new mass politics method provides common platform

1st formal INC resolution for Purna Swaraj — by Hasrat Mohani (with Swami Kumaranand) at Ahmedabad Session 1921; REJECTED by INC primarily due to strong opposition from Gandhi (argued demand was premature + irresponsible + Indian masses not yet disciplined enough for complete independence)

events.label: Mitra Mela founded by Savarkar brothers (Vinayak = Veer Savarkar + Ganesh) @ Nasik — secret society; inspiration: Mazzini's 'Young Italy' (active in 1830 revolts to overthrow Austrian colonialism in northern Italy; Italian unification 1870; Mazzini's method = guerrilla warfare; Savarkar sees direct parallel: Austrian colonialism over Italy = British colonialism over India)

Anushilan Samiti founded @ Calcutta by Pramathanath Mitra (P. Mitra) — begins as body for physical training + character building; inner purpose = cultivate spirit of armed resistance; Prelims 1996: Abhinav Bharat = V.D. Savarkar; Anushilan Samiti = Satish Chandra Basu (correct match)
Fraser Police Commission 1902 — recommends formal establishment of Criminal Investigation Department (CID); implemented 1903

CID (Criminal Investigation Department) formally established 1903 — professionalized network of spies + informers embedded in Indian society; designed specifically to track, infiltrate + dismantle political dissent + secret societies; structural response (not just legal); central to colonial repression throughout INM

Mitra Mela renamed ABHINAV BHARAT (1904) @ Pune — 'Young India' (after Mazzini's Young Italy); secret society; Veer Savarkar organiser; Prelims 1999: Abhinav Bharat organised by V.D. Savarkar (NOT Khudiram Bose / NOT Prafulla Chaki / NOT Bhagat Singh)

Indian Home Rule Society (IHRS) 1905 @ London — founded by Shyamji Krishna Varma; supported by Bhikaji Cama, Dadabhai Naoroji (NOT a revolutionary himself) + S.R. Rana; features: (i) goal = secure self-rule in India + propaganda in Britain; (ii) method = all practicable means; (iii) only Indians can be members; (iv) written constitution modelled on British institutions; (v) strong support among Indian students in Britain; (vi) close contact with revolutionaries in India; (vii) set up India House in London (student hostel promoting nationalist views); (viii) Shyamji's journal The Indian Sociologist (misleading name — not socialist) = foundation of militant Indian nationalist movement in Britain
Abhinav Bharat branch opened @ London by Veer Savarkar (1906) when he goes to London to study law; Mazzini Charitra 1906 (Savarkar compiles translation of Mazzini's writings @ London)

Jugantar (weekly newspaper, meaning 'New Era') founded 1906 — by Barindra Kumar Ghosh (younger brother of Aurobindo) + Bhupendranath Datta + Abinash Bhattacharya; radical inner circle of Anushilan Samiti; message after police repression of Barisal Conference April 1906: '30 crore Indians should raise their 60 crore hands to end oppression'; Jugantar party grows around this publication

Dacca Anushilan Samiti founded 1906 by Pulin Behari Das — with backing of P. Mitra + Bipin Chandra Pal; massive distinct offshoot from Calcutta Anushilan Samiti; rigidly hierarchical, highly centralised, strictly disciplined; Prelims 1995: Barrah Dacoity = 1st major venture of revolutionary terrorists in EAST BENGAL (NOT Bombay-Karnataka / NOT Punjab / NOT Madras Presidency)
All Bengal Conference of Revolutionary Groups 1906 — coordination meeting; leads to formation of Jugantar weekly (1906)
Shyamji Krishna Varma shifts to Paris 1907 — lead role at India House passes to Abhinav Bharat Mandal (Veer Savarkar's organisation)

Madame Bhikaji Cama unfurls 1st version of Indian national flag @ International Socialist Congress @ Stuttgart, Germany — dramatic assertion of Indian sovereignty on global stage; years before any official tricolour adopted; Prelims 1999: Madam Bhikaji Cama = International Socialist Conference Stuttgart 1907
Attempt on life of Lt Governor of Bengal (1907) — failed

BARRAH DACOITY 1908 — Swadeshi dacoity in Dhaka, East Bengal by Dacca Anushilan Samiti under Pulin Behari Das; residence of Zamindar of Barrah looted; funds intended to finance revolutionary activities; funds acquired by armed robbery to fund weapons + printing + travel (Zamindars seen as collaborators of colonial order); Prelims 1995: Barrah Dacoity = East Bengal

MUZZAFARPUR CONSPIRACY CASE 1908 — failed attempt on life of Magistrate Kingsford (particularly hated colonial official); Prafulla Chaki + Khudiram Bose throw bomb at his carriage; Kingsford not inside; two English women killed; Chaki shoots himself in mouth to avoid capture; Khudiram Bose arrested, tried, given death sentence; Bose 18 years old when executed 1908; execution makes him instant martyr across Bengal; songs written; image printed on cloth + sold as mourning wear; British intended execution to deter = had opposite effect

ALIPORE CONSPIRACY CASE (also: MurariPukur / ManickTolla Conspiracy Case) 1908 — British go after masterminds after Muzzafarpur; mass arrests including Aurobindo Ghosh from MurariPukur Road @ ManickTolla; Aurobindo defended by C.R. Das; B.C. Pal REFUSES to testify (without testimony Aurobindo cannot be convicted); Aurobindo acquitted; writes further anti-British articles; senses imminent re-arrest; escapes to PONDICHERRY (French control = outside British jurisdiction); turns to spiritualism + withdraws permanently from politics; Barindra Kumar Ghosh (Aurobindo's younger brother + principal Jugantar organiser) + Ullaskar Dutta + others found GUILTY; sentenced to death; sentences commuted to 'transportation for life' in Cellular Jail (Kala Pani), Andaman Islands; Alipore Case heavily decimates early Jugantar leadership; B.C. Pal forced to retire temporarily

TILAK TRIAL 1908 — Tilak writes article 'Arrival of Bomb' in Kesari: condemns violence of Prafulla Chaki + Khudiram Bose BUT simultaneously defends both men (sustained oppression will produce violence); British charge him with SEDITION; sentenced to 6 years imprisonment + deported to MANDALAY, BURMA; legal defence conducted by JINNAH (1908: Jinnah = young constitutional lawyer with nationalist sympathies; takes Tilak's case on principle; two men disagree on methods but on same side of anti-colonial divide; distance from 1908 to 1940 Pakistan demand = measure of how much communal politics transformed in 3 decades)

Savarkar authors The Indian War of Independence 1857 (1909) — recasts 1857 Revolt as planned war of national liberation (not mere 'mutiny'); British BAN it even before publication; copies circulate underground; become essential revolutionary reading
London: Madan Lal Dhingra kills Lt. Col. William Curzon-Wyllie (1909) — Abhinav Bharat network; NOT Curzon the Viceroy 1899-1905; Curzon-Wyllie = worked with Secretary of State for India
Nasik Conspiracy Case 1909 — District Magistrate Jackson killed by Anant Laxman Kanhere; Savarkar had sent pistols to India from London; one used by Kanhere
Morley-Minto Reforms (ICA 1909) — many contemporaries feel this is partly a result of British anxiety about spread of revolutionary activities; reform offered to buy peace

Savarkar sentenced to transportation for life (1910) — Cellular Jail, Andaman Islands; in connection with Nasik Conspiracy Case 1909; 'Transportation for life' = fate British consider worse than death; isolation + brutal prison conditions + permanent removal from mainland

Bengal Partition ANNULLED + capital shifted from Calcutta to DELHI — announced at Delhi Durbar December 1911 (coronation of King George V + Queen Mary as Emperor + Empress); annulment = political concession; capital shift = strategic correction (reducing Bengal's outsized influence over national movement)
Province of 'Bihar & Orissa' separated from Bengal Presidency; Assam made full province from 'East Bengal & Assam' (EBA1905) — post-1911 administrative tidying up of Bengal's territorial structure

DELHI CONSPIRACY CASE 1912 — capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi 1911; grand procession organised in Delhi; Rash Behari Bose plans + executes failed assassination attempt against Viceroy Hardinge10-16 (1910-1916) in Chandni Chowk; Hardinge seated on elephant during procession; Rash Behari Bose throws bomb from balcony; Hardinge wounded but survives

Ghadar Movement (1913-15) — Rash Behari Bose provides leadership; founded primarily by Lala Hardayal + Sohan Singh Bhakna @ San Francisco; Prelims 1996: Ghadar Party = Sri Sohan Singh Bhakna (correct match)
Rash Behari Bose escapes to JAPAN 1915

Rash Behari Bose convenes conferences in Tokyo + Bangkok 1942 — establishes Indian Independence League (IIL); supreme political organisation for Indians living in Southeast Asia; under IIL's political backing, Captain Mohan Singh organises Indian Prisoners of War (captured by Japanese) into 1st Indian National Army (INA); after arrest of Capt Mohan Singh, Rash Behari Bose takes over INA leadership; due to old age hands over to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose 1943
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose takes over INA (1943) — reorganises into Azad Hind Fauj; through-line from Delhi Conspiracy Case 1912 to INA 1943 passes through Rash Behari Bose
