events.label: Mohammadan Association (1855) — pro-British; opposes 1857 revolts; seeks benefits for Muslims through loyalty to British (not nationalist cause); earliest organised Muslim political body
1857 Revolt — Mohammadan Association stays loyal to British; post-1857 British further favour Muslims (fear of unified Hindu-Muslim front; already saw Hindu-Muslim unity in 1857 as greatest danger)

W.W. Hunter's Indian Musalmans (1871) — argues British neglect of Muslims contributed to Faraizi movement 1830s-70s in Bengal; argues British should appease Muslims for greater political stability; becomes justification for DnR approach of favouring Muslim interests against Hindu-dominated political formations
Census first attempted 1872 (not complete for all of British India); 1881 = 1st FULL census of British India; conducted every 10 years (1881, 1891, 1901...)

Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (1817-98): Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College @ Aligarh (1875) — combines Western education with Islamic values; builds Muslim middle class that can compete for government positions; explicitly argues Muslims are a separate qaum (ethno-religious community/nation) with separate interests from Hindus (early form of Two Nation Theory); argues Muslim qaum as ruling community before British deserves special status

Hindi-Urdu Controversy (1880s-1900) in North West Provinces + Awadh (1877) — led by Madan Mohan Malviya; demands official status for Hindi equivalent to Urdu; Hindi granted official status 1900; unintended byproduct: Hindi becomes associated with Hindus + Urdu with Muslims; communal linguistic divide deepens

Census 1881 (1st full census) — Muslim population ~20% overall; majority in Punjab; ~50% in Bengal; census creates + reinforces consciousness of being a homogeneous religious group among otherwise heterogeneous Muslim community (poor Muslim weaver in Bengal + rich Muslim landlord in Punjab = same community in census logic); British publish religion-wise reports on education, employment + poverty = creates sense of relative deprivation among Muslims (behind Hindus in govt jobs + education + new middle-class professions)
Swami Dayanand Saraswati dies 1883 — Arya Samaj becomes more aggressive post-1883; Shuddhi movement + Cow Protection Movement become more militant
Mohammadan Educational Congress (1886) — set up by Sir Syed as deliberate rival to INC; believes INC is a Hindu organisation; actively discourages Muslim participation in INC

Cow Killing Riots 1893 — result of aggressive Cow Protection Movement by Arya Samaj; INC stays SILENT (its 1886 rule = only political issues); non-condemnation = sharp decline in Muslim participation in INC
British reservation in government jobs for Muslims (1897) — DnR measure to appease Muslim elite
Hindi granted official status alongside Urdu (1900) — Hindi-Urdu controversy resolution; further communal linguistic divide

Bengal Partition (16 Oct 1905) — creates East Bengal + Assam as Muslim Majority Province (MMP); appeases elite Muslims + counters rising Hindu nationalism; Nawab Salimullah of Dacca + elite Muslim leadership welcome Partition

Swadeshi Movement (1905-11) — Hindu symbolism (Bande Mataram, Kali worship, Prabhat Pheris, Ganpati + Shivaji Festivals) contributes to Muslim alienation from movement Simla Deputation (1906) — elite Muslims led by Aga Khan meet Viceroy Minto05-10 @ Shimla; demands: (i) no annulment of Bengal Partition; (ii) reservation proportional to population in ILC, PLCs + govt jobs; (iii) SEPARATE ELECTORATES in future council reforms (= only Muslims vote in Muslim reserved seats; structurally promotes Two Nation Theory; tells every Muslim voter their representative must be Muslim + their interests are separate from Hindu interests); Separate Electorates = hinge of partition history

All India Muslim League (ML1906) founded @ Dacca, December 1906 — immediately following Simla Deputation; features: (i) goal: ensure British don't go back on Simla promises + promote Muslim interests + promote Muslim loyalty to British; (ii) constitution = 'Green Book' written by Mohsin-ul-Mulk + Mohammed Ali Jauhar (both of Aligarh movement); (iii) 1907-09: Provincial Muslim Leagues set up; functional provincial structures for >13 years before INC's PCCs became effective mass instruments (organisational head start for communal politics)

K.G. Gupta + Syed Hussain Bilgrami appointed to Secretary of State's India Council in London — 1st Indians in London administration; precursor action (NOT a provision of ICA1909 itself; done before ICA1909 was passed)

London branch of ML1906 set up (1908) under presidency of Ameer Ali — Prelims 2001: London branch of ML1906 under presidency of = Ameer Ali (NOT Aga Khan / NOT Liaquat Ali Khan / NOT MA Jinnah); this London branch influences ICA1909 (introduces Separate Electorates for Muslims in reformed councils)
ICA1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) — substantive detail in Sec 2 table below
Partition of India — direct consequence of Separate Electorates introduced in ICA1909 + organised communal politics of ML1906; legislative seed of 1947 planted in 1909

tables.title: ICA 1909 (MORLEY-MINTO REFORMS) — COMPLETE PROVISIONS
lines: Context Swadeshi Movement (1905-11) + Surat Split (1907) + Revolutionary Activities (1908+) + DnR strategy:
split Moderates from Extremists; hint of reform in Morley's 1906 Parliament Budget speech widens
Moderate-Extremist fault line -> Surat Split 1907; British repress Extremists + reform for Moderates
simultaneously
Names SoS = John Morley (Liberal in British political tradition; personally open to Indian participation in
governance); Viceroy = Minto05-10 (1905-1910); also called Morley-Minto Reforms
Nature of Govt NOT Responsible Government (Morley explicitly: 'no intent of Responsible Govt in India via ICA1909';
Responsible Govt = every minister must first be elected member of legislature; Executive = child of
Parliament accountable to it); ICA1909 introduces Representative Government (= Limited
Self-Government = some partnership in domestic affairs; not self-rule); even by Moderates' own older
standard, reform arrives too late (INC goal since 1906 Calcutta session = Swaraj, not just Limited
Self-Govt)
VEC UNCHANGED: GG + CIC + 6 Ordinary Members (same as ICA1892)
ILC Size 69 members total = 8 ex-officio (VEC: GG + CIC + 6 ordinary members since 1874) + 1 rotating
ex-officio (Governor/LG of province where session held) + 60 additional members (27 elected + 33
nominated [28 officials + 5 non-officials])
Official Majority YES — Officers = 9 ex-officio + 28 nominated officials = 37; Non-officers = 27 elected + 5 nominated
(ILC) non-officials = 32; British do NOT give up control at Centre
FEATURE ICA 1909 PROVISION
PLCs 1st time NON-OFFICIAL MAJORITY introduced in PLCs (not in ILC); BUT most non-official members =
NOMINATED, not elected; Bengal Exception: Bengal PLC got ELECTED majority (1st province to
have this) but 4 of those elected seats reserved for European Businesses
Elections — 1st PROPER INDIRECT ELECTIONS: taxpayers + rent payers who meet threshold criteria elect local
General bodies -> local bodies elect electoral college from among themselves -> electoral college elects PLC
members -> PLC members elect ILC members; word 'ELECTION' used officially for 1st time in
ICA1909 (ICA1892 deliberately avoided the word)
SEPARATE 1st time separate electorates for Muslims introduced in ILC, PLCs + local bodies; 8 of 27 elected ILC
ELECTORATES seats reserved for Muslims (~30%); Muslim population = ~20%; extra 10% above population share =
FOR MUSLIMS pure appeasement politics; ONLY MUSLIMS vote in Muslim reserved seats; Muslims ALSO had right
to vote in general (unreserved) seats = double advantage; income threshold for Muslims set LOWER
than for other communities (easier to qualify for R2Vote); DIRECT elections for Muslim seats (1st direct
elections anywhere under ICA1909); joint electorates (as in India's SC reservations today) vs separate
electorates = fundamentally different: Reservation + Joint Electorates = Candidate of the People, For
the People, By a Community; Reservation + Separate Electorates = Candidate of a Group, For a
Group, By a Group; conceptually: Country = Sum of Constituencies -> today it's 'our constituencies' ->
tomorrow it's 'our Pakistan'
Indians in 1st time: S.P. Sinha (Satyendra Prasanna Sinha) inducted into VEC as Law Member = 1st Indian in
Executive Viceroy's Executive Council (under ICA1909 provision); K.G. Gupta + Syed Hussain Bilgrami
appointed to SoS's India Council in London August 1907 = precursor action (NOT ICA1909 provision)
Budget Vote on INDIVIDUAL items in Budget allowed for 1st time (ICA1892 = discussion only, NO vote); vote
on WHOLE Budget NOT allowed (rejecting whole Budget = No Confidence Motion; British would not
allow that)
Supplementary ALLOWED for 1st time (ICA1892 = no supplementary questions at all); but ONLY the member who
Questions asked original question can ask supplementary
Resolutions Members can initiate + pass resolutions (ICA1892 = opposition could not move resolutions, no vote on
govt resolutions); BUT resolutions = RECOMMENDATORY ONLY; govt under no obligation to follow
them
Rejection Power Govt retains power to reject/disqualify any candidate considered politically dangerous (= Nationalists);
(Executive) 1892 = power of selection (chose who could stand); 1909 = power of rejection (removes those they
don't want); nationalist leaders kept out of councils either way
Executive Executive remains NON-RESPONSIBLE to Legislature; Viceroy's powers unchanged; NOT remotely
Accountability close to ceremonial President in a democracy
Minto's Title Minto05-10 = 'Father of Communal Electorate' — title history has not handed down with pride
Lifespan 10 years (shortest of all Council reforms); timeline: ICA1861 -> 30 yrs -> ICA1892 -> 17 yrs -> ICA1909
-> 10 yrs -> GOI 1919 -> 16 yrs -> GOI 1935 -> 15 yrs -> COI 1950; Prelims 1999: most short-lived of
all British constitutional experiments = ICA1909 (NOT ICA1861 / NOT ICA1892 / NOT GOI Act 1919)
Legacy Separate Electorates = legislative seed of 1947 partition; Prelims 2002: NOT correct statement about
ICA1909 + ML1906 = 'ML1906 vehemently opposed partition of Bengal + separate electorates' =
FALSE (ML1906 SUPPORTED Bengal Partition + DEMANDED Separate Electorates); also called
Benevolent Despotism: 'Benevolent' = more democratic than ICA1892; 'Despotism' = real power
remains entirely with British Executive answerable to nobody in India

anchors: Separate Electorates vs Joint Electorates — The Constitutional Difference: Joint Electorates (India's SC/ST reservations
today): Candidate from reserved community; ALL voters (any religion/caste) vote for that candidate. = 'Candidate of the People,
For the People, By a Community' -> community member represents all constituents. Separate Electorates (ICA1909 for Muslims):
ONLY Muslims vote in Muslim seats; Muslim candidates represent only Muslim constituents. = 'Candidate of a Group, For a Group,
By a Group' -> group member represents only group members. Logical extension: Country = Sum of Constituencies -> today 'our
constituencies' -> tomorrow 'our Pakistan'. Muslims also kept right to vote in UNRESERVED seats = double advantage (influence
both reserved Muslim seats + general seats). ICA1909 Separate Electorates -> institutionally accepted Two Nation Theory -> 1947
Partition.
PCCs — Trap Alert: PCCs (Provincial Congress Committees) existed formally from INC's 1908 Constitution (NOT first established
at 1920 Nagpur Session). 1920 Nagpur Session (Gandhi): PCCs REORGANISED on linguistic lines (not administrative province
lines); local Congress work could now happen in mother tongue; INC could penetrate villages. Before 1920: PCCs ran in English +
mapped to British administrative provinces = elite organisation. After 1920: PCCs in local languages + linguistic boundaries = mass
organisation. ML1906 had functional provincial structures for 13+ years before INC's PCCs became effective mass instruments =
communal politics had organisational head start.
n Prelims Cluster — ML1906 + ICA1909 (1999 + 2001 + 2002): 1999: Most short-lived of all British constitutional experiments =
ICA 1909 (NOT ICA 1861 / NOT ICA 1892 / NOT GOI Act 1919); lifespan = 10 years. 2001: London branch of ML1906 (1908) set
up under presidency of = Ameer Ali (NOT Aga Khan / NOT Liaquat Ali Khan / NOT MA Jinnah). 2002: NOT correct statement =
'ML1906 vehemently opposed partition of Bengal and separate electorates' = FALSE; ML1906 SUPPORTED Bengal Partition +
DEMANDED Separate Electorates (both at Simla Deputation 1906 + ML founding Dec 1906).

events.label: Punjabis helped British suppress 1857 revolt; Ghadr newspaper later explicitly criticises this + calls for penance; '31 crore Indians should rise against 1.2 lakh British + repeat 1857 revolt'; masthead of Ghadr carries date of 1857 revolt
Police Act 1861 + CID (1903) = British intelligence network strengthened enough by 1914-15 to deeply infiltrate Ghadar Movement

Jugantar party 1906 (Barindra Kumar Ghosh, younger brother of Aurobindo) — Bagha Jatin later reunifies shattered Jugantar factions inside Bengal; Ghadar connects with Jugantar network for Bengal operations

Tarak Nath Das publishes Free Hindustan (1907) from Vancouver — exposes plantation-vs-migration irony: Britain sends Indians as plantation labourers to Fiji in South Pacific BUT bars their entry into North America; Canada restricts Indian entry since 1908 (only those making direct journey from India allowed); 1783 Treaty of Paris between US + Britain = perpetual friendship -> US respected British interests -> Indians faced racism + legally barred from buying land in USA
Canada restricts Indian entry (1908) — only those making UNBROKEN DIRECT JOURNEY from India allowed to enter Canada; ex-Indian Army soldiers who served the very British Empire being shut out
G.D. Kumar publishes Swadesh Sevak (Gurmukhi weekly) from Canada (1909) — directly asks Indian troops to revolt

Rash Behari Bose throws bomb at Viceroy Hardinge10-16 in Chandni Chowk Delhi (Delhi Conspiracy Case 1912); Hardayal praises this attack; Hardayal establishes Bakunin Institute @ Oakland, California (1912) — describes it as 'monastery of anarchism'; Michael Bakunin (1814-1876) = Russian thinker + founding figure of anarchism: State = instrument of oppression; don't petition it, don't reform it, DESTROY it (destructive act = creative act; demolish old structure so truly democratic system can be built; link = Stateless Society of Karl Marx); KEY ANARCHIST CONCEPT FOR GHADAR: 'Propaganda of the Deed' (specific political actions including violence + armed mutiny are more powerful than any speech/pamphlet in awakening masses; words educate, acts ignite; Delhi Conspiracy Case 1912 = exactly this kind of act)

Ghadar Party set up by NRIs in US (1913) — HQ @ San Francisco called YUGANTAR ASHRAM (same terminology as Bengal secret societies); 1st President: Sohan Singh Bhakna; members: Indian immigrants (farmers, labourers, students, ex-soldiers) mostly Punjabis; word 'Ghadar' = revolt/mutiny (deliberate invocation of 1857); Prelims 2014: Ghadar = revolutionary association of Indians with HQ @ San Francisco (NOT nationalist org from Singapore / NOT militant org from Berlin / NOT communist movement from Tashkent)
events.full: Ghadar Party set up by NRIs in US (1913) — HQ @ San Francisco called YUGANTAR ASHRAM (same terminology as Bengal secret societies); 1st President: Sohan Singh Bhakna (Prelims 1996: Ghadar Party = Sri Sohan Singh Bhakna); members: Indian immigrants (farmers, labourers, students, ex-soldiers) mostly Punjabis; word 'Ghadar' = revolt/mutiny (deliberate invocation of 1857); Prelims 2014: Ghadar = revolutionary association of Indians with HQ @ San Francisco (NOT nationalist org from Singapore / NOT militant org from Berlin / NOT communist movement from Tashkent)

events.label: Lala Hardayal (1913) — Professor of Sanskrit + Indian philosophy @ San Francisco; sets up weekly 'The Ghadr'; Prelims 1998: leader of Ghadar Party = Lala Hardayal (NOT Bhagat Singh / NOT Tilak / NOT V.D. Savarkar)

The Ghadr newspaper (1913) — most visible product of 'Propaganda of the Deed in Print'; front page: 'Angrezi Raj ka kachcha Chithha' (exposé of British imperialism); content: (i) summarises all INM demands + grievances; (ii) publishes Savarkar's Indian War of Independence 1909 in parts; (iii) poems titled 'Ghadr Di Goonj' promoting patriotism + unity of all religions (consciously echoes 1857 Hindu-Muslim unity); (iv) criticises loyalist role of Punjabis in 1857 (message = do penance, improve past mistake); (v) final call: '31 crore Indians should rise against 1.2 lakh British + repeat 1857 revolt'; published in Urdu + Punjabi + Hindi + sometimes English; smuggled into India + distributed among soldiers + peasants in Punjab; Prelims 2005: Ghadar revolutionaries active during outbreak of WW1 based in NORTH AMERICA (NOT Central / West / South America)
Komagata Maru departs Hong Kong (April 1914) — Baba Gurdit Singh charters Japanese ship from Hong Kong; 376 passengers (mostly Punjabi Sikhs); challenges Canada's racist 'direct journey' rule
Komagata Maru arrives @ Vancouver (May 1914) — Shore Committee set up to fight for passengers' rights; British refuse; 2-month standoff begins; Canadian authorities refuse to let passengers disembark

Komagata Maru forced out of Canadian waters (July 1914) + begins return journey to India; World War I begins July 28, 1914 (Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia; within a week: Germany + Russia + France + Britain all enter); Prelims 2005: Komagata Maru = a naval ship on voyage to Canada (NOT political party / NOT Chinese peasant leader / NOT Chinese village where Mao began long march)

Rodda & Co. Arms Heist (August 1914, 26 Aug) — colonial Statesman newspaper calls it 'greatest daylight robbery' in history of British India; target: R.B. Rodda & Co. Calcutta (prestigious British-owned gunsmith + arms dealer; primary supplier of firearms to British officials, military + wealthy elites); revolutionary groups: Atmonnati Samiti + Mukti Sangha (affiliated with Bagha Jatin's Jugantar network); insider: Shrish Chandra Mitra (trusted Rodda employee); Rodda received major restricted German firearms shipment @ Calcutta Customs House; Shrish Mitra goes to customs house with 7 bullock carts to collect 202 wooden crates of arms; Revolutionary Haridas Datta disguises himself as bullock cart driver; first 6 carts reach Rodda warehouse; Shrish Mitra quietly redirects 7th cart into narrow lanes of Malanga area -> revolutionary safehouse; STOLEN ARSENAL from single cart: 50 Mauser C96 semi-automatic pistols ('Broomhandle' Mauser) + 46,000 rounds of 7.63mm ammunition; Mauser C96 = hollow wooden holster attaches to grip converting pistol to short-barrelled carbine rifle -> unprecedented rapid-fire capability + range; Shrish Mitra flees Calcutta (never captured); stolen Mausers distributed across Jugantar network; used in almost every major political assassination + armed robbery in Bengal over next decade; most famously: WEAPONS AT

Komagata Maru arrives @ Budge Budge near Calcutta (September 1914) — British try to forcibly transport passengers to Punjab by special train; passengers resist; BUDGE BUDGE RIOT (September 1914): police open fire, killing ~20 passengers; incident radicalises many Punjabis + feeds directly into Ghadar recruitment (proved Indians humiliated both abroad + at home); Ghadarites start returning to India

WW1 context — Britain stretched on multiple fronts; Ghadarites see opportunity; British treat returning Komagata Maru passengers as highly dangerous enemy operatives under wartime conditions PLOT 1: Rash Behari Bose's planned Punjab Mutiny (February 21, 1915) — thousands of Ghadarite NRIs return to India from North America; Rash Behari Bose operates in Lahore to establish contact with sepoys; mutiny scheduled for Feb 21 1915; British intelligence DEEPLY INFILTRATES movement; plot CRUSHED PRE-EMPTIVELY before it could begin; leads to FIRST LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE trials; failure reasons: (i) strong British intelligence network; (ii) poor response from sepoys (Peel Commission post-1857 deliberately reduced political consciousness in army; low western education); (iii) Udasi Sikh Mahants (socially influential priests of Gurudwaras) are pro-British + actively ask religious masses NOT to support Ghadarites
events.full: 1914-15 1915 Feb — WW1 context — Britain stretched on multiple fronts; Ghadarites see opportunity; British treat returning Komagata Maru passengers as highly dangerous enemy operatives under wartime conditions PLOT 1: Rash Behari Bose's planned Punjab Mutiny (February 21, 1915) — thousands of Ghadarite NRIs return to India from North America; Rash Behari Bose operates in Lahore to establish contact with sepoys; mutiny scheduled for Feb 21 1915; British intelligence DEEPLY INFILTRATES movement; plot CRUSHED PRE-EMPTIVELY before it could begin; leads to FIRST LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE trials; failure reasons: (i) strong British intelligence network; (ii) poor response from sepoys (Peel Commission post-1857 deliberately reduced political consciousness in army; low western education); (iii) Udasi Sikh Mahants (socially influential priests of Gurudwaras) are pro-British + actively ask religious masses NOT to support Ghadarites

events.label: Defence of India Act 1915 (March 1915, Emergency) — wartime emergency law; Ghadarites suppressed under it; provisions: (i) detention without trial; (ii) Special tribunals replace ordinary courts; (iii) no right of appeal; link forward: Rowlatt Acts 1919 (Anarchical + Revolutionary Crimes Act 1919) seeks to continue emergency powers even post-WWI

First Lahore Conspiracy Case (April-September 1915) — mass trial of captured Ghadarites; many sentenced to death; many to transportation for life; hundreds interned in villages under Defence of India Act 1915; effectively crushes organisational backbone of Ghadar movement inside India

PLOT 2: Jugantar's Pacific Arms Plot (April-July 1915) — Germany finances massive arms-smuggling operation; 30,000 rifles + ammunition to be shipped from US to eastern coast of India via ship SS Maverick; ships (Annie Larsen + SS Maverick) intercepted by US + British authorities; arsenal never reaches Indian coast
Rash Behari Bose escapes to Japan (May 1915) — British fail to arrest him; later key in establishing IIL 1942 + handing over INA to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose 1943

BATTLE OF BALASORE / CHASAKHAND / BURIBALAM (September 1915) — police forces corner Bagha Jatin (Jatindranath Mukherjee) + 4 followers near banks of Burhabalanga river, Balasore, Odisha; 5 revolutionaries: Bagha Jatin + Chittapriya Ray Chaudhuri + Manoranjan Sengupta + Niren Dasgupta + Jyotish Pal; 5 men vs heavily armed British colonial police + mobilised local villagers; duration: ~75 minutes; TACTIC: took defensive military position behind termite mound + raised embankment in muddy paddy field @ Chasakhand; armed with stolen Rodda Mauser C96 pistols (high-grade semi-automatic; range rivalled police rifles); five men pinned down full police force in trench-warfare-style standoff until literally ran out of ammunition; Bagha Jatin severely wounded; dies in hospital next day; his rallying cry: 'Amra morbo, jagat jagbe' ('We shall die to awaken the nation') — he kept his word; this effectively ends Christmas Day plot before it could materialise
Kartar Singh Sarabha arrested + hanged (November 1915) — only 19 years old; becomes martyr-hero of revolutionary movement; Bhagat Singh later keeps Sarabha's photograph in his pocket

PLOT 3: Jugantar's Christmas Day Plot / Bengal Plot (December 1915) — with Punjab mutiny crushed + Pacific arms intercepted, focus shifts to Bengal; revolutionaries plan massive uprising in Calcutta on Christmas Day 1915; expecting separate delivery of German arms to land in Bay of Bengal/Sundarbans; British intelligence cracks communication codes using international double agents + Indian CID; network intercepted; final leg of Hindu-German Conspiracy fatally crushed; movement collapses
Second Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929-30) — Bhagat Singh + HSRA (1928); DO NOT CONFUSE with First Lahore Conspiracy Case (1915, Ghadar Movement)

events.label: Lord Rosebery coins phrase 'Commonwealth of Nations' (1884) — Annie Besant later popularises the idea of a voluntary Commonwealth of Nations; she authors Commonwealth of India Bill (1925) proposing Dominion Status for India
Tilak at Ganpati Festival 1893 — makes Lord Ganapati (worshipped by both UC + LC) the centrepiece; focus on caste unity goes back to this point even before his later famous quote on untouchability
Tilak publishes Kesari (Marathi) + Maharatta (English) — aggressive use of press; jailed for sedition; deported to Mandalay, Burma 1908-14

G. Subramania Iyer (Journalist, 1855-1916): co-founds The Hindu (English) 1878 @ Madras specifically to protest appointment of Anglo-Indian judge over native Indian candidate; founds Swadesamitran (Tamil nationalist daily) 1882; co-founds Madras Mahajan Sabha 1884; moves historically significant 1st resolution at 1st INC session @ Bombay 1885
Swadesamitran (Tamil nationalist daily) founded by G. Subramania Iyer (1882)
G. Subramania Iyer (Journalist) moves historically significant 1st resolution at 1st INC session @ Bombay (1885)

Sir S. Subramania Iyer (Jurist, 1842-1924) appointed Judge of Madras High Court (1895); knighted 1900 (K.C.I.E. = Knight Commander of the Indian Empire) -> title 'Sir'; later becomes Acting Chief Justice of Madras HC; co-founder + Honorary President of Home Rule League in Madras (1916) alongside Annie Besant; 1917: writes explosive letter to US President Woodrow Wilson + renounces knighthood in protest of Besant's arrest
Sir S. Subramania Iyer (Jurist) knighted 1900 (K.C.I.E.)

Recording Secretary of Theosophical Society 1905-06: Sir S. Subramania Iyer; VP of Theosophical Society 1907-11: Sir S. Subramania Iyer; George Arundale = Organising Secretary of Besant's HRL (right hand to Besant; does heavy lifting of building HRL network across India) Tilak's re-entry into INC blocked in 1906; ICA1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) brings Limited Self-Government but NOT Swaraj; Moderates' 2nd failure (1st was ICA1892)

Annie Besant joins INC (1914) — head of Theosophical Society based @ Madras; Irish woman inspired by Home Rule movement in Ireland; wants self-rule for India; campaigns within INC for re-entry of Extremists; attempt fails in 1914 due to opposition from Pherozshah Mehta (leader of Bombay Moderates)

Tilak returns from Mandalay, Burma (1914) after 6 years imprisonment — INM at dull phase; Extremists + Revolutionaries firmly suppressed; Moderates irrelevant; Tilak strategy: (i) declares Swaraj means self-rule WITHIN British Empire (not overthrow of British rule); (ii) violence has hurt INM; (iii) all Indians should support British war effort; (iv) loyal to Crown; TACTICAL MOVE: makes it difficult for British to repress Extremists again + positions Extremists as compatible with INC's Moderate framework

WW1 begins July 28, 1914 — Gandhi travels across India wanting youth to join British India Army to support Britain in WW1 (believes Allies on side of justice as victims of aggression; not against using WW1 opportunity the way HRL leaders were; Gandhi does NOT join HRLs)

INC Bombay Session 1915 — finally decides to allow re-entry of Extremists (P.M. Mehta had died); INC still does NOT agree to support Home Rule Leagues (Moderates worried: educative propaganda might slide into NC, CD, or violence); actual re-entry of Extremists at 1916 Lucknow Session
Tilak sets up Indian Home Rule League (April 1916) — 6 branches; HQ @ Poona; territory: Bombay Province/Maharashtra (EXCEPT Bombay city), Berar, Karnataka, Central Provinces

Annie Besant sets up All India Home Rule League (September 1916) — 200 branches; HQ @ Madras; territory: REST of British India; Jinnah also joins Besant's All India HRL + becomes President of its Bombay branch; both leagues cooperate but choose NOT to merge (prevent friction among respective followers); Prelims 2018: which changed its name to Swarajya Sabha in 1920 = All India Home Rule League

DEMANDS of HRLs: goal = educative propaganda on Home Rule + Swaraj; Tilak's slogan: 'Swaraj is my birthright + I shall have it'; beyond Swaraj: (i) education in vernacular languages; (ii) linguistic reorganisation of Provinces of British India; (iii) end to untouchability; (iv) Tilak argues demand for self-rule = NOT because British are Christians but because India + Britain have DIVERGENT NATIONAL INTERESTS (reduces communal/religious colouring; therefore Tilak makes less use of Hindu nationalism in HRL period)
Lucknow Pact (1916) — Tilak + Jinnah + Besant combined efforts lead to this; detail in SEC 2 below

Besant arrested + interned (1917) — TURNING POINT; arrest energises movement: (i) even Moderates join HRLs (British overreach unites factions); (ii) Sir S. Subramania Iyer (Jurist) renounces knighthood + writes letter to Woodrow Wilson (powerful symbolic act); (iii) Gandhi begins signature campaign for Besant's release

Montague Statement 1917 — British deploy as DnR tactic ('British will give Swaraj gradually'); within movement: Extremists propose Passive Resistance programme; Moderates oppose; Besant sides with Moderates; ideological divide: Besant = constitutionalist; deeply feared anarchy; opposed law-breaking aspect; believed deliberately disobeying law -> chaos + mob violence; this fundamental divide is exactly why she later completely breaks away from Gandhi when NCM launched 1920
Besant released + made INC President at 1917 Calcutta Session
1918 All India Depressed Classes Conference — Tilak: 'If God tolerates untouchability then I won't recognise him as God' (specific quote delivered here)
All India Home Rule League renamed SWARAJYA SABHA (1920)
Besant completely breaks with Gandhi over Non-Cooperation Movement 1920 (she had sided with Moderates against Passive Resistance in 1917; consistent with her constitutionalism + fear of anarchy)
Annie Besant authors Commonwealth of India Bill (1925) — proposes Dominion Status for India; direct extension of her lifelong campaign for self-governance within Empire

Montague Statement (1917) + GOI Act 1919 contributions partially from HRL + Lucknow Pact pressure; Motilal Nehru Report (August 1928) = 1st time phrase 'Dominion Status' formally used (implied by Lucknow Pact 1916's 'equal status with other Self-Governing Dominions' but not explicitly)

phases.label: LUCKNOW PACT (1916) + DECADE OF MUSLIM ALIENATION (1911–1920)

events.label: ML1906 founded @ Dacca — initially maintains loyal, deferential tone toward British; founded with British support

Annulment of Bengal Partition (1911) — ML1906 had supported Partition (created Muslim-majority East Bengal); abrupt reversal to appease Extremist agitation; seen as MASSIVE BETRAYAL by ML1906; Phase 1 of Decade of Alienation

Italy takes over Libya from Ottoman Empire (1911) — Khalifa = political + religious head of Muslim world globally; Britain does nothing to stop this; shatters illusion of British loyalty to Muslim interests
1st Balkan War (1912) — Montenegro + Serbia + Greece + Bulgaria attack + take over Ottoman territories in Balkan peninsula; Ottoman Empire dismembered piece by piece
WW1 begins (July 28, 1914) — Ottoman Empire fights as part of CENTRAL POWERS against Britain + Allied Powers; Indian Muslims in deep moral crisis (religious head = Khalifa is enemy of Britain)

Lucknow Pact (LP1916) — agreement between INC (1885) + ML1906; 1st time INC + ML1906 give JOINT DEMANDS to British for constitutional reforms; ML1906 also supports HRLs; combined efforts of Tilak + Jinnah + Besant lead to this

Lucknow Pact (LP1916) — JOINT DEMANDS: (i) continue Separate Electorates in future council reforms; (ii) expand councils + bring ELECTED majority (ICA1909 had only non-official majority + only in PLCs not ILC); (iii) at least 50% Indians in VEC; (iv) franchise as broad as possible + direct elections (NOT Universal Adult Franchise yet; formal UAF demand = Motilal Nehru Report 1928); (v) Self-Government at an early date = equal status with other Self-Governing Dominions of British Empire (implies Dominion Status; exact phrase 'Dominion Status' 1st used in Motilal Nehru Report August 1928)

Lucknow Pact — HINDU-MUSLIM ELECTORAL COMPROMISE: ML1906 agrees to give up right to vote in General/Unreserved constituencies; INC formally accepts Separate Electorates + agrees to guaranteed fixed quota of seats for Muslims in legislatures; British later adopt mechanics of this compromise into GOI Act 1919 (strictly segregated 'watertight' electoral rolls = Muslims vote ONLY in Muslim-reserved seats; NOT in unreserved seats)

Lucknow Pact — ASSESSMENT: NEGATIVE: major landmark in Two Nation Theory; INC formally concedes Hindus + Muslims = separate political communities needing separate electoral representation; significant + dangerous concession in hindsight; POSITIVE: INC-ML1906 unity which Gandhi later uses effectively in Khilafat Movement (1919-24) + NCM (1920-22); creates pressure on British -> Montague Statement 1917 + GOI Act 1919; fails British DnR strategy

Balfour Declaration (1917) — Britain declares intent to create Jewish homeland from Palestine (part of Ottoman Empire); Ottoman Empire populated by Turks + Arabs; Arabs had supported Britain in war + had begun civil war against Ottoman Turks; Britain's promise of Jewish homeland = 'stab in the back' for Arabs; Phase 2 of Decade of Alienation
Montague Statement (1917) — 'British will give Swaraj gradually'; intended as DnR tactic to split Moderates from Extremists on Passive Resistance question

Treaty of Sevres negotiations begin — harsh treaty signed with Ottoman Empire post-WW1 (1914-19); seen by Indian Muslims as breach of British promises (during war, British promised to maintain dignity of Khalifa to secure cooperation of Indian Muslims: civilians not striking, joining army, not resigning from army); Treaty of Sevres violates this: (i) Arab regions of Ottoman Empire converted into colonies of Britain + France (France = Syria; Britain = Iraq + Palestine + Transjordan); (ii) Greece given many Turk-populated areas including Smyrna (actually in Turkish mainland) + Eastern Thrace; (iii) Khalifa loses control over religious sites like Hagia Sophia (Istanbul under League of Nations control)

Treaty of Sevres signed (1920) — direct trigger for Khilafat Movement (1919-24); entire decade of alienation (1911-1920) culminates in Khilafat + NCM; Gandhi uses INC-ML1906 unity from Lucknow Pact 1916 to lead Khilafat + NCM jointly

anchors: Passive Resistance — 3 Different Understandings: (1) Aurobindo's Extremist definition (April 1907 Bande Mataram, 'Doctrine of
Passive Resistance'): umbrella term explicitly including NC (boycott British goods/schools/courts/admin) + CD (deliberately break
oppressive laws + accept punishment); 'passive' = non-violent means only. (2) Besant's constitutionalist refusal: willing to agitate +
petition + spread propaganda right to edge of legality; deep-seated fear of anarchy; strictly opposes law-breaking aspect; believes
deliberately disobeying law -> chaos + mob violence; this is why she completely breaks with Gandhi over NCM 1920. (3) Gandhi's
complete rejection of the TERM 'Passive Resistance': to Gandhi, both NC + CD are highly active, fearless moral forces =
SATYAGRAHA; never passive; Gandhi does not use the term 'Passive Resistance' at all.
Decade of Muslim Alienation (1911–1920) — 5 Events: Phase 1 (triggers for Lucknow Pact 1916): (1) 1911: Annulment of
Bengal Partition (ML1906 supported it; reversal = betrayal). (2) 1911: Italy takes over Libya from Ottoman Empire; Britain does
nothing (Khalifa = religious head of Muslim world). (3) 1912: 1st Balkan War (Ottoman territories taken). (4) 1914: WW1 begins;
Ottoman Empire = Central Powers (enemies of Britain); Indian Muslims in moral crisis. Phase 2 (triggers for Khilafat Movement
1919-24): (5) 1917: Balfour Declaration (Britain promises Jewish homeland in Palestine = Arab betrayal). (6) 1920: Treaty of
Sevres (Arab regions -> British + French colonies; Smyrna to Greece; Khalifa loses Hagia Sophia; British promises during war =
broken). This arc = why ML1906 was anti-British enough by 1916 to sign the Lucknow Pact + by 1919-24 to join the Khilafat
Movement.

-> Gandhi arrives in India (Jan 1915) -> Tilak's Home Rule League (Apr 1916) = 2, 3, 1. 2005: Proponent of Fabianism as a
movement = Annie Besant (NOT A.O. Hume / NOT Michael Madhusudhan Dutt / NOT R Palme Dutt). 2013: Annie Besant — (1)
responsible for starting Home Rule Movement (CORRECT) + (2) founder of Theosophical Society (INCORRECT — Henry Steel
Olcott + Helena Blavatsky founded Theosophical Society in 1875 in USA; Besant later became its head) + (3) President of INC
(CORRECT — 1917 Calcutta session) = 1 and 3 only. 2018: changed its name to Swarajya Sabha in 1920 = All India Home Rule
League (NOT Hindu Mahasabha / NOT South Indian Liberal Federation / NOT Servants of India Society).

sections.title: The Montagu Statement, 1917 — Why Did Britain Move at All?
Provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919
Dyarchy at the Provincial Level — The Most Debated Feature

phases.label: CHRONOLOGY: MONTAGU STATEMENT TO GOI ACT 1919 (1916–1935)

events.label: Lucknow Pact (1916) — INC + ML1906 joint demands: (i) continue Separate Electorates; (ii) expand councils + elected majority; (iii) at least 50% Indians in VEC; (iv) franchise as broad as possible + direct elections; (v) Dominion Status implied; ML1906 agrees to give up R2Vote in unreserved seats; INC accepts Separate Electorates; creates political context pushing British toward reform

Montagu Statement / August Declaration (20 August 1917) — Edwin Montagu (SoS for India) in House of Commons: declares 'gradual development of self-governing institutions with view to progressive realisation of responsible government in India within the British Empire'; KEY WORDS: 'gradual' + 'progressive' (= slow, controlled movement toward self-governance on British terms; demand acknowledged but timeline firmly in British hands); GOI 1919 = conceived as 1st step toward this; deployed by British as DnR tactic to split Moderates from Extremists on Passive Resistance question; Extremists propose Passive Resistance; Moderates + Besant side against it

Montagu visits India personally (unusual step for SoS) — tours various provinces to assess conditions on ground; co-authors joint report with Viceroy Chelmsford16-21 Montagu-Chelmsford Report (1918) — joint document; blueprint for GOI Act 1919; Prelims 2003: Indian Liberal Federation (Moderates who left INC after condemning this Report); Prelims 2004: MC Report -> Act 1919 lineage; Prelims 2015: Act 1919 defined Centre-Province jurisdiction

GOI Act 1919 (Government of India Act 1919 / Montford Reforms / Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) — NOTE: Report (1918) = recommendation; Montford Reforms = popular name for entire package; GOI Act 1919 = actual law passed by British Parliament; CONTEXT: WW1 (1914-19) + Allied propaganda for democracy + self-determination; large Indian war contribution; Ghadar Movement 1913-15 + HRL Movement 1916-18 + Lucknow Pact 1916 = political pressure

BICAMERAL LEGISLATURE AT CENTRE — 1st time: Central Legislative Assembly (CLA, lower house, ~145 members, life 3 years) + Council of States (CoS, upper house, ~60 members, life 5 years); ELECTED MAJORITY in CLA + CoS + all Provincial Legislative Assemblies (PLAs) for 1st time; DIRECT ELECTIONS in CLA, CoS + PLAs for 1st time (CoS also had direct elections with higher income criteria; unusual for upper house); ADJOURNMENT MOTIONS allowed for 1st time; ONLY for British India (NOT whole of India; GOI Act 1935 extended framework to include Princely States)

PROVINCIAL LEVEL — Provincial Legislative Assemblies (PLAs): unicameral; elected majority (1st time); direct elections (1st time); life 3 years; Under ICA1909: PLCs had non-official majority but most non-officials = nominated not elected

NARENDRA MANDAL (CHAMBER OF PRINCES) — advisory body for Princely States; key recommendation of MC Report (1918); constituted by Royal Proclamation in 1921 (NOT by GOI Act 1919 itself; Act provided framework; Proclamation brought it to life); reward to Princes for support during WW1; no legislative power = purely advisory; later venue where Mountbatten in 1947 addressed Princes urging them to sign Instrument of Accession

ELECTIONS + RIGHT TO VOTE — R2Vote linked to strict income/property criteria as in ICA1909; NO Universal Adult Franchise; Lucknow Pact 1916 had demanded franchise as broad as possible = NOT conceded; Women's Franchise: Act did NOT directly grant women R2Vote; only EMPOWERED Provincial Legislative Assemblies to pass resolutions removing sex disqualification; women admitted to vote had to meet EXACT SAME strict property qualifications as men = less than 1% of women actually qualified; provision allowing voting based on husband's property + lower income criteria for women came ONLY with GOI Act 1935

SEPARATE ELECTORATES — WATERTIGHT (1st watertight roll): Separate electorates for Muslims continued from ICA1909 BUT critical change: under ICA1909 Muslims could vote in Muslim reserved seats + ALSO in unreserved seats (double advantage); under GOI 1919 Muslims could NO LONGER vote in unreserved seats = watertight segregation; origin: Lucknow Pact 1916 (ML agrees to give up R2Vote in unreserved seats; INC accepts Separate Electorates); British eagerly seized on communal division logic = dovetailed perfectly with DnR; GOI 1919 extended same communal separation further to Sikhs + Anglo-Indians + Christians (all with watertight rolls; members can vote ONLY in respective reserved constituencies not in unreserved seats); Depressed Classes: reservation of NOMINATED seats (not elected seats) in all legislatures; nominated share inherently small since legislature now has elected majority

DIVISION OF SUBJECTS BETWEEN CENTRE + PROVINCES — 1st time; NOT true federal distribution (no formal lists = no 7th Schedule of COI1950; Centre can still take away any subject from province or legislate upon it at will); PROVINCIAL BUDGET separated from Central Budget for 1st time; LR (Land Revenue) -> Provinces; Customs + Income Tax -> Centre; allocation of seats in CLA + CoS to Provinces = by perceived importance (NOT by population; Punjab weighted for military importance; Bombay weighted for commercial importance)

DYARCHY AT PROVINCIAL LEVEL — dual rule; all provincial subjects split into 2 categories: (i) RESERVED SUBJECTS: politically important (Law + Order = Police; Administration of Justice; Finance; Land Revenue; Irrigation; Control over Officials); legislative + executive powers with Governor + his officials; NO accountability to PLA on reserved subjects; ministers handling reserved subjects NOT responsible to PLA; WHY IRRIGATION RESERVED: from 1850s onwards canals built through FDI by British investors; keeping Irrigation under Governor's grip = shield returns from Indian elected ministers (same logic as 5% guaranteed FDI interest on railways); ASYMMETRY: Land Revenue Reserved but Agriculture Transferred = British kept lever generating revenue; Indian ministers inherited lever generating peasant complaints = 'Reserving the Spoils, Transferring the Tension'; (ii) TRANSFERRED SUBJECTS: less politically sensitive (health, education, local government, agriculture); legislative power with PLA; administered by ministers responsible to PLA; PROBLEMS in practice: Indian ministers received 'soft' subjects but NO control over finance or officials; without money + without control over bureaucracy -> cannot effectively govern even transferred subjects; when they fail to deliver -> unpopular with public (exactly as British designed); goal: hurt legitimacy of Indian ministers + demonstrate Indians cannot govern -> delay demand for full responsible government; in case of failure of constitutional machinery: Governor can take over executive + legislative powers over transferred subjects too

VEC (VICEROY'S EXECUTIVE COUNCIL) — GOI Act 1919 removes old statutory maximum limit on number of ordinary members; CONVENTION (not statutory mandate): VEC = Viceroy + CIC + 6 ordinary members = 8 total; 3 of the 6 ordinary members = Indians (convention = political/administrative practice, not hard legal requirement); Lucknow Pact 1916 demanded 50% Indians in VEC; 3/8 = demand UNMET

VICEROY POWERS — NO RESPONSIBLE GOVT AT CENTRE (VEC NOT accountable to legislature; no No Confidence Motion); retained powers: (i) VETO over all bills; (ii) power to APPROVE REJECTED BILLS (Viceroy can pass bills rejected by CLA/CoS); (iii) ORDINANCE POWER (valid 6 months); (iv) POWER TO RESTORE CUTS IN GRANTS (override budget votes); (v) 75% OF BUDGET ITEMS NON-VOTABLE (legislature can discuss but real financial control stays with executive); 'Taxation Without Representation' continuing even after 1919

ICS REFORM — GOI Act 1919 mandates ICS examination held SIMULTANEOUSLY IN INDIA alongside England; 1st India-based exam held 1922; Section 96C mandates Public Service Commission for India; Commission established 1926 with Ross Barker as 1st Chairman (direct institutional ancestor of modern UPSC); gradual increase to 33% Indians in senior civil service positions mandated; GOI 1919 divided subjects between Centre + Provinces -> ICS split into All India Services (AIS) + Central Civil Services; structure of AIS + Central Services today = essentially this 1919 structure continued + modified by Constitution

MONTAGU STATEMENT REPORT-ACT DISTINCTION: Montagu-Chelmsford Report (1918) = RECOMMENDATION; Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms / Montford Reforms = popular name for ENTIRE PACKAGE; GOI Act 1919 = ACTUAL LAW; all three used loosely in UPSC; precise answer when asked which is the 'law' = GOI Act 1919

Extremists re-enter INC (1916 Lucknow Session); Gandhi takes over INM (Nagpur Session 1920); GOI 1919's Dyarchy = immediate provocation for Rowlatt Acts 1919 -> Jallianwala Bagh 1919 -> Non-Cooperation Movement 1920-22

Rowlatt Acts 1919 (Anarchical + Revolutionary Crimes Act 1919) — continuation of Defence of India Act 1915 emergency powers even post-WW1; triggers mass anger -> Gandhi's 1st pan-India Satyagraha; Jallianwala Bagh Massacre April 13, 1919 (under Dyer)
Narendra Mandal / Chamber of Princes formally constituted by Royal Proclamation (1921) — recommended by MC Report 1918; GOI Act 1919 provided framework
1st ICS examination held in India (1922) — mandated by GOI Act 1919
Gaya Session 1922 — 'End or Mend Councils' Resolution of Pro-Changers (link: adjournment motions allowed for 1st time under GOI Act 1919 = lever Pro-Changers wanted to use)
Public Service Commission for India established (1926) — Ross Barker as 1st Chairman; mandated by Section 96C of GOI Act 1919; direct ancestor of modern UPSC
Simon Commission appointed 1927 (under Baldwin govt) — 7 British members + 0 Indians; review of GOI Act 1919; triggers 'Simon Go Back' agitation; leads to Motilal Nehru Report (1928)

Motilal Nehru Report (August 1928) — 1st formal use of phrase 'Dominion Status' (implied by Lucknow Pact 1916 but first time explicit); also demands Universal Adult Franchise (formal UAF demand = Motilal Nehru Report 1928)

GOI Act 1935 — next major reform; extends framework to include Princely States in all-India federation; Provincial Autonomy; provision allowing women to vote based on husband's property + lower income criteria

sections.title: Who Was in South Africa — and Why Did It Matter?
How Did Gandhiji End Up Staying?
What Started the Struggle? The Two Trigger Laws
The Poll Tax Campaign and the Final Countdown (1913)

events.label: Indentured labour from India accelerates after 1890 — white settlers in South Africa recruit cheap labour; Indians in South Africa = two groups: (i) Memon Muslims (voluntary traders + merchants); (ii) Indentured labourers (brought under bond contracts = tied labour; arrived in large numbers post-1890 to work on sugar plantations + in mines; indentured labour = step above slavery in name only; labourer signed contract usually without fully understanding it = binding him to employer for fixed term under conditions he cannot easily escape)
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi arrives in South Africa (1893) — young barrister; hired to handle commercial legal case for Memon Muslim merchant; planned to stay briefly + return to India

PIETERMARITZBURG INCIDENT (1893) — Gandhi ejected from first-class railway compartment solely for being Indian despite holding valid ticket; humiliation on cold station platform = his political catalyst; moment he resolves to fight racial discrimination rather than quietly endure it

Indian community persuades Gandhi to stay — community was leaderless + without any educated advocate who understood both law + their grievances; Gandhi = only person who could fight for them within the system; what began as short visit stretched into 22 years

Franchise Amendment Bill, Natal (1894) — seeks to disenfranchise Indians: strip them of Right to Vote; some Indians had earlier qualified for vote based on wealth criterion (property above certain value); 1894 Bill closes that door entirely on purely racial grounds; form of 'Taxation Without Representation' (Indians paid taxes + contributed to economy but denied any say in who governed them; parallel: American colonists' grievance against Britain 1776)

Natal Indian Congress (NIC) founded by Gandhi (1894) — modelled on Indian National Congress back home; gives Indian community formal organised political voice; EXAM TRAP: NIC (1894) + INC (1885) = SEPARATE organisations founded in different countries for different contexts; Gandhi founded NIC; he did NOT found INC

Immigration Law Amendment Bill, Natal (1895) — gave Indian indentured labourers a brutal choice on completion of work contract: (i) leave South Africa; (ii) re-indenture for 2 more years; (iii) if chose neither = pay POLL TAX of £3 per year (significant sum for labourer earning bare subsistence wages); tax NOT about revenue = making Indian settlement economically unsustainable

PHASE 1 — CONSTITUTIONAL STRUGGLE (1896-1906): Gandhi's early response entirely within the law; organised petitions + prayers + public meetings; founded NIC (1894); launched Indian Opinion newspaper; approach = Moderate, respectful + constitutional: appeal to conscience of rulers + expose injustice through argument + trust reason would prevail; ECHOES: exactly what Moderate leaders of INC were doing in India at same time (petitions, prayers + press); Gandhi = Moderate in South Africa before he became something far more

Phoenix Settlement established near Durban (1904) — inspired by John Ruskin's Unto This Last; Gandhiji establishes communal settlement; residents live + work together; practice self-reliance + simple living; Indian Opinion newspaper printed here; Phoenix Settlement = Gandhi's 1st communal living experiment = philosophical precursor to Tolstoy Farm (1910) + to his ashrams in India (link Ruskin's influence on Gandhian ideology); PROGRESSION: Phoenix Settlement 1904 -> Tolstoy Farm 1910 -> Sabarmati/Sevagram in India (each building on the last)

Asiatic Law Amendment Act 1906 (Transvaal) / 'BLACK ACT' — required every Indian to carry Registration Certificate (RC) at all times; failure to produce on demand = fine + imprisonment + deportation; RC = physical identity card to be produced on demand to any authority with deportation as penalty for not carrying it = instrument of RACIAL SURVEILLANCE

SATYAGRAHA BORN (1906) — Gandhi concludes by 1906 that constitutional methods alone not enough; government unmoved by petitions; crucible in which Satyagraha is born; Satyagraha = ACTIVE, DISCIPLINED RESISTANCE grounded in specific personal code; true Satyagrahi must be: (i) Truthful (word, action + intention); (ii) Non-violent (absolutely, even under provocation); (iii) Fearless (willing to face arrest, imprisonment, physical suffering); (iv) Ready to accept suffering (not to inflict it); (v) Loving toward the wrongdoer (hate has no place); standard: NOT 'protest when convenient' = demands complete transformation of individual; undisciplined Satyagrahi = contradiction in terms; EXAM TRAP: Satyagraha first developed + deployed in SOUTH AFRICA (NOT India); Gandhi brings it to India only after 1915; Champaran Satyagraha 1917 = 1st use of Satyagraha on Indian soil

SATYAGRAHA AGAINST REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES (1906-1914) — govt makes offer: if Indians voluntarily register, law will be withdrawn; Gandhi (remarkable act of good faith) is FIRST TO REGISTER; leads by example expecting govt to keep word; GOVT BREAKS PROMISE; Gandhi organises BONFIRE OF REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES (powerful public act of defiance); then leads Indians in COURTING ARREST (= 'Jail Bharo'); struggle conducted through PASSIVE RESISTANCE ASSOCIATION

Transvaal Immigration Restriction Act 1907 — bars Indians from moving freely between provinces (from Cape Province, Natal, or Orange Free State into Transvaal); Indians physically caged within provincial boundaries; Gandhi's response: Indians deliberately cross provincial boundaries illegally + court arrest + refuse bail; Indians in Transvaal engage in hawking without licence (minor illegal act deliberately committed to fill jails)
Gandhi jailed (1908) — prisons overflowing; strategy: make enforcement so costly that govt forced to negotiate

Tolstoy Farm established near Johannesburg (1910) — communal settlement for Satyagrahis + their families during passive phases of struggle; named after Russian writer Leo Tolstoy (ideas on non-violent resistance influenced Gandhi); part ashram + part training ground; residents taught self-reliance (farming + crafts + basic trades); philosophical seed of what later became Gandhi's ashram model in India; if truly fearless + self-sufficient = govt has fewer levers to use against you; PROGRESSION: Phoenix 1904 -> Tolstoy Farm 1910 -> Sabarmati/Sevagram

Gokhale visits South Africa (1912) — Gopal Krishna Gokhale = Gandhi's political mentor + one of most respected Moderate leaders of INC; South African govt impressed by his stature + promises Gokhale discriminatory laws will be repealed; PROMISE BROKEN after Gokhale leaves; Gokhale's strategic advice: focus movement on 2 specific + emotionally resonant demands: (i) abolition of Poll Tax (under Immigration Law); (ii) abolition of RC requirement (under Black Act); these 2 issues most capable of mobilising mass participation; movement needs issue people feel viscerally = these 2 hit every Indian household

SC judgement invalidates non-Christian marriages (1913) — South African Supreme Court declares ONLY CHRISTIAN MARRIAGES legally valid; marriages conducted under Hindu, Muslim or other rites NOT recognised by law = Indian wives legally not wives + their children potentially illegitimate; community outraged; overnight struggle = no longer just about taxes + documents but about FAMILY + DIGNITY +

POLL TAX CAMPAIGN (1913) — movement reaches turning point; Poll Tax Campaign = vehicle through which struggle finally acquires MASS CHARACTER; till now largely led by educated Indians (lawyers, merchants, community leaders); poll tax hits indentured labourer DIRECTLY = working class joins

FINAL STRUGGLE EVENTS (1913): (i) Illegal crossing into Transvaal (Indians defy Transvaal Immigration Restriction Act openly); (ii) KASTURBA GANDHI arrested (galvanises entire Indian worker community); (iii) Gandhi organises march of 2,000 workers into Transvaal; arrested marchers rejoin after release swelling numbers; (iv) ALL Indian workers across province go on STRIKE; economic disruption impossible to ignore; (v) Gokhale travels across India building Indian public opinion + political pressure; (vi) VICEROY HARDINGE10-16 publicly condemns South African govt's treatment of Indians (unprecedented diplomatic pressure from within British Empire itself); RESULT: South African govt comes to table; talks held with Gandhi

OUTCOME — Gandhi wins on all 3 demands (1914): (i) POLL TAX ABOLISHED (£3 annual penalty on ex-indentured labourers who chose to stay = removed); (ii) REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES dropped (requirement under Black Act); (iii) INDIAN MARRIAGES VALIDATED (marriages under Hindu + Muslim + other rites given legal recognition); these were NOT small victories; each one had direct concrete impact on thousands of Indian families; Prelims 2019: Mahatma Gandhi was instrumental in abolition of system of Indentured Labour

Gandhi returns to India (January 1915) — NOT as defeated petitioner but as leader who had won; South African years: taught Gandhi that mass civil disobedience works; that ordinary people (not just educated elites) can be soldiers of non-violent movement; that govt's most powerful weapon (the law) can be neutralised when people voluntarily accept punishment without fear; all of this applied in India: Champaran 1917 + Kheda + Dandi + beyond; laboratories of Natal + Transvaal produced experiments deployed across India

Champaran Satyagraha (1917) — 1st use of Satyagraha on INDIAN SOIL (indigo cultivators of Bihar; Tinkathia System of forced indigo cultivation; Gandhi wins: Champaran Agrarian Act 1918 ends Tinkathia System)

anchors: Progression of Communal Living Experiments: Phoenix Settlement (1904, near Durban): inspired by John Ruskin's Unto This
Last; 1st communal living experiment; self-reliance + simple living; Indian Opinion printed here. Tolstoy Farm (1910, near
Johannesburg): named after Leo Tolstoy; residential base for Satyagrahis + families during passive phases of struggle; farming +
crafts + basic trades; if fearless + self-sufficient = fewer govt levers to use against you. Sabarmati Ashram (1915, Ahmedabad) +
Sevagram Ashram (1936, Wardha): same principles in India. Philosophical arc: Phoenix -> Tolstoy Farm -> Sabarmati/Sevagram;
each building on the last. Link forward: Champaran Satyagraha (1917) = 1st Satyagraha on Indian soil; Kheda + Non-Cooperation
+ CDM + Quit India follow.
What South Africa Taught Gandhi — 6 Lessons Applied in India: (1) Mass civil disobedience works against colonial
administration. (2) Ordinary people (not just educated elites) can be the soldiers of a non-violent movement. (3) The government's
most powerful weapon (the law) can be neutralised when people voluntarily accept its punishment without fear. (4) A movement
needs an issue people feel viscerally — like poll tax or family dignity — to achieve mass participation. (5) Communal living +
self-sufficiency strengthens activists against economic pressure. (6) Diplomatic pressure within the imperial framework (Viceroy
Hardinge's condemnation 1913) can be part of the strategy. All 6 applied in India: Champaran (issue felt viscerally: Tinkathia),
Kheda (LR + debt), Dandi (salt tax), NCM + CDM (mass civil disobedience across India).
n UPSC Exam Traps — CH 35: TRAP 1: Natal Indian Congress (NIC, founded 1894 by Gandhi in South Africa) vs Indian National
Congress (INC, founded 1885 at Bombay by A.O. Hume + others). Gandhi founded NIC; he did NOT found INC. TRAP 2:
Satyagraha was first developed + deployed in SOUTH AFRICA (1906), NOT in India. Gandhi brings it to India only after 1915.
Champaran Satyagraha (1917) = 1st use on Indian soil. TRAP 3: Prelims 2019 — Mahatma Gandhi was instrumental in abolition of
system of Indentured Labour (in South Africa via Poll Tax Campaign 1913-14 wins + globally by advocating abolition of indentured
labour system after returning to India). TRAP 4: Phoenix Settlement (1904) is near Durban (Natal province). Tolstoy Farm (1910) is
near Johannesburg (Transvaal). Different provinces, different purposes.

tables.title: INTELLECTUAL INFLUENCES — CHRONOLOGICAL ANCHOR
lines: 1849 Henry David Thoreau — Civil Disobedience (1849): argues when a law is unjust the citizen has MORAL
DUTY to disobey it; obedience to unjust State = itself a moral failure; Gandhi finds Western intellectual
articulation of what he already practises in South Africa; term 'Civil Disobedience' enters Gandhi's political
vocabulary through Thoreau; becomes one of 2 pillars of Satyagraha alongside Non-Cooperation
1862 John Ruskin — Unto This Last (1862): Gandhi says 'this book transformed my life'; Ruskin argues: (i) good
of individual = good of all; (ii) manual labour (farmer, barber, craftsman) has same dignity as intellectual
labour; (iii) life of labour truly worth living; Gandhi reads it on train in South Africa -> immediately founds
Phoenix Settlement 1904 near Durban (cooperative community based on Ruskin's principles of shared
manual work + simple living); Prelims 2011: link between Ruskin's Unto This Last + Gandhi
1875 Swami Dayanand Saraswati + Arya Samaj 1875 — makes same civilisational argument: Indians enslaved
themselves by abandoning their own heritage; Gandhi extends Dayanand's cultural argument into full
economic programme; DnR (cultural nationalism) -> Gandhi takes it further than predecessors
1882 Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay — Anandamath 1882 (Bande Mataram); cultural nationalism building in
India; Gandhi stands in this tradition
1894 Leo Tolstoy — The Kingdom of God is Within You (1894): argues State + military + Church all rest on
organised violence; morally self-regulated individual needs none of them; non-resistance to evil by force +
moral self-regulation as only legitimate basis for society; Gandhi corresponds directly with Tolstoy; names
Tolstoy Farm 1910 @ Johannesburg after him (Satyagraha training commune = prototype for later Indian
ashrams)
1897 Swami Vivekananda + Ramakrishna Mission 1897 — Constructive Work tradition; Constructive Work as
nation-building lineage: Ramakrishna Mission 1897 -> Arya Samaj DAV schools -> Tagore's Shantiniketan
1901 -> Tilak's Constructive Swadeshi -> Gandhi's Tolstoy Farm 1910 + Sabarmati 1917; Gandhi absorbs
entire tradition + makes CW structural middle phase of every movement; Vivekananda's 'strength is life,
weakness is death' = fearlessness; both Gandhi + Vivekananda agree on fearlessness
Timeless Bhagavad Gita — Nishkama Karma: action performed as duty WITHOUT ATTACHMENT to its result;
Gandhi's personal moral compass throughout his life; spiritual grounding to act decisively in politics while
remaining inwardly detached from power, fame, personal gain; calls Gita his 'spiritual dictionary' + reads
from it every day
Timeless Sermon on the Mount (New Testament) — Christ's teaching of non-violence: turning the other cheek +
loving one's enemy + overcoming evil with good; reinforces conviction that non-violence = NOT passive
weakness but highest form of moral courage; Gita + Sermon on the Mount = twin spiritual pillars of Ahimsa;
Gandhi draws simultaneously from Hindu + Christian + Western secular traditions = not accidental; central
to claim that Satyagraha = universal moral method (not Hindu religious one); makes him credible across
civilisational divides
1901 Rabindranath Tagore's Shantiniketan 1901 — CW tradition; Tagore shares Gandhi's love of Indian
civilisation but fears mass religious nationalism could slide into dangerous intolerance; Gandhi's response:
you cannot raise consciousness before you first mobilise the people
SOURCE INFLUENCE ON GANDHI
1909 Hind Swaraj (1909) — written during 10-day sea voyage; structured as dialogue between 'Reader' and
'Editor'; most authentic source of Gandhi's ideology; Gandhi's unconventional positions: (i) Western
civilisation = Godless, driven only by profit; (ii) Indians responsible for own enslavement (adopted Western
capitalism; doctors, lawyers, railways = instruments of alien economic system looting India from within); (iii)
India = nation since ancient times; civilisation (not race or language) = source of unity; (iv) Swaraj = not
merely national independence but every individual should be his own master = Enlightened Anarchism;
Prelims anchor: published 1909 in Gujarati; English translation 1910

anchors: Core Gandhian Ideology — Summary: (1) CIVILISATION: India = nation since ancient times; civilisation (not race/language) =
source of unity; Western civilisation = Godless, only profit motive; Gandhi = Cultural Nationalist (tradition: Dayanand, Vivekananda,
Bankim). (2) STATE: Ideal = stateless society (Enlightened Anarchism); same end-goal as Marx but irreconcilably different path;
interim = parliamentary democracy with weak State + Village Republics (direct democracy); Gram Sabha = Article 243 of COI =
Gandhi's most concrete institutional legacy. (3) ECONOMY: Reject IR + Western capitalism; return to village self-sufficiency;
Trusteeship over expropriation; voluntary land redistribution (-> Bhoodan Movement, Vinoba Bhave, Telangana, 1951). (4)
METHOD: Satyagraha = NC + CD + CW + Non-Violence + Morality; Rising Tempo; Controlled mass movement; S-CW-S; never
exploit weakness of opponent; hate breach of promise. (5) STRATEGY: Ambiguous Swaraj to maximise support across plural
India; inclusive = all sections on streets. (6) INTELLECTUAL ROOTS: Ruskin (dignity of labour; Phoenix Settlement 1904), Tolstoy
(non-resistance; Tolstoy Farm 1910), Thoreau (CD as moral duty), Gita (Nishkama Karma), Sermon on the Mount (love the
enemy). Publications phase arc: Indian Opinion (SA, 1903) -> Young India + Navajivan (1919-1932) -> Harijan series (1933-1948).

arrest = Regulation XXV of 1827 (no trial); 1932 arrest = post-RTC; emergency ordinances; BOTH led to Yerwada Jail but different
