phases.label: CHRONOLOGY: THREE PILOT PROJECTS + ROWLATT + NCM + PASSIVE PHASE (1915–1927)

events.label: Gandhi (MG) arrives in India — does NOT rush into mass politics; founds Satyagraha Ashram @ Kochrab (1915); travels + listens + understands the country for nearly 2 years before acting

Satyagraha Ashram relocated to Sabarmati, Ahmedabad (1917); BHU founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya (1916); Awadh Kisan Sabha context: Baba Ramchandra organising Awadh peasants from ~1918-19 against taluqdars (illegal evictions, nazrana, begar)

INC Lucknow Session 1916 — Rajkumar Shukla (peasant leader from Bihar) meets MG + requests visit to Champaran; grievance = Tinkathia System (ryots forced to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land under contracts with British planters); Tinkathia = 3 kathas out of every 20 must be under indigo cultivation; background: after Indigo Revolt 1859-60 in Bengal, indigo plantation shifted to Bihar by 1863; German synthetic dyes popular after 1895 eating into indigo market globally; but during WW1 those dyes unavailable -> planters pushed Tinkathia harder than ever

CHAMPARAN SATYAGRAHA 1917 — MG arrives in Champaran; British authorities order him to leave the district; HE REFUSES = act of CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE (1st civil disobedience on Indian soil; disobeys direct official order; accepts legal consequence; Prelims 2007: first Indian Satyagraha site = Champaran; Prelims 2018: Champaran significance = 1st civil disobedience on Indian soil); govt (uncertain how to handle) makes MG head of Inquiry Committee; MG systematically documents exploitation; convinces administration to abolish Tinkathia System; Champaran Agricultural Act 1918 passed; leaders who accompanied MG: Rajendra Prasad + J.B. Kripalani (teacher by profession; Prelims 2008) + Mazhar-ul-Haq; hallmark = CD; outcome = arbitration method -> legislation

AHMEDABAD MILL STRIKE 1918 — MG invited by Anasuya Sarabhai (social worker); her brother Ambalal Sarabhai heads Ahmedabad Mill Owners' Association; grievance: during WW1 Ahmedabad hit by plague deaths; mill owners paid Plague Bonus to compensate workers for epidemic risk; discontinued once worst plague over; WW1 inflation + Spanish Flu crushing purchasing power of workers; workers demand 50% wage increase; mill owners refuse to negotiate until all strikes end; MG demands 35% wage increase; begins FAST UNTO DEATH directed as moral pressure at mill owners (1st hunger strike; also makes it difficult for workers to abandon strike); Arbitration Board set up; settles on 27.5% wage increase; hallmarks = 1st hunger strike + arbitration method; impact: lays foundation of working-class movement in Ahmedabad -> Textile Labour Association (TLA) formed 1920 (MG founds TLA; Prelims 2009: TLA founder = MG); AITUC also formed 1920 by Lala Lajpat Rai (1st all-India organisation of working class); CPI set up in Tashkent 1920 under M.N. Roy (reconstituted inside India 1925); WC finding political voice

KHEDA SATYAGRAHA 1918 — grievance: under Ryotwari system, farmers in Kheda district Gujarat entitled by law to REMISSION of LR if crop yield below 1/4 of normal output; 1918 harvest failed; plague compounded misery; govt refuses legally mandated remission (needs money for WW1); MG asks peasants to WITHHOLD PAYMENT of LR; govt eventually agrees not to confiscate property of those who cannot pay = concedes principle that only those who can pay must; hallmark = 1st NON-COOPERATION / No Revenue Movement; WHY NOT CD: goal was NOT Swaraj; ryots not refusing tax permanently; quarrel = not with tax itself but with govt's refusal to apply its own legal provisions correctly; law was on ryots' side; therefore Non-Cooperation: withholding cooperation with unjust action without challenging colonial sovereignty as such; IMPACT: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel becomes follower of MG through this movement (Kheda = Patel's 1st experience of organised mass action)

Viceroy's War Conference Delhi 1918 — MG actively supports resolution to recruit Indians for WW1 (unlike many leaders who hold back); reasoning: wartime help will be repaid with self-government; therefore Rowlatt Act (next) feels to MG like a broken promise

ROWLATT ACT Feb 1919 — ILC passes what becomes Rowlatt Act = Anarchical + Revolutionary Crimes Act 1919; based on recommendations of Sedition Committee chaired by Justice S.A.T. Rowlatt; TWO bills produced + passed together as ONE Act; extends emergency powers of Defence of India Act 1915 into PEACETIME (DOIA 1915 was for duration of WW1 only; Rowlatt Act keeps draconian powers permanently: detention without trial + suppress press freedom + trial without jury); passed despite UNANIMOUS OPPOSITION from every single Indian member of ILC; every Indian member votes against it; passes anyway (official majority); Indian members who protested: Jinnah + Madan Mohan Malaviya + Mazharul Haq; Prelims 2012: Rowlatt Act aim = imprisonment without trial + summary procedure; Prelims 2015: based on Sedition Committee report; WWI inflation context: Spanish Flu killed ~12 million Indians; British alarmed by October Revolution 1917 in Russia + CPI Tashkent 1920; GOI Act 1919 being framed at very same time
events.full: ROWLATT ACT Feb 1919 — ILC passes what becomes Rowlatt Act = Anarchical + Revolutionary Crimes Act 1919 (Prelims 1996: Anarchical + Revolutionary Crimes Act 1919 = Rowlatt Act); based on recommendations of Sedition Committee chaired by Justice S.A.T. Rowlatt; TWO bills produced + passed together as ONE Act; extends emergency powers of Defence of India Act 1915 into PEACETIME (DOIA 1915 was for duration of WW1 only; Rowlatt Act keeps draconian powers permanently: detention without trial + suppress press freedom + trial without jury); passed despite UNANIMOUS OPPOSITION from every single Indian member of ILC; every Indian member votes against it; passes anyway (official majority); Indian members who protested: Jinnah + Madan Mohan Malaviya + Mazharul Haq; Prelims 2012: Rowlatt Act aim = imprisonment without trial + summary procedure; Prelims 2015: based on Sedition Committee report; WWI inflation context: Spanish Flu killed ~12 million Indians; British alarmed by October Revolution 1917 in Russia + CPI Tashkent 1920; GOI Act 1919 being framed at very same time

events.label: ROWLATT SATYAGRAHA April 1919 — MG alone calls nationwide non-violent strike (NOT INC; MG had not yet taken control of INC); 1st mass strike + 1st all-India movement in Indian history; Prelims 1999: Gandhi's 1st all-India venture = Rowlatt Satyagraha; WHY MG REACTED STRONGLY: breach of promise (Montague Statement 1917 promised gradual self-govt; Rowlatt Act = British want to retain most coercive wartime powers permanently); MG arrested @ Palwal on train en route to Delhi (Punjab govt orders); news of arrest -> widespread violence especially in Punjab where INC leaders Dr Satya Pal + Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew had already been arrested; Lt Governor O'Dwyer + General Dyer impose martial law in Punjab with O'Dwyer's approval; public gatherings banned

JALLIANWALA BAGH MASSACRE — 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi); people gathered PEACEFULLY @ enclosed garden @ Amritsar to celebrate Baisakhi + protest arrest of leaders; WITHOUT WARNING General Dyer orders troops to open fire; firing continues 10 minutes; exits narrow + blocked = people trapped; Official British count: 379 dead; INC count: 1,500 dead; Hunter Committee set up Oct 1919 (report 1920): finds Dyer guilty ONLY of being overly zealous in Empire's service; no meaningful punishment; whitewashing = 2nd wound after massacre itself; Prelims 2004: Tagore returned knighthood = protest against Jallianwala Bagh; Mahants of Golden Temple actually HONOURED General Dyer (pro-British as in Ghadar Movement 1913-15); O'Dwyer later assassinated by Udham Singh in London 1940 (retribution for his role); MG overwhelmed by violence -> WITHDRAWS Rowlatt Satyagraha; lesson: mass action without training + discipline = dangerous; Rowlatt Act repealed March 1922; Prelims 2008: Viceroy when Rowlatt Act passed = Chelmsford16-21

Khilafat Committee set up (March 1919) — Ali Brothers (Md Ali Jauhar + Shaukat Ali); NOT a ML1906 initiative; many individual ML members join it; demands: revise Treaty of Sevres + restore Khalifa's dignity + suitable territory + control over Muslim holy places + Arabs not under non-Muslim rule

Tilak dies (1 August 1920) — had opposed supporting a religious (Khilafat) goal fearing communalism later; B.C. Pal resigns from INC Aug 1920 (opposed personality-centric INC + opposed NV as absolute principle + disagreed with MG's definition of Swaraj as enlightened anarchy with Stateless society)

Allahabad Conference of Khilafat Committee (June 1920) — Khilafat Movement formally launched; call for boycott of titles + civil services + army + no-tax campaign; MG sees 'once in a hundred years' opportunity for Hindu-Muslim unity; convinces INC to launch NCM; Jinnah opposes extra-constitutional methods + resigns from Congress; Annie Besant opposes + resigns

Special Calcutta Session INC (September 1920) — President: Lala Lajpat Rai; INC formally launches NCM; 3 goals: (i) Swaraj; (ii) redressal of Punjab wrongs (Jallianwala Bagh); (iii) redressal of Khilafat wrongs; MG promises Swaraj in 1 year; programme for 1st year NC: [BOYCOTT]: leave titles + honours; boycott councils + courts + educational institutions + British goods; [SWADESHI]: panchayats as alternative dispute resolution + national education + Khadi (focus on hand-spun Khadi = deeper more rural form; different from Swadeshi 1905-11 which emphasised Indian industrial goods broadly); [CW]: picketing liquor shops + anti-untouchability campaign (breaks INC's 1886 rule of not raising social issues) + build H-M unity; Prelims 2025: NCM programme = Boycott of law-courts + Strict non-violence

Awadh Kisan Sabha (AKS) co-founded by Baba Ramchandra + Jawaharlal Nehru (October 1920) — Nehru visited villages of Pratapgarh + Pratapgarh in June 1920 seeing peasant conditions firsthand (radicalised him); Ramchandra built movement from soil up; Nehru gave it political shape + Congress connection; AKS adopted direct mass action: no-rent campaigns + nai-dhobi bandhs + taluqdar boycotts; quickly grew to 300+ branches; AKS joins NCM 1920-22; AKS turned violent 1921 (looting of bazaars + attacks on taluqdar houses = even INC leadership distanced itself)

INC NAGPUR SESSION December 1920 — President: C. VIJAYARAGHAVACHARIAR (EXAM TRAP: NOT C. Rajagopalachari; NOT M. Veeraraghavachariar/M. Vijayaraghavachariar who co-founded The Hindu 1878 + Madras Mahajana Sabha 1884); Vijayaraghavachariar = 'Lion of South India' / 'Hero of Salem'; Salem Riot Case 1882 = falsely implicated; fought from prison; won honourable acquittal; successfully SUED Secretary of State for India for damages (unheard of for an Indian at the time); known for fearless oratory + uncompromising nature; MG takes over INC at this session; INC goal changed: Swaraj by PEACEFUL MEANS (non-violent extra-constitutional mass struggle replacing constitutional methods); ORGANISATIONAL REFORMS: (i) CWC of 15 members (top executive body so movement continues if senior leaders arrested; AICC ~350 members; CWC = cabinet of 15; full session = 1000s of members); (ii) PCCs on LINGUISTIC LINES (link: Tilak's 1917 demand for linguistic reorganisation); (iii) membership fee 4 annas (1/16 of rupee = masses can join + organisation has funds); (iv) Hindi to be used as far as possible; (v) members of Princely States can join INC (though cannot launch movements in INC's name); MG shifts INC from CLASS politics to MASS politics; 2nd phase CDM would include: no-tax campaign (= CD) + resignation from govt services (= NC but far more powerful)
Tilak Swaraj Fund — MG raises Rs. 1 crore, oversubscribed; named in honour of Tilak (died Aug 1920); mass movement needs money + organisation

Eka Movement 1920-21 led by Madari Pasi (Extremist in method, not Gandhian) — merged into NCM; Akali Movement 1920-25 (people's control over Gurudwaras from British-loyal Mahants) supports NCM from 1921; Hindu-Muslim-Sikh unity during NCM

Gandhi-Reading Talks 1921 — Viceroy Reading21-26 seeks talks (one year of NC nearly over; British fear coming CDM; Reading had read MG's S-T-S pattern); talks FAIL: Reading wanted MG to publicly criticise Ali Brothers for speeches endorsing violence; MG REFUSES to be used as instrument of DnR; defeats DnR strategy by holding firm

Visit of Prince of Wales November 1921 — nationwide strikes by workers (working class responds with shutdowns + demonstrations); violence breaks out against Parsis + Christians + landlords who supported royal visit; MG grows alarmed; decides: no all-India CDM; CDM to be confined to Bardoli only via limited no-tax campaign (fears movement spiralling as Rowlatt Satyagraha had)

CHAURI CHAURA February 1922, UP — police fires on procession of satyagrahis killing 3; crowd retaliates: 22 policemen burned alive inside police station; MG's response: (i) WITHDRAWS NCM (INC stops calling on masses to do NC; only 'M' = mass movement withdrawn; institutional NC by boycotting 1923 council elections continues); (ii) suspends CDM planned for Bardoli; BARDOLI RESOLUTION 1922: training in non-violent Satyagraha through CW must PRECEDE any future movement; British sentences 170 to death for Chauri Chaura; Madan Mohan Malaviya fights cases in court; after appeals 19 hanged; Prelims 1998: NCM stopped 1922 = Chauri Chaura; Prelims 2025: Chauri Chaura accused legal defence = Madan Mohan Malaviya
Rowlatt Act repealed (March 1922); MG arrested; Great Trial 1922 (MG pleads guilty; Judge Broomfield; 6 years; Yerwada Jail Pune); released Feb 1924 after appendicitis operation

Gaya Session INC 1922 — Swarajists (Pro-Changers) led by C.R. Das + Motilal Nehru propose 'End or Mend Councils' at Gaya Session; resolution FAILS; Swarajists resign from official INC posts (NOT from INC membership); form Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party (Swaraj Party; 'Khilafat' added to get Muslim voters while Khilafat Movement 1920-24 still ongoing)

1923 elections to CLA — Swaraj Party contests; wins 42 of 104 elected seats; only 5% voted in 1920 CLA elections (council boycott succeeded; delivered opposite of democratic legitimacy British wanted); Motilal Nehru forms Nationalist Party parliamentary bloc by forging alliance with 'Independents' led by M.A. Jinnah; together they repeatedly outvote British govt, reject budget + force Viceroy to use 'certification' (veto) powers; Swarajists inside CLA: (i) Motilal demands new constitution in 1st session itself; (ii) demanded civil liberty + repeal of repressive laws; (iii) demanded concessions for Indian industry; (iv) used adjournment motions of GOI Act 1919 effectively; filled political void left by withdrawn NCM

Bengal Pact 1923 (C.R. Das) — Das needed Muslim members' support for blocking British govt legislations; pact proposes proportional representation in Bengal's local bodies + 60% reservation for Muslims in new govt jobs despite Muslims being in majority; Hindu groups oppose bitterly; Das sees it as only way to build political unity

Gandhi released Feb 1924 from jail; 1924 Belgaum Session = ONLY INC session ever presided over by MG himself; Gandhi-Das Pact 1924 recognises Swarajists as parliamentary wing of INC; MG praises Swarajists for good work in councils; Moplah Revolt 1921 (Malabar): began as peasant revolt (INC mobilised ryots on Khilafat issue with Ulamas; once INC leaders arrested movement became leaderless + turned communal with attacks on Hindu Janmies/landlords); post-NCM: communal riots 1922-24 (Tilak had predicted); H-M unity temporary
21-Day Fast for H-M Unity (1924) — Delhi; at house of Muhammad Ali; widespread H-M communal riots across India + Kohat riots

Responsivists emerge within Swaraj Party — want to abandon obstructionist strategy; cooperate with govt rather than obstruct; Lajpat Rai + Malaviya associated; accuse Motilal Nehru of being too pro-Muslim; some (N.C. Kelkar + Jayakar) actually join Executive Council in CP (= 'seat-hungry' = contrary to 'End or Mend' programme)

C.R. Das dies June 1925 — severe blow to Swaraj Party; Das had been principal architect + most credible face of Swarajists; leadership vacuum never fully recovered from; Bengal Pact collapses with him

Khilafat Movement ends 1924 — NOT by Indian decision; people of Turkey abolished the Khalifate + established secular republic under Mustafa Kemal Ataturk; movement built on foreign religious institution = vulnerable to decisions made in Ankara

Satyananda Stokes (Samuel Evans Stokes) — American settled in Himachal Pradesh; introduced American Red Delicious apple to Himalayan region (transformed rural economy of Shimla hills); ONLY AMERICAN ever arrested by British under sedition law for active part in NCM 1921; rare instance of Western individual participation in Gandhian agitational politics

Swaraj Party loses heavily in 1926 elections — lost almost all support from Muslim voters + leaders after communal riots of 1924 + C.R. Das's death; INC decides to withdraw from councils 1926 (all finally withdraw 1930 after Lahore Congress Resolution 1929 for Purna Swaraj)

Lala Lajpat Rai (1865-1928) leads massive protest against Simon Commission @ Lahore October 1928 — Commission had no Indian members; nationwide protests; Lajpat Rai severely beaten by police lathi-charges under Superintendent Scott's orders; reportedly declares: 'Every blow on my body is a nail in the coffin of the British Empire'; dies 17 November 1928 from injuries; DIRECT INSPIRATION: radicalises Bhagat Singh + Rajguru + Sukhdev -> assassinate J.P. Saunders (British police officer mistaken for Scott); chain of events -> Assembly Bomb Case 1929
Simon Commission announced 1927 (under Baldwin govt) — 7 British members + 0 Indians; review of GOI Act 1919; triggers 'Simon Go Back' agitation; ENDS the Passive Phase; opens next chapter of INM

Gandhian at Champaran = J.B. Kripalani. 2009: Ahmedabad TLA founder = Mahatma Gandhi (1920). 2012: Rowlatt Act aim =
imprisonment without trial + summary procedure. 2015: Rowlatt Act based on Sedition Committee report. 2025: NCM programme =
Boycott of law-courts + Strict non-violence (retention of titles = NOT a NCM demand). 2025: Chauri Chaura accused legal defence
= Madan Mohan Malaviya.

sections.title: How did Peasant Movements connect with INM?
Kisan Sabha Movement (1918) and Awadh Kisan Sabha (1920)
A Note on Peasant Movements and INC

events.label: Singh Sabha Movement (1880s) — raises issue of Sikh religious reform + control over Gurudwaras; origin of the Akali Movement (1920-25) which later emerges from it

Maharaja Ranjit Singh (RS01-39) — gives rich lands to Udasi Sikh Mahants; Mahants receive resources from Sikh Empire; over time become corrupt + live lives of luxury; British ally with them after annexation of Punjab 1849 Earlier Moplah uprisings (1840s + 1870s) — same agrarian grievance: heavy rents + arbitrary eviction by Hindu Jenmies (hereditary landowners); Muslim Mapilla tenants; same pattern repeats in 1921
events.full: 1801-39 1840, 1870s — Maharaja Ranjit Singh (RS01-39) — gives rich lands to Udasi Sikh Mahants; Mahants receive resources from Sikh Empire; over time become corrupt + live lives of luxury; British ally with them after annexation of Punjab 1849 Earlier Moplah uprisings (1840s + 1870s) — same agrarian grievance: heavy rents + arbitrary eviction by Hindu Jenmies (hereditary landowners); Muslim Mapilla tenants; same pattern repeats in 1921

events.label: British annexation of Punjab 1849 — British in collusion with Mahants vs Chadrites (reform-minded devotees); Mahants backed by British
Golden Temple issues Hukumnama (official religious decree) against Chadrites at behest of Mahants (1913) — at British backing; backdrop to later Akali anger

Home Rule League Movement (1916-18) — creates political awareness among masses; significantly inspires Kisan Sabha movement; peasants who heard language of rights + self-rule now begin to organise around own demands UP Kisan Sabha (UPKS) founded February 1918 — co-founded by Gauri Shankar Mishra + Indra Narayan Dwivedi + Madan Mohan Malaviya; Mishra + Dwivedi = operational organisers; Malaviya = senior political patron; Kisan Sabha leaders attend INC sessions (connection between peasant cause + national movement); PRELIMS 2005 TRAP: Jawaharlal Nehru NOT associated with UPKS 1918 (he engaged with Kisan Sabha movement only from June 1920 onwards when he visited Pratapgarh with Baba Ramchandra); Malaviya = Moderate -> does NOT support NCM -> therefore Baba Ramchandra (with Nehru's support) sets up Awadh Kisan Sabha 1920 for extra-constitutional struggle

Jallianwala Bagh massacre — Mahants of Golden Temple HONOUR General Dyer; triggers widespread outrage + protests by ordinary Sikh devotees; this = DIRECT TRIGGER for Akali Movement (when Mahants honour the man who massacred Sikhs at Amritsar, ordinary devotees decide they can no longer tolerate Mahant control)

SGPC (Shiromani Gurudwara Prabandhak Committee) formed 1920 — for organised management of Golden Temple; British give control of Golden Temple early (policy: appease moderates + suppress extremists among Akalis)
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) formed 1920 — for further organised protests against Mahants; for getting control of other Gurudwaras beyond Golden Temple

Awadh Kisan Sabha (AKS) co-founded October 1920 by Baba Ramchandra + Jawaharlal Nehru — peasant grievances in Awadh: illegal abwabs + nazrana (extra cesses by landlords) + bedakhli (eviction at will) + hari + begar (unpaid forced labour) + WWI-related inflation (prices rose during war but rents did not come down after); AKS adopts extra-constitutional methods: resist eviction + social boycott of non-joiners + refusal of forced labour; AKS joins NCM 1920-22; quickly grows to 300+ branches; AKS turns violent 1921 (looting of bazaars + attacks on taluqdar houses)

NANKANA TRAGEDY 1921 — Mahant of Nankana Gurudwara uses 500 mercenaries when Sikhs try to enter Gurudwara; hundreds of Akalis killed; eventually Akalis take control of Nankana Gurudwara; in 1921 Akalis pass resolution adopting Non-Cooperation -> Akali Movement becomes part of NCM

MAPILLA REVOLT 1921, MALABAR — Mapillas (Muslim tenants) part of Khilafat movement; primary grievance: oppression by Hindu Jenmies (hereditary landowners) = heavy rents + arbitrary eviction; INC joins + supports movement initially; when INC leaders arrested = lack of leadership; revolt turns violent + takes COMMUNAL COLOUR (anger against Jenmies as economic class turns into Hindu-Muslim violence); British declare martial law + suppress revolt; hurt Hindu-Muslim unity within NCM; Prelims 1997: Moplah Revolt = Malabar, Kerala; background: Mapillas had long history of revolts (1840s + 1870s = same agrarian grievance)

EKA MOVEMENT 1921, AWADH — same grievances as Kisan Sabha movement + added tyranny of thikedars (rent collectors who squeezed peasants even harder than zamindars themselves); same methods: resistance + boycott + refusal of forced labour; KEY DIFFERENCE: leader = Madari Pasi (from lower castes = significant; shows peasant struggle draws leaders from most oppressed sections); did NOT adhere to non-violence (unlike Gandhian movements); made it easy for British to repress on law + order grounds; CRUSHED BY 1922; Prelims 1997: Eka Movement = Awadh; Madari Pasi = Extremist, not Gandhian, of the peasant world

Awadh Rent Amendment Act 1921 — British bring this to address some rent-related grievances + take sting out of Kisan Sabha agitation; AKS movement ends: partly through repression (Seditious Meetings Act 1911) + partly through legislative concession

KEYS AFFAIR 1921 — Akalis had got control over Golden Temple but NOT over Toshikhana (treasury) of Temple; movement for keys of Toshikhana; led by Baba Kharak Singh (MODERATE); British soon give keys (policy: appease moderates + suppress extremists among Akalis)

GURU KA BAGH INCIDENT 1922 — Gurudwara given to Akalis but Mahant still controlled lands around Gurudwara; movement to get control over these lands; high Government suppression (NCM already over; British want to restore authority); Akalis continue to bear repression + finally win

BORSAD SATYAGRAHA 1922-24, Gujarat — leader: Vallabhbhai Patel; grievance: monetary collusion between dacoits + police (police in league with dacoits + not protecting people); PLUS govt applies additional tax on villagers to fund upkeep of extra police force to deal with dacoity problem; dual tyranny: dacoits loot them + police colludes with dacoits + govt makes peasants pay for extra police force that doesn't do its job; ACTION: Patel asks villagers NOT to pay additional tax + NOT to resort to violence even if govt confiscates movable property; volunteer corps raised to alert villagers when police come for confiscation; RESULT: Governor of Bombay upset over accusation of police-dacoit collusion -> orders inquiry -> immediate halt to confiscation + withdrawal of additional tax; textbook Gandhian satyagraha: specific grievance + non-violent resistance + moral pressure + concrete outcome; Patel's organisational skills already becoming visible; Prelims 1996: Sarabandi (no-tax) campaign 1922 leader = Vallabhbhai Patel GURUDWARA REFORM ACT 1925 — British pass to prevent disaffection in Army (Sikhs = significant part of British Indian Army; British could not afford Sikh disaffection in military ranks); RESULT: SGPC (elected body of Sikhs) gets control over ALL Gurudwaras; Akali Movement succeeds; POSITIVES: politicisation of Punjab's peasantry; educated middle-class Sikhs take over leadership from pro-British feudal class; rural + urban unity; Hindu-Muslim-Sikh unity; growth of nationalist + anti-British sentiments in Princely States of Punjab; NEGATIVES: religiously charged atmosphere -> later encourages communalism; post-movement Akalis split into 3 factions: (i) Gandhians + Leftists -> Kirti Kisan Party; (ii) Communalists -> continued as Akali Dal; (iii) Loyalists to British -> Unionist Party
MG withdraws support to Akali Movement when Akalis protest for restoration of deposed Raja of Nabha (Princely State) — movement turns violent; MG's support = conditional on non-violence

Gandhi visits Bardoli 1927 — campaigns through Young India + Navajivan; works to unite low-caste Kaliparaj with Ujaliparaj by opposing Hali system (hereditary forced labour + alcohol addiction -> debt trap); Gandhi renames Kaliparaj as 'Rani Paraj' (People of the Forests) giving them dignified identity; Bhajan Mandalis used to raise political awareness; CW phase before Bardoli movement launches

BARDOLI SATYAGRAHA 1928, Surat, Gujarat — Prelims 2003: Bardoli Satyagraha 1928 leader = Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; background: Bardoli people already politically organised from NCM; two caste groups: Kaliparaj (lower castes) + Ujaliparaj (upper castes); bonhomie between two groups; INC had originally planned CDM to begin from Bardoli itself; GRIEVANCE: (i) Hali system (hereditary forced labour + alcohol addiction -> debt trap); (ii) Govt imposes 30% increase in land revenue assessment (peasants consider it unjust + based on miscalculation); PATEL TAKES LEADERSHIP 1928: focus kept LIMITED to unjust aspects only; highlights miscalculation in 30% increase; asks peasants to pay LR only at OLD RATES; demands independent tribunal to examine assessment; ORGANISATION: uses Chhavnis as basic unit for organising peasants; women included in movement; social boycott of non-supporters; Bardoli Patrika (local newspaper) for spreading awareness about miscalculated assessment; PLAs members resign (e.g. K.M. Munshi); Gandhi reaches Bardoli 1928 adding weight (classic MG style = CW first -> localised agitation -> wider political pressure -> rising tempo); PATEL RECEIVES TITLE 'SARDAR' from women + ryots of Bardoli; RESULT: truce reached; independent tribunal appointed; tribunal revises LR increase DOWN to 6.03% (from original 30%); MG style of arbitration to reveal economic truth = always seeks middle path based on facts not maximalist demands; Bardoli = preparation ground for CDM 1930 (same region INC had originally planned CDM from)

anchors: Akali Movement — Why British Conceded (Gurudwara Reform Act 1925): British did NOT concede on principle. They
conceded because they could not afford Sikh disaffection in their military ranks (Sikhs = significant part of British Indian Army).
British strategy inside Akali Movement = appease moderates + suppress extremists: (1) Golden Temple given to Akalis easily
(appease moderates). (2) Keys Affair: Baba Kharak Singh (moderate) leads -> British give keys quickly. (3) Nankana Tragedy
1921: 500 mercenaries + hundreds of Akalis killed; eventually Akalis take control. (4) Guru Ka Bagh 1922: Mahant keeps lands;
high repression; Akalis bear repression + finally win. Post-Akali split: Kirti Kisan Party (Gandhians + Leftists) + Akali Dal
(Communalists) + Unionist Party (British loyalists). MG withdraws support when Akalis turn violent over deposed Raja of Nabha.
Peasant Movements vs INC — Key Distinction: Peasant movements of 1920s were BOOSTED BY INM (Home Rule 1916-18,
NCM 1920-22, Khilafat) BUT were NOT of INC and were INDEPENDENT of INC. Peasants had own grievances, own leaders,
often own methods. Two-way street: INC raised Swaraj among peasants; peasants raised land + rent issues within INM. Evolution
from disorganised unrest to disciplined Gandhian satyagraha: UPKS 1918 -> AKS 1920 -> Eka 1921 -> Borsad 1922-24 -> Bardoli
1928. Future linkage: Kisan Sabha participation in NCM -> All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) 1936 (covered in later chapters). INC
leadership not always comfortable with direction peasant anger could take (AKS 1921 violence; Mapilla communal turn 1921).
n Prelims Cluster — Peasant Movements (1996 + 1997 + 2003 + 2005): 1996: Sarabandi (no-tax) campaign 1922 leader =
Vallabhbhai Patel. 1997: Match-List: Moplah Revolt = Malabar Kerala; Eka Movement = Awadh UP (led by Madari Pasi); Bardoli =
Surat Gujarat; Pabna Revolt = Bengal (Pabna Agrarian Leagues 1873). 2003: Bardoli Satyagraha 1928 leader = Sardar
Vallabhbhai Patel. 2005: UP Kisan Sabha February 1918 — NOT associated with it = Jawaharlal Nehru (engaged only from June
1920); ASSOCIATED with UPKS 1918 = Gauri Shankar Mishra + Indra Narayan Dwivedi + Madan Mohan Malaviya (all three).

sections.title: Why Did Revolutionary Activities Revive after 1922?
1929 Bomb in CLA by Bhagat Singh & B.K. Dutt
Ideology of Bhagat Singh and HSRA1928

events.label: Amnesty 1920 — revolutionaries who had been jailed under Defence of India Act 1915 released; enthusiastically join Gandhi's NCM 1920-22

NCM abruptly withdrawn after Chauri Chaura — revolutionaries DEEPLY DISAPPOINTED; no interest in parliamentary politics of Swarajists (Pro-Changers) OR in Constructive Work of No-Changers (Gandhians); return to revolutionary activity; but this time with socialist + secular ideological framework (unlike 1907-15 era)
Lahore Student Union set up 1923 by Lala Lajpat Rai — Bhagat Singh later works actively in it; parallel to setting up Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha 1926

HRA (Hindustan Republican Army / Association) set up 1924 — founders: Ram Prasad Bismil + Ashfaqullah Khan + Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee + Chandrashekhar Azad + Sachin Sanyal (Sanyal was associated with Delhi Conspiracy Case 1912 + wrote Bandi Jeevan = guide to revolutionary activities); GOAL: armed revolution to establish 'United States of India' with UNIVERSAL ADULT FRANCHISE; 'Philosophy of Bomb' document: written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra + Azad — elaborated ideology of revolutionaries + defined them as not criminals but revolutionaries with clear vision

KAKORI ROBBERY CASE 1925 — HRA1924 needs money to buy arms; on 9 August 1925 train robbed @ Kakori (near Lucknow); cash looted from train carrying British government treasury funds; Ram Prasad Bismil (chanted Gayatri Mantra before pulling chain) + Ashfaqullah Khan + others participate; many members arrested; RAM PRASAD BISMIL + ASHFAQULLAH KHAN hanged; Chandrashekhar Azad NOT caught; HRA1924 goes inactive; Prelims 1997: Kakori Conspiracy leaders = Ram Prasad Bismil + Ashfaqullah Khan (Match-List)
Sachin Sanyal sentenced to life imprisonment in Kakori case; Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee arrested in Kakori case
events.full: Sachin Sanyal sentenced to life imprisonment in Kakori case; Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee arrested in Kakori case (Prelims 2022 Ghadar trap: Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee belongs to 1920s HRA/HSRA phase NOT Ghadar 1913-15)

events.label: Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha (PNBS) set up 1926 by Bhagat Singh — to educate youth on mass politics; Bhagat Singh: 'I acted like a terrorist but I am not a terrorist; I urge youth to join INC + INM rather than follow path of revolutionary activities'

HSRA (Hindustan Socialist Republican Army / Association) set up 1928 — Chandrashekhar Azad + Bhagat Singh revive HRA1924 as HSRA1928; word 'SOCIALIST' added to name = reflects leftward ideological shift; brings together all revolutionaries of North India; key members: Sukhdev + Rajguru + Bhagwati Charan Vohra; Vohra killed 28 May 1930 while testing bomb near River Ravi, Lahore (significant loss to movement)

LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE TRIGGER — Lala Lajpat Rai ('Sher-e-Punjab') brutally assaulted during anti-Simon Commission protests in Lahore October 1928 under Superintendent of Police James Scott's orders; Lajpat Rai reportedly declares: 'Every blow on my body is a nail in the coffin of the British Empire'; dies 17 November 1928 from injuries; BHAGAT SINGH decides to AVENGE his death

SAUNDERS ASSASSINATION December 1928 — target was James Scott (SP who personally ordered + led assault on Lajpat Rai); MISTAKEN IDENTITY: John Saunders (DSP = Deputy Superintendent of Police) killed instead; perpetrators: Bhagat Singh + Rajguru + Sukhdev + Chandrashekhar Azad; Bhagat Singh escapes dressed as woman; leads to SECOND LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE (1929-31) [DO NOT CONFUSE with FIRST LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE 1915 = Ghadar Movement]

BOMB IN CLA April 1929 — Central Legislative Assembly (CLA) discussing: (i) Public Safety Bill + (ii) Trade Disputes Bill — both aimed at curbing Working Class movement + communists (British feared rising communist influence); Bhagat Singh + B.K. Dutt throw HARMLESS BOMB inside CLA along with leaflets carrying now-famous phrase: 'TO MAKE THE DEAF HEAR'; intention = NOT to kill anyone but to draw attention; Bhagat Singh deliberately COURTS ARREST; uses court trial as platform for propaganda to inspire nationalism among masses; courtroom = his stage; speeches during trial do more for nationalist cause than the bomb
Hunger strike in jail 1929 — Bhagat Singh starts hunger strike against inhuman living conditions of prisoners; fellow prisoner JATIN DAS dies on 64th day of hunger strike due to forced feeding

Bhagat Singh in jail sets up LIBRARY — believes more in power of pen than in violence; writes essay 'Why I Am an Atheist' (1930) in jail: powerful articulation of rationalist worldview; rejects religious dogma; affirms commitment to reason + revolutionary ideals
BHAGWATI CHARAN VOHRA killed 28 May 1930 @ River Ravi Lahore while testing bomb — significant loss to HSRA1928

SECOND LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE (1929-31) — trial for Saunders assassination + CLA bomb; AZAD: encounter @ Alfred Park (now Chandrashekhar Azad Park) Allahabad on 27 February 1931; SHOT HIMSELF rather than surrender to British

phases.label: RESULT: BHAGAT SINGH + SUKHDEV + RAJGURU hanged 23 MARCH 1931; CHANDRASHEKHAR

events.label: CHITTAGONG ARMORY RAID 1930 — Surya Sen (school teacher from East Bengal) sets up Indian Republican Army (IRA); mobilises even WOMEN into IRA (significant — women as active combatants); raid on Chittagong Armory; declared PROVISIONAL REVOLUTIONARY GOVERNMENT; cut off Chittagong from rest of Bengal by destroying communication systems + railway lines; when British attack = move to hills + villages for guerrilla warfare; 1st time since 1857 that there was GROUP ACTION in armed struggle; Prelims 2001: Chittagong Armoury raid organiser = Surya Sen; Prelims 1997: Match-List Chittagong Armoury Raid = Surya Sen

CHITTAGONG EVENTS 1930-33: Pritilata Waddedar (age 21): consumed POTASSIUM CYANIDE to avoid capture by British -> becomes martyr; Kalpana Dutt: receives life imprisonment; Muslim villagers gave food + shelter to revolutionaries (showing deep secular + communal solidarity of movement); Muslim cadre members in IRA: Sattar + Mir Ahmad + Fakir Ahmad Mian + Tunu Mian SHANTI GHOSH (age 15) + SUNITI CHAUDHARY (age 14) — school girls; shot dead District Magistrate of Comilla C.G.B. Stevens on 14 December 1931

BINA DAS (age 21) — fired FIVE SHOTS at Governor Stanley Jackson during convocation ceremony @ Calcutta University February 1932; Jackson survived; (Note: post of Lt Governor of Bengal created in 1854; elevated back to Governor in 1912)

BENGAL REVOLUTIONARIES CONTEXT: Bengal revolutionaries had supported Swarajist leader C.R. Das; this leads British to repress Bengal Swarajists; after C.R. Das died 1925: factionalism weakens Bengal Congress; two rival groups: S.C. Bose (support of revolutionary group Yugantar) vs J.M. Sen Gupta (support of revolutionary group Anushilan Samiti); failed attempt on life of Police Commissioner by Gopinath Saha leads to arrest of S.C. Bose + fresh wave of repression in Bengal Jawaharlal Nehru arrested 1933 on Sedition Charges — sentenced to 2 years imprisonment for condemning imperialism + praising heroism of Chittagong revolutionaries
By 1933 — Chittagong revolutionaries crushed; revolutionary movement post-NCM comes to end; greatly inspired nationalism across India
Surya Sen captured + hanged 1934 — end of the Chittagong armed struggle

sections.title: What did INC do? — The 1927 INC Madras Session

events.label: Montague Statement / August Declaration 1917 — promises 'gradual development of self-governing institutions with view to progressive realisation of responsible government in India within British Empire'; GOI Act 1919 = 1st step; built-in 10-year review provision in GOI Act 1919 = mechanism for Simon Commission; Prelims 1998+2013: Simon Commission boycott reason = NO INDIAN MEMBER (violation of principle of self-government promised in Montague Statement)

GOI Act 1919 (Montford Reforms) — Section 84A built-in provision: review of reforms after 10 years (i.e. by 1929); BUT Simon Commission appointed in 1927 = 2 YEARS AHEAD OF SCHEDULE; reason: Conservative Govt in Britain did not want to leave politically sensitive matter to next govt + pressure from Pro-Changers in INC + rising revolutionary activity + fear of communism spreading in India
Bardoli Resolution 1922 — passive phase of INC begins after NCM withdrawal; Simon Commission appointment 1927 = end of this passive phase

SIMON COMMISSION (Indian Statutory Commission) appointed 1927 — COMPOSITION: Sir John Simon (head) + 7 members of British Parliament; CLEMENT ATTLEE = one of members (later PM of Britain 1945-51 who oversaw Indian independence); NO SINGLE INDIAN AMONG 7 MEMBERS; this = direct reason for INC boycott; SoS for India BIRKENHEAD challenges Indians: 'draft a constitution yourselves' (believed Indian leaders could not overcome internal differences + act unitedly; taunting Indians; partially proved right by Jinnah's 14 Points 1929)

Butler Committee appointed 1927 — to examine + clarify relationship between British Crown + Princely States; Prelims 2017: Butler Committee 1927 object = improve relations between Govt of India + Princely States

All India State People's Congress (AISPC) set up 1927 — INC-like organisation working within 565 Princely States; submitted to Butler Committee that AISPC (not the Princes) should be treated as representative body of Princely States (challenge to feudal authority of Princes from their own people)

INC MADRAS SESSION December 1927 — INC rejects Simon Commission; decides to set up ALL PARTY CONFERENCE (APC) for drafting Principles of a Constitution (basic structure of a Constitution; actual legal language would take years)

FOUR DELHI PROPOSALS December 1927 by ML1906 — addressed to Motilal Nehru; INC initially accepts; later rejected by APC; demands: (i) 1/3 reservation for Muslims in central legislature (Muslims ~20% of population = over-bargaining at 33%); (ii) creation of 3 new Muslim Majority Provinces (MMPs) by: separating Sindh from Bombay Presidency + granting full province status to Baluchistan + NWFP (more provinces = more MLAs + MPs + Ministers from ML1906 = more political power); (iii) reservation in MMPs of Punjab + Bengal in proportion to Muslim share of population; (iv) if above 3 met: ML1906 WILLING TO ACCEPT JOINT ELECTORATES (1st + last time ML1906 agreed to joint electorates — but loaded with conditions)
APC formally set up in Delhi (1928) — headed by M.A. Ansari; committee under APC constituted under Motilal Nehru in May 1928 to draft Principles of a Constitution

NEHRU REPORT August 1928 — Motilal Nehru chairs; 1st Indian attempt at a constitutional blueprint; DEMANDS: (i) DOMINION STATUS (not Purna Swaraj): maximum self-governance without leaving British Empire; sovereignty remains with British Crown; Britain retains power to change constitution + overall responsible for Defence + Foreign Policy; Indians have self-governance in domestic sphere; (ii) UNION OF INDIA (1st time): bringing together British India + Princely States in federal relations (565 versions of Article 370 without democracy = non-interference by Centre in Princely States' affairs); for British India = UNITARY STRUCTURE (strong Centre + residuary powers with Centre); Prelims 2011: Nehru Report 1928 recommendations = Dominion Status + joint electorates + fundamental rights

NEHRU REPORT — OTHER PROVISIONS: (i) Linguistic reorganization of Provinces (Tilak's original demand from HRL 1917; eventually: States Reorganisation Act 1956); (ii) Supreme Court + independent Judiciary; (iii) Bicameral legislature at Centre (upper house 7-year term + lower house 5-year term); (iv) Governor-General to function on aid + advice of Executive Council; (v) UNIVERSAL ADULT FRANCHISE (demanded clearly for 1st time; formal UAF demand); (vi) Directive Principles for State's Policy (DPSPs); (vii) 19 Fundamental Rights (UAF + women's equality + trade union rights + dissociation of State from religion + liberty + education + workers + Lower Castes + minorities)

NEHRU REPORT — COMMUNAL PROVISIONS (friction point): (i) NO separate electorates (reversal of LP1916; blow to ML1906); (ii) NWFP + Baluchistan to be made full provinces (ML1906 wanted this = accepted); (iii) separation of Sindh from Bombay Presidency = CONDITIONAL ONLY (after Dominion Status achieved + only if Sindh financially viable; ML1906 wanted unconditional separation = partially met); (iv) NO reservation for Muslims in MMPs (ML1906 unhappy); (v) reservation for Muslims in Muslim-minority provinces + at Centre = in proportion to population percentage (NOT 1/3 ML1906 demanded; ML1906 unhappy); (vi) reservation for non-Muslim minorities in Sindh + NWFP; (vii) reservation to last only 10 years + reviewed after (like COI 1950 reservation provision); (viii) no State religion but protection of culture of minorities

SIMON COMMISSION SECOND VISIT October 1928 — triggers massive anti-Simon protests across country; 'SIMON GO BACK'; Lala Lajpat Rai subjected to brutal lathi charge by SP James Scott during Lahore protests; Lajpat Rai: 'Every blow on my body is a nail in the coffin of the British Empire'; Lajpat Rai dies November 1928 from injuries -> leads to Saunders assassination by Bhagat Singh Dec 1928 -> Lahore Conspiracy Case 1928

THREE CALCUTTA AMENDMENTS December 1928 by ML1906 / Jinnah — proposed to Nehru Report at APC Calcutta meeting; ALL THREE REJECTED by APC; demands: (i) 1/3 Muslims in Central Legislative Assembly (CLA); (ii) reservation in MMPs of Punjab + Bengal in proportion to Muslim population until UAF implemented (logic: under income-based voting criteria Muslims who are generally poorer may not form majority in voter list even in Muslim majority provinces); (iii) RESIDUARY POWERS to Provinces not to Centre (minority/regional party always desires federalism as it knows it will not be in power at Centre)

INC CALCUTTA SESSION December 1928 — INC formally approves Nehru Report; S.C. Bose moves resolution to adopt PURNA SWARAJ as INC goal instead of Dominion Status = FAILS; COMPROMISE: if Dominion Status not granted within ONE YEAR -> INC goal becomes Purna Swaraj + will launch CDM; INC also passes CW (Constructive Work) resolution: boycott of foreign cloth + promotion of Khadi + self-reliance (not for political Swaraj but for income of poor; thus NOT Non-Cooperation) + anti-liquor campaign + anti-untouchability + women empowerment awareness + training in non-violent satyagraha + organisational strengthening of INC

Butler Committee Report 1929 — 2 key findings: (i) British Paramountcy over Princely States RE-AFFIRMED; (ii) Paramountcy should remain intact = Princely States SHOULD NOT BE TRANSFERRED into Union of India without their own consent (this is why GOI Act 1935 uses mechanism of Instrument of Accession (IOA) for Princely States to join proposed federation; IOA operative until COI 26 January 1950)

JINNAH'S 14 POINTS March 1929 — after failure of Four Delhi Proposals Dec 1927 + Three Calcutta Amendments Dec 1928; Birkenhead's challenge to Indians = partially proved right (not because Indians lacked ability but because British-era communal divisions made consensus difficult); Jinnah's 14 Points = summary of every communal demand ever made by any Muslim organisation; blueprint for all future political actions of ML1906 (contained every divisive demand EXCEPT demand for Pakistan which came later); KEY DEMANDS: (1) Separate electorates; (2) Veto power if 3/4 minority members oppose bill; (3) 1/3 Muslims in central legislature; (4) minimum 1/3 reservation in cabinet at Centre + Provinces; (5) reservation in all elected bodies even where Muslims in majority; (6) reservation in govt services; (7) reservation in MMPs; (8) creation of new MMPs (Sindh + Baluchistan + NWFP); (9) Federal constitution; (10) Residuary powers to Provinces; (11) Provincial autonomy; (12) No constitutional amendment without consent of Provinces; (13) No territorial reorganization negatively affecting Muslim majority status; (14) Protection of Muslim culture; Birkenhead partially proved right: INC + ML1906 could not agree

CLA Bomb April 1929 (Bhagat Singh + B.K. Dutt) — 'to make the deaf hear'; Public Safety Bill + Trade Disputes Bill in CLA (both aimed at curbing WC movement + communists; British fear rising communist influence); harmless bomb + leaflets; Bhagat Singh deliberately courts arrest; courtroom = propaganda stage

Meerut Conspiracy Case 1929 — many communists arrested due to ongoing rail strikes + attempts at establishing Indian branch of Comintern; WC movement repressed; Delhi Manifesto later demands amnesty in this case

DIWALI DECLARATION / IRWIN STATEMENT 31 October 1929 — Viceroy Irwin26-31 issues statement: 'Dominion Status is implicit in Montague Statement 1917 + it is intent of British to give Dominion Status at a future date + for this purpose Britain will hold Round Table Conference (RTC) in London'; notice: NO DECISION (only intent); NO TIMELINE (vague future date); MECHANISM = RTC in London (not Constituent Assembly in India); British offer nothing concrete; INC responds with Delhi Manifesto

DELHI MANIFESTO November 1929 — meeting of national leaders of INC; specific conditions on INC's participation in proposed RTC: (i) RTC should act as CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY (CA) = draft constitution implementing Dominion Status not merely discuss reforms; (ii) MAJORITY of Indian delegates in RTC should be from INC; (iii) AMNESTY in 'Bomb in CLA' incident of 1929 (Bhagat Singh + B.K. Dutt; CLA bomb NOT Lahore Conspiracy Case which was about Saunders assassination) + amnesty in Meerut Conspiracy Case 1929 (communists arrested due to rail strikes + Comintern attempts); British reject all 3 conditions -> leads to Lahore Declaration (Purna Swaraj) Dec 1929 + CDM 1930

LAHORE SESSION December 1929 (follows directly from Delhi Manifesto rejection) — Jawaharlal Nehru elected INC President; PURNA SWARAJ = INC's goal; tricolour flag hoisted on banks of Ravi on 31 December 1929; 26 January 1930 = 1st Independence Day (Poorna Swaraj Day); CDM to follow; leads to Dandi March April 1930

(term used explicitly for 1st time; earlier LP1916 had implied it but not used the phrase). (3) 1st demand for Union of India (British
India + Princely States in federal relations). (4) 1st formal demand for Universal Adult Franchise. (5) 1st proposal for Directive

sections.title: Why Was CDM Not Launched Immediately?
NWFP: The Khudai Khidmatgars and the Qissa Khwani Bazaar Massacre
Karachi Special Session of INC, March 1931

events.label: INC LAHORE SESSION December 1929 — President: JAWAHARLAL NEHRU; 5 major decisions: (i) PURNA SWARAJ = INC goal (NOT Dominion Status); (ii) 26 January 1930 = Independence Day (independence pledge; date = last Sunday of January 1930 = holiday = maximum participation; this WHY 26 January chosen as Republic Day 1950 = date already carried symbolic weight from 1930; Constitution adopted 26 November 1949 = Constitution Day; came into effect 26 January 1950 = Republic Day); (iii) INC rejects RTC (does NOT participate in 1st RTC of 1930); (iv) INC withdraws from legislatures immediately (end of Pro-Changer strategy); (v) AICC (set up Nagpur 1920) empowered to launch CDM at appropriate time; Prelims 2012+2014: Lahore 1929 = Purna Swaraj declared as INC goal
events.full: INC LAHORE SESSION December 1929 — President: JAWAHARLAL NEHRU (Prelims 2006: Lahore 1929 President = Jawaharlal Nehru); 5 major decisions: (i) PURNA SWARAJ = INC goal (NOT Dominion Status); (ii) 26 January 1930 = Independence Day (independence pledge; date = last Sunday of January 1930 = holiday = maximum participation; this WHY 26 January chosen as Republic Day 1950 = date already carried symbolic weight from 1930; Constitution adopted 26 November 1949 = Constitution Day; came into effect 26 January 1950 = Republic Day); (iii) INC rejects RTC (does NOT participate in 1st RTC of 1930); (iv) INC withdraws from legislatures immediately (end of Pro-Changer strategy); (v) AICC (set up Nagpur 1920) empowered to launch CDM at appropriate time; Prelims 2012+2014: Lahore 1929 = Purna Swaraj declared as INC goal

events.label: MG's 11-POINT DEMANDS January 1930 — Irwin26-31 rejects ALL 11; CDM now inevitable; LOGIC: defines what Swaraj would mean for masses; 4 MIDDLE-CLASS ISSUES: (1) lower exchange rate Rupee to 1Rs = 1s 4d (from Hilton-Young Commission 1926 rate of 1s 6d; depreciation boosts Indian exports + discourages British imports); (2) protective tariffs for cotton; (3) full status to Indian Tariff Board; (4) Postal Reservation Bill (50% postal dept seats for Indians); 2 PEASANTS' ISSUES: (5) 50% decrease LR + zero LR during famine; (6) release confiscated property from Bardoli 1928; 5 GENERAL ISSUES: (7) decrease military expenditure + civil servant salaries; (8) amend Arms Act 1878 (right to bear arms for self-defence); (9) total prohibition on intoxicants; (10) release political prisoners not guilty of violence; (11) ABOLISH SALT TAX (8.2% of Govt revenue) + Govt salt monopoly (salt issue not new: demanded also in 1851-52 by BrIA + Bombay Association + Madras Native Association before Charter Act 1853; Salt Act 1882 applied tax + affirmed monopoly)
INDEPENDENCE DAY pledge ceremony — 1st celebration of Independence Day; tricolour hoisted across India; crowd takes independence pledge

DANDI MARCH begins March 1930 — MG marches from SABARMATI ASHRAM (set up 1917) to DANDI coast to break salt law; Prelims 1995: CDM started from Dandi/Sabarmati Ashram; Prelims 2009: Dandi March began the CDM; WHY SALT: consumed by everyone + highlights British oppression even in basic necessities + unites all especially poor + NOT Hindu issue (ML1906 cannot object on communal grounds) + NOT Bourgeoisie issue (CPI1925 cannot label it capitalist cause) + less chance of immediate repression (abolishing salt tax = does not significantly hurt Govt revenues)
MG reaches DANDI and breaks salt law (6 April 1930)

RAJAJI'S VEDARANYAM MARCH (Madras) — C. Rajagopalachari marches from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranniyam with 98 volunteers (selected from 1000+ applicants; trained to endure police brutality without retaliating); date chosen: 13 April 1930 = both Tamil New Year (Puthandu) + Jallianwala Bagh massacre anniversary (two powerful emotional triggers in one day); reaches coast 28 April; breaks salt law 30 April; DC Tanjore J.A. Thorne issues orders: criminal offence to provide food/water/shelter to marchers; local population ties food packets to tree branches + leaves provisions at secret spots; march anthem: 'Kathi indri ratham indri yuddham ondru varugudhu' (Namakkal Kavignar Ramalingam Pillai); Rajaji arrested 30 April; RUKMINI LAKSHMIPATHI = 1st woman in India to pay penalty for violation of salt laws; Prelims 2015: Tanjore coast salt march = C. Rajagopalachari, Vedaranyam
KELAPPAN'S MALABAR SALT MARCH (same day as Rajaji's march) — K. Kelappan ('Kerala Gandhi') from Calicut to Poyannur on 13 April 1930; also known for Guruvayur Temple Entry Satyagraha 1931-32

OTHER REGIONAL SALT MARCHES: Assam: Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani marches from Sylhet to Noakhali Bengal; Odisha: Inchudi @ Balasore = 'Second Dandi' (led by Gopabandhu Chaudhuri + Harekrushna Mahatab; massive women's participation: Rama Devi + Malati Choudhury); Karnataka: Ankola @ Uttara Kannada = 'Bardoli of Karnataka' (raids on Sanikatta salt works; leaders: M.P. Nadkarni + R.R. Diwakar + Karnad Sadashiv Rao); Maharashtra: Shiroda salt works @ Ratnagiri; Bombay: Vile Parle = movement HQ (Jamnalal Bajaj); Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay sells contraband salt outside Bombay Stock Exchange + Bombay HC; Andhra: Sibirams (military-style training camps) in Krishna + Godavari + Guntur districts; Konda Venkatappaiah in Vijayawada; Pattabhi Sitaramayya major organiser

KHUDAI KHIDMATGARS + QISSA KHWANI BAZAAR MASSACRE — NWFP: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan ('Frontier Gandhi' / 'Badshah Khan' / 'Fakhr-e-Afghan') = educator + social reformer; opened schools across NWFP; published Pashto-language journal Pakhtun (started 1928); founded Khudai Khidmatgars ('Servants of God') 1929 = volunteer brigade; popularly called Red Shirts / Surkh Posh (uniforms dyed with cheap brick-dust since white khadi got dirty too quickly in rugged terrain); integrated traditional Pashtun code of honour (Pukhtunwali) with Gandhian non-violence; framed non-violence as ultimate test of bravery for true Muslim + true Pashtun; volunteers took solemn oath to forgive oppressors + live pure life + serve humanity without reward; British arrested Ghaffar Khan 23 April 1930 @ Peshawar; massive unarmed crowds gathered @ Qissa Khwani Bazaar (Storytellers' Market) to protest; British sent armoured cars + ran over people + opened machine-gun fire; hundreds of peaceful protesters killed; eventually Pashtuns erupted + responded with violence; ROYAL GARHWAL RIFLES REFUSAL: British ordered predominantly Hindu Garhwali soldiers to open fire on unarmed Muslim crowds; soldiers led by CHANDRA SINGH GARHWALI flatly REFUSED; stated would not shoot unarmed citizens; court-martialled + given severe prison sentences for mutiny; = ultimate symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity during CDM + proof non-violent resistance penetrated even British Indian Army; Prelims 2002: Khudai Khidmatgars = Red Shirts + NWFP + Abdul Ghaffar Khan

MG ARRESTED May 1930 — gives British prior warning about planned peaceful raid on Dharasana salt works; ARRESTED in May 1930; DHARASANA SATYAGRAHA: leadership passes to Abbas Tyabji (76-year-old retired judge; marches with Kasturbai Gandhi; arrested before reaching Dharasana); then Sarojini Naidu + MG's son Manilal + Imam Saheb take charge 21 May 1930; ~2,500 volunteers march to salt works; ~400 police with steel-tipped lathis; satyagrahis beaten mercilessly; NOT ONE raises arm; 300+ injured; WEBB MILLER (American journalist, United Press) witnesses entire raid; report published in 1000+ newspapers worldwide; turns international opinion against British rule; British try to censor Miller's dispatch but truth gets out; MG later says Miller 'helped make' Indian independence

2nd STAGE CDM (May 1930 - March 1931) — no-revenue campaign in Ryotwari + Mahalwari areas (masses pay LR directly to Govt); non-payment of Chowkidari tax in Zamindari areas (deliberately chosen: confrontation framed as Indians vs British; NOT no-rent campaign in Zamindari areas which would have been Indian ryot vs Indian landlord, hurting unity); violation of forest laws in Central Provinces; Assam: protests against Cunningham Circular 1930-31 (forced parents to give assurance of good behaviour of children = mechanism to prevent youth from joining CDM) CDM REASONS (Great Depression GD1929): US Stock Market Crash October 1929 -> global depression; cash crop prices crash in international markets (cotton + jute both export crops badly hit = ryots devastated; recall: end of US Civil War 1861-65 caused similar cotton price fall contributing to Bombay Deccan Riots 1875); prices of wheat + rice also fall in domestic markets; LR stays same; moneylenders stop lending + demand repayment of old loans; peasants sell land for sowing season money; WC suffers low wages + lay-offs; CDM STRUCTURE: 1st Phase 1930-31 -> Gandhi-Irwin Pact 5 March 1931 (TRUCE) -> 2nd RTC September-December 1931 (INC participates) -> 2nd Phase 1932-34
GOVERNMENT DECLARES INC + ALLIED BODIES ILLEGAL 1930 — outlaws Congress Working Committee + provincial committees; 1st ever ban on Congress (ban returned January 1932)

1st ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE December 1930 — INC does NOT participate (boycotts); fails; British realise any constitutional settlement without INC carries no popular legitimacy; Prelims 2005: 1st RTC = all major political organisations of India did NOT participate (because INC boycotted = INC = the mass organisation; others without INC had no popular base)

GANDHI-IRWIN PACT (Delhi Pact) 5 March 1931 — REASONS: MG = rising violence during CDM 1st phase (Chittagong Armory Raid + Qissa Khwani Bazaar violence + Sholapur workers' violence); British = 1st RTC failed without INC; CDM proved INC has mass legitimacy; FEATURES: (i) CDM suspended; (ii) INC to participate in 2nd RTC 1931; (iii) right to make salt for personal use; (iv) right to picketing of liquor shops; (v) withdrawal of emergency ordinances; (vi) release of political prisoners not charged with violence; (vii) cancellation of fines + return of confiscated lands of peasants; (viii) BRITISH REJECT commutation of death sentence of Bhagat Singh (martyred 23 March 1931 = 18 days after pact); Prelims 2020: Gandhi-Irwin Pact terms = RTC invitation + prisoner release except violence-convicted + salt-tax relief in coastal areas

BHAGAT SINGH + SUKHDEV + RAJGURU HANGED 23 March 1931 — British refuse to commute sentence despite Gandhi-Irwin Pact; S.C. Bose's supporters show black flags to MG at Karachi Session 'MG Go Back' (angry MG did not save Bhagat Singh)

KARACHI SPECIAL SESSION INC March 1931 — President: SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL; 4 significant decisions: (i) approves Gandhi-Irwin Pact; (ii) passes resolutions on Fundamental Rights + National Economic Programme influenced by socialist principles (drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru; Prelims 2005: Karachi 1931 FR resolution drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru); (iii) defines Swaraj for masses = political freedom must include economic freedom (INC will get power; what will people get? economic freedom from oppression of poor by rich); (iv) S.C. Bose's supporters show black flags to MG; formal tribute paid to martyrs Bhagat Singh + others
events.full: KARACHI SPECIAL SESSION INC March 1931 — President: SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL (Prelims 2010: Karachi 1931 Session President = Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel); 4 significant decisions: (i) approves Gandhi-Irwin Pact; (ii) passes resolutions on Fundamental Rights + National Economic Programme influenced by socialist principles (drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru; Prelims 2005: Karachi 1931 FR resolution drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru); (iii) defines Swaraj for masses = political freedom must include economic freedom (INC will get power; what will people get? economic freedom from oppression of poor by rich); (iv) S.C. Bose's supporters show black flags to MG; formal tribute paid to martyrs Bhagat Singh + others

events.label: 2nd ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE September-December 1931 — INC participates (per Gandhi-Irwin Pact); FAILS: deadlock over separate electorates; ALL minorities demand separate electorates: Muslims + Anglo-Indians + Europeans in India + Indian Christians + Depressed Classes (represented by B.R. Ambedkar); MG + INC oppose separate electorates (Nehru Report 1928 had proposed joint electorates); British also reject Purna Swaraj; MG announces resumption of CDM (= 2nd phase); BRITISH DECLARE: NWFP to be full province (done 1932) + Sindh to be separated from Bombay as full province (done 1936) + Communal Award = separate electorates will be imposed by Govt if Indians fail to reach consensus
INC BANNED again January 1932 — MG imprisoned in Yeravda prison; CDM 2nd Phase begins

3rd ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE November-December 1932 — without INC (INC banned since January 1932); produces White Paper 1933; examined by Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC); JPC's report forms basis of GOI Act 1935

COMMUNAL AWARD / MacDONALD AWARD August 1932 — British PM Ramsay MacDonald announces because Indians could not reach consensus on joint electorates; extends separate electorates to DEPRESSED CLASSES as well (other minorities had separate electorates since GOI Act 1919); INC NEITHER ACCEPTS NOR REJECTS: because separate electorates had been demanded by Depressed Classes themselves (Ambedkar at 2nd RTC) + not imposed on them by British alone; MG undertakes 21-DAY FAST UNTO DEATH against Communal Award; Prelims 2013: Gandhi's 1932 Fast Unto Death = against Communal Award's separate electorate for Depressed Classes

POONA PACT September 1932 — MG's issue: not with quantum of representation but with METHOD of election (separate electorates = permanently divides Hindus + makes untouchability permanent feature of Indian political life); signatories: Ambedkar (on behalf of LC) + Madan Mohan Malaviya (on behalf of UC); PACT TERMS: (i) REJECTS Communal Award's separate electorates for Depressed Classes; (ii) INCREASES reservation: from 71 seats to 147 seats in PLAs + 18% reservation in CLA; EXAM NOTE: Poona Pact REJECTED method (separate electorates) but INCREASED reservation (from 71 to 147 seats = more than doubled); students confuse 'rejection' of Communal Award with 'reduction' in reservation = OPPOSITE IS TRUE; Depressed Classes contest in joint electorates with reserved seats = model forming basis of SC/ST reservation in Indian elections today; Prelims 1997: Poona Pact = between MG + Dr B.R. Ambedkar (NOT British Govt); Prelims 2025: MG included upliftment of Harijans after Poona Pact

MG RELEASED September 1932 on health grounds after 21-day fast — CDM 2nd Phase shifts focus to ANTI-UNTOUCHABILITY CAMPAIGN: MG asks Hindus to do penance + appeals for complete eradication of untouchability; works on internal reforms among Harijans (education + health + hygiene); appeals to Harijans to remove untouchability from within own communities; ORGANISATIONS SET UP: (i) Harijan Sevak Sangh / All India Anti-Untouchability League (1932); (ii) Harijan Sevak Fund (1932); (iii) Harijan Magazine (1933) + 20,000 km march across India + two fasts to raise awareness

Nellie Sengupta — 3rd WOMAN INC PRESIDENT (1933 Calcutta Session) — born Edith Ellen Gray @ Cambridge, England; married to J.M. Sengupta; took mantle during peak of British repression 1933; following arrest of designated President Madan Mohan Malaviya she defied govt ban to chair session; 3rd woman INC President (after Annie Besant 1917 + Sarojini Naidu 1925) = 2nd foreign-born woman; symbolises universal moral appeal of movement

CDM formally ended 1934 — RESULTS OF 2ND PHASE: low response (demoralisation after suspension of 1st phase); neither UC nor LC showed much enthusiasm for Harijan campaign (LC becoming more radical wanting political + economic rights; MG mainly addressed social dignity); Govt repression; YET INC benefitted: performed very well in 1937 provincial elections under GOI Act 1935 (political capital accumulated during years of mass mobilisation cashed in at ballot box)

anchors: CDM Impact — 1st Phase Positives + Negatives: POSITIVES: High urban + rural participation; MG shows more radicalism than
in NCM (did not withdraw despite initial violence); 1st time ALL-INDIA CD (not just NC); 1st time large-scale CAPITALIST CLASS
participation (traders stopped importing British cloth; 50% decrease in import of foreign cloth; GD1929 also contributed); 1st time
LARGE-SCALE WOMEN'S PARTICIPATION in both urban + rural areas; Rajaji + Kelappan + Dharasana + Chittagong =
geographically spread unlike Swadeshi 1905-11 which remained largely Bengal. NEGATIVES: No major WC participation except
Sholapur + Nagpur (CPI1925 boycotts CDM; workers not attracted to non-violent methods; MG cautious about WC participation
due to communist influence); Low Muslim participation (no INC-ML1906 pact unlike LP1916 before NCM); Middle-class youth not
attracted to non-violent Satyagraha (inspired by revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh); Capitalist participation decreased as financial
losses mounted; Peasant participation decreased due to property confiscation; Tenant ryots began no-rent campaigns on own (MG
cautious: no-rent = Indian ryot vs Indian landlord = hurt unity); Govt repression drove down participation after September 1930.

phases.label: CHRONOLOGY: GOI ACT 1935 — LEGAL BASIS TO CONGRESS MINISTRIES

events.label: 1st Burma War 1824-26 + 2nd Burma War 1852-53 -> Burma annexed; finally separated from India in 1937 under GOI Act 1935 NWFP carved from Punjab as Chief Commissioner (CC) Province 1901 — equivalent to Union Territory; directly under central administration
Province of 'Bihar + Orissa' created 1912 — combined province after Bengal's 1911 reorganisation

SIMON COMMISSION REPORT June 1930 — 7 members; 0 Indians; recommendations: (i) Provincial Autonomy: abolish Dyarchy (GOI1919) + replace with full responsible govt in provinces (with some emergency powers retained by Governor); (ii) NO change at Centre (Centre remains under British despotism); (iii) expansion of franchise (wider electorate but still short of UAF); (iv) retention of separate electorates; (v) NWFP province status + Sindh separation only after Finance Boundary Commission; (vi) SEPARATION OF BURMA from India; Prelims 2010: Simon Commission recommendation = abolition of Dyarchy at provincial level

1st RTC 1930 — Princely States representatives + non-INC parties participate; Princes DEMAND FEDERATION (union combining British India + Princely States); INC boycotts; fails; background demand for Federation of India
2nd RTC 1931 — INC participates; Indian demands (federation + responsible govt at Centre + Purna Swaraj) REJECTED; Nehru Report 1928 remains unfulfilled
3rd RTC 1932 — INC boycotts; practically irrelevant; produces White Paper 1933

NWFP raised from CC Province to GOVERNOR'S PROVINCE 1932 — limited legislative council of ~40 members with dyarchy-type arrangements; Governor retains very strong reserve + veto powers; executive NOT responsible to council; full responsible govt in NWFP comes ONLY with GOI1935 implementation from 1937
White Paper 1933 — produced by 3rd RTC; examined by Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC); JPC headed by Lord Linlithgow; JPC's report forms basis of GOI Act 1935
events.full: White Paper 1933 — produced by 3rd RTC; examined by Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC); JPC headed by Lord Linlithgow (Prelims 2004: JPC head = Lord Linlithgow); JPC's report forms basis of GOI Act 1935

events.label: CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY DEMAND 1934 — M.N. Roy (founder of CPI 1920 in Tashkent) first moots idea in 1934; then in May 1934 Swaraj Party (1923) also passes resolution demanding Constituent Assembly; INC consistently demands CA elected by UAF from 1927 onwards

RBI ACT 1934 — Reserve Bank of India established under RBI Act 1934; becomes operational 1 APRIL 1935; timed to coincide with broader constitutional + financial restructuring; set up as central banking authority to manage currency + credit = prerequisite for fiscal federalism envisaged by GOI1935; Prelims 2001: RBI 1935 established under GOI1935 framework

GOI ACT 1935 — key quote: Linlithgow36-43: 'the best way to maintain control over India'; 321 sections; THREE ROUNDS OF PRESSURE produced it: (i) HRA1924 + HSRA1928 + Chittagong 1930-33 (revolutionary pressure); (ii) Anti-Simon agitations 1928 + CDM 1930-34 (mass movement pressure); (iii) GD1929 (mass economic suffering from Great Depression)

GOI Act 1935 — TERRITORIAL REORGANISATION: Orissa + Bihar become FULL SEPARATE PROVINCES (1936); Sindh separated from Bombay Presidency as full province (1936); NWFP reaffirmed as province (full responsible govt from 1937); Burma separated from India (1937); United Provinces formalised as name (1937)

GOI1935 — CENTRE: FEDERATION OF BRITISH INDIA + PRINCELY STATES (NEVER BECAME OPERATIONAL): required at least 50% of Princes to sign Instrument of Accession (IoA) as defined in Section 6; threshold NEVER MET; GOI Act 1919 continued to govern Centre; WHY PRINCES REFUSED: (i) Paramountcy not abolished by GOI1935 = two bosses (Union Govt + British Crown); (ii) financial autonomy at stake (GOI could compel Princes to contribute to Defence Budget once IoA signed); (iii) smaller Princely States = low representation at Centre; (iv) feared democracy = INC could launch movements inside their States once part of Union; After signing IoA: Princely State transfers only DEFENCE + FOREIGN AFFAIRS + COMMUNICATIONS to Union Govt (structurally identical to J&K; signing IoA in 1947 with only 3 subjects + Art. 370 as legacy); Butler Committee 1927 had promised not to change Princely States' status without consent = Princes used this as cover to stay out

GOI1935 — BICAMERAL LEGISLATURE AT CENTRE (NEVER OPERATIONAL): Federal Assembly (FA, lower house) + Council of States (CoS, upper house); FA: 1/3 members = NOMINEES OF PRINCES (not elected) = practically eliminated INC majority chances; Elections to FA = INDIRECT (to limit INC strength; regional parties do better under indirect elections); Elections to CoS = DIRECT (better regional representation); Life: CoS = PERMANENT (1/3 retire every 3rd year; compare COI1950: 1/3 retire every 2 years); FA = 5-year life (compare CLA under GOI1919 = 3 years)

GOI1935 — DYARCHY AT CENTRE (proposed; never operational): Federal subjects divided into RESERVED (4) + TRANSFERRED; RESERVED SUBJECTS (STRICTLY 4): Defence + External Affairs + Ecclesiastical Affairs (Church) + Tribal Areas = Absolute Legislative + Executive control of Viceroy + up to 3 Counselors NOT responsible to legislature (link: 5th Schedule COI1950 for tribal areas); TRANSFERRED SUBJECTS: all other Federal List subjects including FINANCE + HOME = Viceroy acts on aid + advice of Council of Ministers responsible to FA + CoS; EXAM TRAP: Finance + Home = TRANSFERRED (not Reserved); BUT Section 12 gave Viceroy 'Special Responsibilities' allowing intervention to protect 'financial stability + credit of Federal Govt' (= override Finance Minister) + to prevent 'grave menace to peace or tranquillity of India' (= override Home Minister)

GOI1935 — FIRST FEDERAL DISTRIBUTION OF SUBJECTS: Federal List + Concurrent List + Provincial List (1st time proper federal distribution = ancestor of 7th Schedule COI1950); under GOI1919: Centre had outsourced some subjects to provinces but constitutional ownership remained with Centre; under GOI1935: provinces receive CONSTITUTIONAL OWNERSHIP of their subjects = PEAK OF FEDERALISM in British era (journey begins 1861, peaks here)

GOI1935 — VICEROY POWERS (Centre): 80% of Budget NON-VOTABLE; Viceroy retains residual + veto + ordinance powers + power to restore cuts in grants + power to certify rejected bills; Viceroy = NOT powerless ceremonial President

GOI1935 — FISCAL AUTONOMY: financial control transferred from Secretary of State for India (SoS) in London to VICEROY in India (since GOI1858 SoS had been top authority on Indian finances; Nehru calls this 'the only major change' in entire GOI1935); FEDERAL COURT: GOI Act 1935 provides for establishment of Federal Court = 1st court with jurisdiction over disputes between provinces + between provinces + Centre; Federal Court ACTUALLY SET UP 1937 (institutional ancestor of Supreme Court of India under COI1950); Prelims 1996: Federal Court 1937 = predecessor of Supreme Court of India

GOI1935 — RIGHT TO VOTE: extended to more Indians but income + education criteria = only 10% of population qualifies; WOMEN'S FRANCHISE = DERIVED NOT INDEPENDENT: (i) woman votes on basis of husband's income or property (financial threshold lower than direct qualification for men); (ii) widow votes on basis of property/income left by dead husband; (iii) in many provinces literacy alone sufficient for woman to qualify (vs men without property need middle school or matriculation); REPRESENTS

GOI1935 — DEPRESSED CLASSES / SCs: for 1st time get ELECTED RESERVED SEATS with JOINT ELECTORATES (under GOI1919 = only NOMINATED seats); significant step forward; Communal Award 1932 had separate electorates for Depressed Classes but Poona Pact 1932 replaced with joint electorates + more seats; GOI1935 implements Poona Pact model; women's seats = 'internal carve-out' within communal quota (Muslim quota has X seats; within that, some specifically reserved for Muslim women); voting = BOTH men + women vote for women's reserved seats but watertight communal rule still applies (only Muslim men + women can vote for Muslim Women's seat)

GOI1935 — PROVINCIAL AUTONOMY (came into force 1937): end of Dyarchy at provinces; all subjects = transferred subjects; Premier (CM) + Council of Ministers responsible to PLA; FULLY RESPONSIBLE GOVT at provincial level for 1st time; BUT GOVERNOR STILL TOO POWERFUL: 40% provincial Budget NON-VOTABLE; Governor retains: veto + ordinance + discretionary powers to summon PLA + administration of tribal areas (link: 5th Schedule COI1950) + special powers to protect minority rights + British business interests + civil servant privileges + POWER TO TAKE OVER GOVT indefinitely (link: Art. 356 COI1950 = President's Rule)
Orissa made full province 1936; Bihar made full province 1936; Sindh separated from Bombay as full province 1936; Prelims 2018: GOI Act 1935 = Provincial Autonomy + Federal structure proposed
GOI1935 comes into effect at PROVINCIAL LEVEL 1937 — Burma separated from India 1937; Federal Court set up 1937; NWFP gets full responsible govt 1937

PROVINCIAL ELECTIONS 1937 — INC contests; RESULTS: INC wins MAJORITY in 6 provinces (Madras + Bombay + UP + CP + Bihar + Orissa) + forms ministries in 8 of 11 provinces; coalition govts in Assam + NWFP; in Punjab: UNIONIST PARTY under Sikandar Hayat Khan wins majority; ML1906 managed only 2 of 175 seats in Punjab; in Sindh: Sind United Party wins; Prelims 2005: 1937 elections = Congress majorities in 8 of 11 provinces

CONGRESS MINISTRIES (28-MONTH RULE 1937-39) — WHY INC DECIDED TO FORM GOVTS: (i) same logic as Pro-Changers 1923 (prevent non-INC parties from occupying space); (ii) promote Constructive Work + governance experience; IMPACT: boosted morale of party cadre + peasants + workers; INC gained crucial administrative + governance experience (invaluable after 1947); INM strengthened in Princely States (Congress ministries inspired Praja Mandals / State People's Congresses to grow; AISPC 1927 membership increased) Congress Ministries resign September 1939 — Britain declares India at war with Germany without consulting INC; INC protests; Jinnah celebrates ('Day of Deliverance'); ML gains ground in Muslim political space vacated by INC

sections.title: Setting the Stage: Three Players, Four Questions
