phases.label: FRAMEWORK: FOUR QUESTIONS + COMPLETE CHRONOLOGY (1938–1942)

events.label: Pakistan term coined by Choudhary Rahmat Ali in his 1933 pamphlet 'Now or Never' — from Punjab + Afghania (NWFP) + Kashmir + Sindh + '-tan' of Balochistan; NOTE: 1940 Lahore Resolution NEVER USED the word 'Pakistan'; press + public attached the name to it later
Congress Socialist Party (CSP) founded 1934 — Jayaprakash Narayan (JP Narayan) + Ram Manohar Lohia; left wing inside INC; precursor to later left-INC mobilisation

INC HARIPURA SESSION 1938 — Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose as President; Haripura Address: urged adopting Roman script for Hindi to make common national language easier to learn; DECLARED: Purna Swaraj is goal for WHOLE OF INDIA including Princely States + Princely States are integral part of India (= no special status for Princely States; elected representatives only in CA, no nominees of Princes)

INC TRIPURI SESSION 1939 — Bose defeats Gandhi's preferred candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya in presidential election; Gandhi: 'Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat'; Pant Resolution passed by Gandhian right wing: Bose must form CWC strictly per Gandhi's wishes; BREAKDOWN OF LEFT COALITION: Communists (CPI) voted with Bose against resolution; Congress Socialist Party (CSP/JP Narayan) + MN Roy's followers ABSTAINED on Pant Resolution (chose Congress unity over Bose; feared permanent split destroying anti-imperialist movement); with right wing hostile + left fragmented Bose had no base left inside Congress; Bose unable to function as President without CWC support -> RESIGNS from INC; forms FORWARD BLOC 1939 (left-wing faction inside INC; aim: consolidate left wing + capture INC from within; later becomes political base from which Bose launches international campaign + INA)

WW2 BEGINS September 1939 — Britain declares India a belligerent WITHOUT consulting Indian leaders; Viceroy Linlithgow36-43 (1936-43) does not bother to consult INC; this single act of colonial arrogance sets tone for next 6 years

INC POSITIONS ON WWII — 3 distinct internal views: (1) MG = justice on Allied side (Nazi Germany + fascist Italy = aggressors; morally India should support Britain unconditionally; to take advantage of Britain's difficulty = wrong); (2) BOSE = Britain's weakness = India's opportunity; immediate CDM; (3) NEHRU = no cooperation unless India receives actual independence = Purna Swaraj; but also no mass movement during war itself; MAJORITY INC LEADERS privately favour Allied victory (cold strategic reason: after WW1 1914-19 victorious powers took over colonies of defeated powers; if Axis Powers won = India could become colony of Japan; Axis Powers = themselves dictatorships who would not give democracy to colonies); INC DEMANDS ON BRITAIN FOR WAR SUPPORT: (@ToP) immediate Responsible Govt at Centre + (@COI) promise Constituent Assembly after war + (@Swaraj) declare war aims regarding India's future; Linlithgow36-43 REJECTS ALL THREE + offers only advisory committee of Indian politicians (= feel consulted without being given power)

CONGRESS MINISTRIES RESIGN October 1939 — INC refuses to support British war effort; Congress ministries in provinces directed to resign; Prelims 2010: Congress Ministries resigned October 1939 because Linlithgow made declaration without consulting them
JINNAH'S 'DAY OF DELIVERANCE' — ML1906 sees opportunity in INC's confrontation with British; Jinnah announces Day of Deliverance (celebrates INC resignation from provincial govts)

ML1906 LAHORE RESOLUTION March 1940 — demands CREATION OF PAKISTAN (separate Muslim states in NW + NE India); NOTE: word 'Pakistan' NOT used in the Resolution itself; press + public attached the name later; @Swaraj: Linlithgow36-43 had panicked after Congress ministry resignations + promised Dominion Status after war

AUGUST OFFER (AO1940) by Linlithgow36-43 — attempt to bring INC back to table after Congress ministry resignations; PROVISIONS: (1) Advisory War Council set up; (@ToP) VEC expanded with more Indians; (@COI) Constituent Assembly after war where MAINLY Indians (not solely) would frame constitution = 1st time British formally promised constitution-making 'primarily responsibility of Indians themselves'; (@Swaraj) DOMINION STATUS AFTER WAR (Montagu 1917 = gradually; Irwin 1929 = gradually; Linlithgow 1940 = AFTER THE WAR = 1st time with clear timeline); (@Unity) 'no future constitution without consent of minorities' = effectively gives ML1906 VETO POWER over framing India's constitution (imagine: Article 1 'Union of India' proposed; ML votes No; Article fails; hung Assembly; British don't create Pakistan; India ungoverned)

WHY AO1940 REJECTED BY BOTH SIDES: INC rejected (Wardha Meet 1940): (@Swaraj) accepting AO = accepting Dominion Status instead of Purna Swaraj (INC goal since 1929) + veto clause = backdoor partition mechanism; ML1906 also rejected: (@Unity) no explicit mention of 2 separate CAs or of Pakistan; ML's anxiety: if British transfer executive power at Centre, Hindu-majority govt could simply ignore ML's veto + use force to prevent Pakistan; ML left with neither power nor Pakistan (imagine: Article 1 'Union of India' proposed; ML votes No; Article fails; British continue to rule India because of hung CA; ML's Pakistan STILL not created)

INDIVIDUAL SATYAGRAHA October 1940 — MG resists pressure from within INC to launch CDM; instead launches carefully limited symbolic protest: Satyagrahi makes PUBLIC ANTI-WAR SPEECH + asserts right to freedom of speech; goal = NOT Purna Swaraj = SPECIFIC NARROW DEMAND for freedom of speech (civil disobedience against Defence of India Act 1939 restricting civil liberties during wartime); FIRST 3 SATYAGRAHIS: Vinoba Bhave -> Nehru -> Brahma Dutt (arrested in that order under Defence of India Act 1939); movement generates own energy: Delhi Chalo Movement + Jail Bharo Movement; builds organisational tempo + popular mood feeding into Quit India Movement 1942-45; Prelims 2009: Individual Satyagraha = Gandhi launched with Vinoba Bhave 1st, then Nehru = selective + symbolic

VEC EXPANDED 1941 — British expand VEC under war pressure; Indians in VEC rise from 3 of 8 (GOI Act 1919 convention) to 8 of 12; (@ToP) HOWEVER Defence + Home + Finance portfolios NOT given to Indian ministers; 1st time Indians in majority at Centre but portfolios that mattered most remain out of reach
GERMANY ATTACKS USSR June 1941 — strategic shift; Axis Powers appear unstoppable; fear of Japanese invasion of India becomes very real
JAPAN ATTACKS US AT PEARL HARBOUR December 1941 — both USSR + USA now Allied partners; USA + USSR pressure Britain to demonstrate India as willing partner not unwilling colony

INC OVERRIDES NEHRU + MG December 1941 — majority INC offers to support British war effort IF: (@Swaraj) Purna Swaraj after war + (@ToP) immediate Transfer of Power at Centre (Viceroy becomes powerless President + Indian PM + Indian Ministers)
JAPAN OCCUPIES RANGOON March 1942 — Burma falls; India's eastern border directly exposed; Britain under intense pressure from USA + USSR to bring India as willing partner

CRIPPS MISSION March 1942 — led by Sir Stafford Cripps (minister in Churchill's War Cabinet); INC official negotiators: Nehru + Maulana Azad (serving INC President); MNEMONIC: Crispy chip that snaps + breaks into smaller pieces = Cripps Plan could crumble India into 565+11 = 576 parts; Prelims 2003+2009+2016+2022: Cripps Mission provisions + rejection grounds

CRIPPS MISSION PROVISIONS: (@Swaraj) Dominion Status after war + Indian control over foreign policy (adds foreign affairs to AO1940's Dominion Status package; still NOT Purna Swaraj); (@COI) Constituent Assembly after war composed SOLELY of Indians (upgrade from AO1940 which said 'mainly' Indians; 1st time solely Indian); CA composition: elected members from PLAs (after fresh elections under GOI Act 1935) + NOMINEES of Princely States (not elected = INC objects); (@Unity) EXPLOSIVE PROVISION: once CA frames constitution, any Province of British India OR any Princely State that disagrees can: (a) NOT join Union + (b) frame own constitution or set up own union within British Empire; STEP-BY-STEP: CA frames India's constitution -> Members representing Province/PS pass resolution disagreeing -> Province/PS allowed to SECEDE from Union -> can frame own constitution or join British Empire; 565 Princely States + 11 Provinces = 576 possible countries; (@ToP) IF power transferred during war: Defence continues under Viceroy; no dilution of Viceroy's powers over ministers (Viceroy NOT powerless constitutional President); this last point = ACTUAL BREAKDOWN of talks (British adopt 'take it or leave it' approach on Viceroy's war powers)

CRIPPS MISSION REJECTION: MG: 'post-dated cheque drawn on a failing bank' (most things take effect after war; nothing immediate); INC REJECTS: (@Swaraj) wanted Purna Swaraj after war not Dominion Status; (@COI) wanted Princely States represented by ELECTED members in CA not nominees of Princes (Haripura 1938: PS = integral part of India; elected reps only); (@Unity) NO right to secede given to any Province or PS; ML1906 REJECTS: wanted TWO Constituent Assemblies (one for Pakistan + one for rest of India); (@Unity) INC CONCESSION during Cripps negotiations: INC agreed to AUTONOMY for Muslim Majority Provinces within future COI (Centre to be weak compared to non-Muslim majority provinces = Article 370 principle applicable to ALL Muslim Majority Provinces; this INC concession = made during negotiations, NOT in formal Cripps offer itself)

Results and Significance of the QIM(1942-45)

phases.label: CHRONOLOGY

events.label: Congress Working Committee (CWC) at WARDHA July 1942 — accepts MG's idea of Quit India; CWC accepts idea; MG drafts resolution demanding Quit India + committing INC to non-cooperation against Japan if India were invaded; PHRASE 'QUIT INDIA' coined by Yusuf Meherally (same man who earlier coined 'Simon Go Back'); Prelims 2011: Quit India slogan coiner = Yusuf Meherally

INC QUIT INDIA RESOLUTION 8 August 1942 — INC holds special session @ Bombay; followed by massive public meeting @ GOWALIA TANK (AZAD MAIDAN) Bombay; QIM Resolution passed: demand for immediate Purna Swaraj; MG gives historic speech including 'DO OR DIE' (KARO YA MARO) call; lays out plan of action for public; Prelims 2009: Bombay 8 August 1942 = 'Do or Die' call + QIM Resolution; Prelims 2005: Cripps failure -> AICC Bombay 8 August 1942 Quit India resolution

ENTIRE TOP INC LEADERSHIP ARRESTED 9 August 1942 — same night as MG's public speech; detailed resolution NOT made public (public only knew what MG had said in speech the evening before; everything not mentioned in speech = private strategy of movement); ARUNA ASAF ALI hoisted national flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan after leaders arrested
events.full: ENTIRE TOP INC LEADERSHIP ARRESTED 9 August 1942 — same night as MG's public speech; detailed resolution NOT made public (public only knew what MG had said in speech the evening before; everything not mentioned in speech = private strategy of movement); ARUNA ASAF ALI hoisted national flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan after leaders arrested (Prelims 2009: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted national flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan during QIM)

events.label: MG's SPEECH — WHAT PUBLIC WAS TOLD: (i) Govt servants: do NOT resign; stay in posts but declare loyalty to INC + people of India; (ii) Soldiers: support Britain against Fascists (Allied war effort) but do NOT fire on own countrymen; (iii) Students: leave studies + join QIM; (iv) Princes: accept sovereignty of own people + stop supporting British; (v) People of Princely States: declare you are part of India; support your prince ONLY if he is anti-British; KEPT PRIVATE (not told publicly): (i) Peasants: do NOT pay land revenue; (ii) Tenants: pay only FAIR RENT + pay ONLY IF your zamindar is anti-British (1ST TIME INC explicitly raises NO-RENT campaign as part of its programme); (iii) INC position: LAND BELONGS TO ITS ACTUAL TILLER (1st time INC states vision of free India includes Ryotwari for all = significant ideological step)

MASS STRUGGLE PHASE — SIX WEEKS from 9 August 1942: movement was NOT non-violent (entire leadership under arrest; people acted on own angry understanding); PRIMARY TARGET: symbols of British authority; crowds removed railway tracks + blew up bridges + cut telephone + telegraph wires + attacked railway stations + police stations + courts + post offices; Tricolour flag hoisted on trains + public buildings; PARTICIPANTS: (1) COMMON PEOPLE (unparalleled heroism; harshest repression yet in INM); (2) Provincial + local INC leaders (top leadership in bars); (3) Villagers (joined as news of arrests spread); (4) PEASANTS (soul of QIM; esp eastern UP + Bihar + Midnapore Bengal + Satara Maharashtra; both rich + poor peasants; anger directed ENTIRELY at British with NO violence against zamindars or moneylenders); (5) Zamindars (big zamindars stayed neutral; smaller zamindars participated esp in UP + Bihar); (6) Workers (CPI1925 did NOT participate; yet many worker strikes broke out independently; Ahmedabad mills strike lasted 3.5 months; hundreds of individual Communists participated despite CPI official stand); (7) Women (school + college girls vital; Aruna Asaf Ali + Sucheta Kriplani = active organisers during underground phase; Usha Mehta ran Congress Radio); (8) Students (left studies; led processions; distributed illegal patrikas; acted as couriers); (9) Muslims (overall participation not high since ML1906 opposed QIM; BUT even ML1906 supporters gave shelter to underground activists + did NOT act as informers; TOTAL ABSENCE OF COMMUNAL VIOLENCE throughout movement)

BRITISH REPRESSION — immediate + severe; harshest response to any movement in INM history; British already prepared: Revolutionary Movement Ordinance + Defence of India Rules (preventive detention powers); entire top INC leadership arrested 9 August itself; press gagged; machine guns deployed on AIRCRAFT; collective fines on villages; whole villages burnt; 60,000 arrested by end of 1942; mass struggle phase crushed in SIX WEEKS; movement then goes underground

UNDERGROUND PHASE — led primarily by Congress Socialist Party; leaders: ACHYUT PATWARDHAN BHAI PURANIK + RAMNATH GOENKA (founder of Indian Express) + JAYAPRAKASH NARAYAN (JP); MNEMONIC: 'JP Goenka ASA Ram se BaCho' = JP + Goenka + Aruna Asaf Ali + Sucheta + Achyut + Ram Manohar Lohia + Biju; what network did: supplied bombs + arms to activists; pilots + train drivers delivered supplies (underground had penetrated critical British infrastructure); students as couriers; villagers refused to give information to police; Govt officials + police officers leaked details of impending raids (British authority eroded even within own apparatus); businessmen donated generously; SUMATI MORARJEE gave Achyut Patwardhan a different car every day so he could not be tracked

phases.note: THREE PRESSURES making QIM unavoidable by 1942: (1) FAILURE OF CRIPPS MISSION 1942

phases.label: + RAM MANOHAR LOHIA + BIJU PATNAIK + ARUNA ASAF ALI + SUCHETA KRIPLANI + CHHOTU

events.label: Mahadev Desai (MG's personal secretary) dies 15 August 1942 @ AGA KHAN PALACE PUNE (where MG was being held) — MG describes as losing his right hand; deepens public demands for MG's release

MG'S 21-DAY FAST 1943 (at Aga Khan Palace Pune) — British wanted MG to condemn violence of movement; he REFUSES + begins 21-day fast as protest against British violence; IMPACT: (i) triggered mass upsurge of demonstrations + strikes; (ii) Indian members of Viceroy's Executive Council resigned (did not want to be held responsible for MG's death); (iii) international media focuses on British repression; (iv) even those who had opposed QIM now demanded MG's release (fast brought unity that movement itself had struggled to generate)
Kasturba Gandhi dies 22 February 1944 @ Aga Khan Palace Pune — deepens public demands for MG's release; MG held here Aug 1942 to May 1944

PARALLEL GOVT 1: BALLIA EASTERN UP August 1942 — 1ST PARALLEL GOVT; leader: CHITTU PANDEY; people of Ballia overthrow District Collector + free INC leaders from jail; held briefly until British forces return then dissolves; British FAIL TO ARREST PANDEY; he later becomes Member of Parliament; Prelims 2000: Parallel Govt @ Ballia = Chittu Pandey

PARALLEL GOVT 2: JATIYA SARKAR MIDNAPORE BENGAL December 1942 - September 1944 — more sustained administration; INC had done extensive constructive work in Midnapore giving organisational foundation; Jatiya Sarkar: (i) set up arbitration courts; (ii) gave grants to schools; (iii) distributed rice to poor; (iv) provided cyclone relief; (v) established armed wing called VIDYUT VAHINI (= enforcement arm of functioning parallel state; direct challenge to British sovereignty); Prelims 2000: Tamluk-Midnapore = Tamralipta Sarkar

PARALLEL GOVT 3: PATRI SARKAR SATARA MAHARASHTRA mid-1943 to 1945 — MOST SUCCESSFUL + LONG-RUNNING parallel govt; founded by NANA PATIL (earlier engaged in Robin Hood-style robberies against colonial targets); guidance from ACHYUT PATWARDHAN (earned title 'LION OF SATARA' for his role); YB CHAVAN = most important leader until arrest end 1942; Prelims 2000: Satara = YB Chavan + Nana Patil; 'PATRI' = harsh punishment given to govt officials + informers collaborating with British; what Patri Sarkar did: (i) set up people's courts + village libraries; (ii) enforced prohibition on alcohol; (iii) organised GANDHI MARRIAGES where Dalits invited + given proper respect (direct challenge to caste hierarchy); (iv) functioned continuously mid-1943 to 1945
MG RELEASED May 1944 on health grounds — turns to constructive work
Germany surrenders May 1945
ALL INC LEADERS RELEASED June 1945 — to participate in SIMLA CONFERENCE June 1945; formally marks END OF QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT
Japan surrenders September 1945 — Britain's position in India never the same again

QIM RESULTS + SIGNIFICANCE: (1) India proved UNGOVERNABLE BY FORCE (scale: parallel govts for months; underground networks British could not dismantle; people choosing arrest over submission); (2) LOYALTY OF BRITISH ADMINISTRATIVE MACHINERY BROKE (officials leaking raid plans; police turning blind eye; Indian VEC members resigning = steel frame rusting from within); (3) PARALLEL GOVTS showed Indians could self-govern (courts + relief + law + administration = demonstrated fact; British argument 'India not ready' lost credibility); (4) INTERNATIONAL ATTENTION shifted decisively (MG's fast + 60,000 arrested + machine guns on aircraft = global coverage; USA applying quiet pressure on Britain); (5) MOVEMENT UNIFIED FRAGMENTED FORCES (even QIM opponents rallied behind demand for MG's release + end to repression); CONCLUSION: if CDM 1930-34 made world NOTICE India's demand, QIM 1942-45 made world ACCEPT the demand cannot be denied; British left 1947 NOT because they became generous but because AFTER 1942 THEY KNEW THEY COULD NOT STAY

sections.title: Indian National Army / Azad Hind Fauj (1942–1945)

phases.label: SEC. 1 — BENGAL FAMINE (1943): A MAN-MADE FAMINE

events.label: Viceroy LINLITHGOW36-43 in office (1936–1943) — during the famine he DID request food for India + proposed a BAN on food exports from Bengal; PM CHURCHILL DENIED BOTH
JAPAN OCCUPIES BURMA March 1942 — food imports from Burma, which Bengal had been receiving, STOP ENTIRELY (one of the four causes of the famine)

BENGAL FAMINE 1943 — roughly 5 MILLION Indians die ; THERE WAS NO ACTUAL FOOD SHORTAGE ; NOT a failure of crops = MAN-MADE FAMINE ; FOUR CAUSES: (1) food supplies from India incl Bengal DIVERTED TO EUROPE to feed British soldiers + European civilians (needs of army + Europeans given priority over Indian lives); (2) Burma food imports stopped after Japanese occupation March 1942; (3) government managed LOGISTICS + SUPPLY CHAINS POORLY (distribution of whatever food existed = chaotic); (4) war-driven SPECULATION pushed market prices beyond what ordinary people could afford

CHURCHILL'S RESPONSE 1943 — denies Linlithgow's food request + denies ban on food exports from Bengal; reportedly asks whether GANDHI was still alive or had died in his ongoing FAST UNTO DEATH (1943) ; in Britain, Churchill was COMPARED TO HITLER for this

IMPACT — deep + lasting DISTRUST OF BRITISH RULE among Indians (European lives visibly prioritised; govt did little by way of relief); British public opinion shifts noticeably: by 1943 MOST BRITISH POLITICIANS were sympathetic to Indian independence ; the famine ACCELERATED that shift

FAMINE INQUIRY COMMISSION 1945 — headed by SIR JOHN WOODHEAD ; investigates causes of the Bengal Famine; largely blames NATURAL FACTORS + SUPPLY DISRUPTION ; analysis remained INCOMPLETE + criticised for NOT holding the colonial administration adequately accountable insufficient food in Bengal but because large sections of the population LOST THEIR ENTITLEMENT TO FOOD : wages collapsed + prices skyrocketed due to speculation + govt procurement policies drained food from rural markets; = FAILURE OF ACCESS, NOT OF SUPPLY ; became one of the most influential ideas in development economics; Prelims 2008

FORWARD LINKAGE — devastation of Bengal's peasantry during 1943 DEEPENED the agrarian crisis that fuelled the CPI-led TEBHAGA MOVEMENT (1946–47) : demand that the landlord's share be reduced from HALF to ONE-THIRD (*link Ch 47 for Tebhaga + peasant mobilisation under CPI)

phases.label: SEC. 2 — INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY / AZAD HIND FAUJ (1939–1945)

events.label: HARIPURA SESSION 1938 — Subhas Chandra Bose elected INC President (first term)

FORWARD BLOC founded May 1939 by Bose WITHIN Congress — to consolidate the left + radical elements opposing the Gandhian old guard's dominance; advocated a MORE MILITANT approach to independence; sought to rally socialists + communists + other anti-imperialist groups into a unified front; founded BEFORE his formal resignation; after Bose left India, the Forward Bloc's organisational strength DECLINED significantly
TRIPURI SESSION of INC December 1939 — Bose elected President for a consecutive SECOND term (following Haripura 1938); differences with Gandhian leadership IRRECONCILABLE → he had to leave the INC
BOSE ARRESTED July 1940 — British view him as a political threat to their stability in India; he favoured starting a movement to OVERTHROW BRITISH RULE DIRECTLY
BOSE RELEASED January 1941 — failing health from a hunger strike forces the British to release him; placed under
THE ESCAPE — Bose escapes in disguise as an AFGHAN → Afghanistan → crosses into the USSR → travels in disguise as 'ORLANDO MAZZOTTA' → Italy → ARRIVES GERMANY March 1941

COLLAPSE OF BRITISH POWER IN SOUTH-EAST ASIA — Japan takes MALAYA (January 1942) + SINGAPORE (February 1942) + BURMA (March 1942) from the British; territories held for decades fall in a matter of weeks (this collapse = the direct birth-context of the INA)

MOHAN SINGH CONCEIVES THE INA — following the fall of Singapore (Feb 1942), Captain MOHAN SINGH conceives the idea of the INA by organising Indian PoWs; approaches the Japanese army + convinces them to hand over Indian Prisoners of War (PoWs); 40,000 PoWs in Singapore join
IIL BRANCH in the ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLANDS set up April 1942 by RAMA KRISHNA

INDIAN INDEPENDENCE LEAGUE (IIL) set up June 1942 @ BANGKOK, THAILAND — by independence-minded Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) motivated by Japanese victories, mainly PRITAM SINGH + SWAMI SATYANANDA PURI ; (*IIL = POLITICAL organisation; INA = its MILITARY arm — two wings, one purpose)
QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT begins in India (August 1942) — running parallel to INA developments abroad
INA FIRST DIVISION formally established September 1942 under Mohan Singh — this is when the INA comes into existence
AZAD HIND RADIO set up by Bose FROM GERMANY (1942) — broadcasts messages to India to boost the morale of those in the Quit India Movement (1942–45)
MOHAN SINGH ARRESTED BY THE JAPANESE December 1942 — he had demanded a PRIMARY ROLE + genuine AUTONOMY for the INA in any attack on British India → friction with the Japanese command
RASH BEHARI BOSE takes over INA leadership (early 1943) + reorganises it — an aged revolutionary who had escaped to Japan after the GHADAR MOVEMENT (1913–15)

anchors: PRELIMS TRAP n TRAP: Mohan Singh CONCEIVED + FIRST ORGANISED the INA in 1942 . Bose TOOK OVER LEADERSHIP in
1943 . Claiming the INA 'CAME INTO EXISTENCE' in 1943 is FACTUALLY INCORRECT — the INA existed from
September 1942 under Mohan Singh ; what happened in 1943 was a CHANGE OF LEADERSHIP , first to Rash
Behari Bose + then to Netaji

race + Indians as not (*Bose needed allies, not patrons who looked down on India — Hitler was the wrong ally)
Jul 1943 BOSE ARRIVES SINGAPORE July 1943 — in the Indian Ocean he transfers from a GERMAN SUBMARINE to a
JAPANESE one ; in a ceremony @ Singapore he takes over leadership of the IIL + the INA from an aged R.B. Bose

NOT dependent on Japan); raises the RANI JHANSI REGIMENT = all-women NRI regiment (*symbolism:
revolutionaries always held the 1857 revolt as reference point; Rani of Jhansi = its most iconic symbol); also a GANDHI
REGIMENT + a NEHRU REGIMENT ; extracts a crucial assurance from Japanese GENERAL TOJO : 'Japan does not

BADHAYE JA

(Burma) + SINGAPORE ; deliberately called 'PROVISIONAL' : Netaji believed a PERMANENT government could only
be a DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED one; Prelims 2017

Stadium); renames the Andamans = 'SHAHEED DWEEP' + the Nicobars = 'SWARAJ DWEEP'
1944 KOHIMA & IMPHAL CAMPAIGN 1944 — INA + Japan attack the India–Burma border ; targets = KOHIMA +
IMPHAL ; THE CAMPAIGN FAILS ; worse, during the Imphal campaign Indian INA soldiers were DISCRIMINATED
AGAINST by the Japanese in the allocation of weapons + supplies (*being an ally of Japan did not mean being treated
as an equal)

15 Aug 1945 JAPAN SURRENDERS 15 August 1945

SUBHAS CHANDRA BOSE ; a death that has remained SURROUNDED BY CONTROVERSY ever since
SEC. 3 — INA TRIALS + INA AGITATIONS (November 1945 – 1946)
Nov 1945 INA TRIALS BEGIN November 1945 — British put INA men (now PoWs) on trial; most famous trial held at the RED
FORT : accused = SHAH NAWAZ KHAN (close aide of Netaji) + PREM SEHGAL + GURBAKSH SINGH DHILLON ;
Prelims 2021
DATE EVENT

MASS UPSURGE across India cutting across ALL sections of society , supported by EVERY political party ; the
British themselves admitted NO ISSUE in the entire history of the INM had generated so much sympathy among
Indians ; INA agitations = MAXIMUM UNITY seen throughout the INM ; agitations were STARTED BY THE PEOPLE
THEMSELVES — NO political party gave the call; they arose SPONTANEOUSLY
1945-46 INC's ROLE — makes the INA agitations part of its ELECTION CAMPAIGN , demanding release of INA men; fights the
cases under BULLABHAI DESAI (lawyer + INC leader in the Central Legislative Assembly); sets up an INA RELIEF
COMMITTEE (raised funds + gave money to INA men on release + worked for rehabilitation); FOR THE FIRST TIME in
Indian history GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS OPENLY SUPPORTED A MOVEMENT — contributing money for INA
men; common people + Gurudwaras + even Bollywood contributed funds
SEC. 4 — THE NAVAL RATINGS MUTINY (February 1946)
Feb 1946 NAVAL RATINGS MUTINY BEGINS February 1946 — during the INA agitations; naval ratings on HIS MAJESTY'S
INDIAN SHIP (HMIS) TALWAR go on strike; THREE GRIEVANCES: (i) FEAR OF UNEMPLOYMENT — losing their
jobs once the war ended; (ii) POOR SERVICE CONDITIONS + RACIAL DISCRIMINATION IN SALARIES (*recall
1857 — the racial differential in pay + treatment had been a constant grievance in the Indian armed forces since the
sepoy era); (iii) INSPIRATION FROM THE INA — they had supported the INA agitations + contributed money for INA
men, and felt a direct identification with the cause
Feb 1946 THE REVOLT — ratings raise TRICOLOUR flags on their ships alongside flags of the INA + INC + MUSLIM LEAGUE ;
write 'QUIT INDIA' on ships incl HMIS Talwar; drive through BOMBAY in trucks carrying pictures of Netaji Bose ;
CPI1925 gives them support; workers across Bombay go on a MASSIVE STRIKE bringing the city to a standstill;
ARUNA ASAF ALI advises the ratings + provides leadership DESPITE opposition from MG + the INC (who felt it was
a truce period + time for negotiations); AIRFORCE MEN IN KARACHI begin sympathy strikes
Feb 1946 MUTINY ENDS — British repression played a role, BUT so did the WITHDRAWAL OF SUPPORT by the INC + the
MUSLIM LEAGUE ; SARDAR PATEL + JINNAH personally hold meetings to calm the ratings down ; Prelims 2005
1946 WHY IT MATTERED BEYOND THE EVENT — the Naval Ratings Mutiny + the ROYAL INDIAN AIR FORCE (RIAF)
strikes in several stations SHATTERED THE 'MARTIAL RACES' MYTH the British had cultivated since 1857 (the
notion that certain Indian communities were inherently loyal to the Crown + could always be relied upon to enforce
imperial authority against other Indians); Indian sailors + airmen turning against British command — NOT as isolated
incidents but as COORDINATED, POLITICISED acts of defiance — proved the British had IRREVOCABLY LOST
CONTROL OF THE INDIAN ARMED FORCES ; widely seen as ONE OF THE KEY FACTORS that convinced the
British that the TRANSFER OF POWER COULD NOT BE POSTPONED
Post-1947 AFTERMATH — after independence, MOST INA MEN + NAVAL RATINGS were NOT recruited into the armed
forces , on grounds of BREACH OF DISCIPLINE :(

Bengal Famine 1943 — Was There Actually a Food Shortage? (NO): The most important thing to understand is that the famine was NOT
caused by a failure of crops . It was a MAN-MADE famine and roughly 5 million Indians died . FOUR FACTORS combined: (1) food
diverted from India + Bengal to EUROPE for British soldiers + European civilians; (2) Burma imports stopped after Japan's occupation
(March 1942); (3) government mismanaged logistics + supply chains ; (4) war-driven speculation pushed prices out of reach. The
Famine Inquiry Commission 1945 (Sir John Woodhead) blamed natural factors + supply disruption — incomplete, and criticised for not
holding the colonial administration accountable. Decades later AMARTYA SEN gave the sharper answer: 'ENTITLEMENT FAILURE' —
people lost their ENTITLEMENT to food (wages collapsed + speculation-driven prices + govt procurement draining rural markets). A failure
of ACCESS, not of SUPPLY.
Why the Naval & RIAF Mutinies Mattered Beyond the Event Itself: The entire edifice of British India rested on using Indian soldiers
against Indians . The 'martial races' myth — cultivated since 1857 — held that certain Indian communities were inherently loyal to the
Crown. February 1946 shattered it: Indian sailors + airmen turned against British command, not as isolated incidents but as coordinated,
politicised acts of defiance . Once that instrument cracked — visibly, publicly, and with political consciousness — the game was over. The
armed forces, the last reliable instrument of British control , were showing cracks. It is widely seen as one of the key factors that
convinced the British that the transfer of power could not be postponed .

sections.title: Plan Balkan / Ismay Plan / Dickie Bird Plan (April 1947)

phases.label: SEC. 1–2 — RAJAJI FORMULA (C.R. FORMULA), 1944 + COLLAPSE OF THE TALKS

events.label: RAJAJI FORMULA (C.R. FORMULA) 1944 — THREE PLANKS: (1) @ Swaraj: ML1906 should support the goal of PURNA SWARAJ ; (2) @ Transfer of Power: INC + ML1906 should be ready to form a COALITION GOVERNMENT AT THE CENTRE ; (3) @ Unity: AFTER THE WAR, a PLEBISCITE in Muslim-majority regions on the question of partition — if the vote is in favour, the result would be a CONFEDERATION = weak common centre + strong provinces (*link forward to CMP1946 + Syed Ahmed Khan's Two-Nation, One-State theory); Prelims 1998

GANDHI–JINNAH TALKS COLLAPSE — Jinnah's demands were very different from what Rajagopalachari had proposed: (i) voting on partition should be on SEPARATE ELECTORATES (only Muslims would vote); (ii) the outcome should be a FULLY SEPARATE, INDEPENDENT PAKISTAN — NOT Two Nations One State, but TWO NATIONS, TWO STATES ; (iii) all of it implemented BEFORE the British left (Jinnah did not trust INC to honour any agreement once in power); THE FORMULA FAILED COMPLETELY — but it had shown Jinnah EXACTLY HOW FAR INC WAS WILLING TO BEND , and he found the answer useful; Prelims 2003

DESAI-LIAQAT PACT 1945 — negotiated + finalised by BULLABHAI DESAI + LIAQAT ALI KHAN , leaders of INC + ML1906 in the Central Legislative Assembly (CLA) ; goal same as the Rajaji Formula: build INC-ML unity + present JOINT DEMANDS to the British (like LP1916) for a smoother transfer of power; TWO PROPOSALS: (i) in the VEC , ALL ministers to be Indians EXCEPT the Governor General + the Commander-in-Chief; of these Indian ministers, 50% INC + 50% ML1906 ; (ii) in the Central Legislature , 20% of seats reserved for MINORITIES (esp Dalits + Sikhs), remaining seats split EQUALLY between INC + ML1906 — filled initially by NOMINATION , with elections (direct or indirect) to follow; Prelims 2010

WHY IT FAILED — Gandhi WAS aware of the pact. It failed because JINNAH REFUSED TO ACKNOWLEDGE ANY KNOWLEDGE OF IT (*he was testing how far INC could bend; now he had a MINIMUM BASE — any future negotiation would have to offer ML1906 something even more); EACH CONCESSION WAS NOT BUILDING GOODWILL — IT

SHIMLA CONFERENCE June 1945 — the Wavell Plan is discussed; held after the RELEASE OF INC LEADERS imprisoned during the QIM (1942–45) — the release also formally ENDED THE QIM ; TIMING driven by British domestic politics: CHURCHILL wanted visible progress on the India problem BEFORE ELECTIONS IN BRITAIN ; the plan was based closely on the DESAI-LIAQAT PACT (1945) — because INC + ML1906 had already agreed on it in principle, making rapid acceptance likely; also, any change to the VEC could be made swiftly at the behest of the Governor General; Prelims 1996 + 1998

WAVELL PLAN — PROPOSALS: (i) in the VEC , all ministers Indian except the Governor General + the C-i-C ; 50% of Indian ministers Hindus + 50% Muslims ; (ii) the Governor General / Viceroy would rule on the aid + advice of ministers BUT RETAIN VETO POWER ; (iii) the portfolio of FOREIGN AFFAIRS offered to Indians (*recall Cripps Mission 1942 had already offered foreign policy to Indians — consistent with that); (iv) a JOINT LIST of names for ministership to be submitted by the parties — if a joint list was not possible, each party would submit a separate list

WHY IT FAILED — the plan collapsed on a SINGLE POINT : ML1906 insisted that Muslim ministers in the VEC come ONLY from ML1906 — NOT from INC, which had its own Muslim leaders; ML1906 REJECTED the plan when Wavell4347 refused to guarantee this; INC refused ML's demand, arguing INC was not a Hindu organisation + that Muslim leaders of INC also had the right to be ministers; Wavell announced the failure, saying ML could not be convinced — in effect an IMPLICIT VETO given to ML1906 on the question of transfer of power; the announcement BOOSTED ML1906's PRESTIGE ENORMOUSLY ; Prelims 2000
CLEMENT ATLEE becomes British PM (July 1945) after Churchill loses the elections

JAPAN SURRENDERS 15 August 1945 → the INA TRIALS then begin (Red Fort: Prem Sehgal + Shah Nawaz Khan + Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon), generating remarkable communal unity during the INA agitations of 1945–46 (*link Ch 45); Prelims 2007

DECEMBER 1945 ELECTIONS to the PLAs — (i) INC gets a majority EVERYWHERE EXCEPT Bengal, Punjab, Sindh ; (ii) in PUNJAB INC forms a coalition government with the AKALIS + the UNIONIST PARTY ; (iii) ML1906 does very well in seats reserved for Muslims + gets a majority in BENGAL + SINDH ; INC gets a majority in NWFP + ASSAM (*NWFP: the poor Muslim masses supported KHAN ABDUL GAFFAR KHAN — the Frontier Gandhi — and his KHUDAI KHIDMATGARS / Red Shirts , since INC had their support from the Khilafat Movement 1920–24; the elite Khans were pro-ML1906. *Assam: only 31% Muslim , concentrated mainly in the SYLHET district where Muslims were in majority)

CABINET MISSION ARRIVES IN INDIA February 1946 — three members: LORD PETHICK-LAWRENCE (Secretary of State for India) + SIR STAFFORD CRIPPS (President of the Board of Trade) + A.V. ALEXANDER (First Lord of the Admiralty); ON THE SAME DAY the NAVAL MUTINY broke out in BOMBAY (*the timing was not a coincidence — it was a signal)

WHY DID THE BRITISH NOW OFFER A UNITED INDIA? The sequence had shaken them badly: QIM (1942–45) → INA agitations (1945–46) → Naval Mutiny (1946) ; the British realised that if the Cabinet Mission failed, the NEXT MOVEMENT WOULD OVERTHROW THEM VIOLENTLY — they no longer had confidence in the loyalty of the Indian military ; add to this that in three decades THREE EVENTS HAD WRECKED THE BRITISH ECONOMY: WWI (1914–19) OFFERED A UNITED INDIA + PURNA SWARAJ ; (@ Cold War — begun 1945; Britain wanted a strong, friendly India for influence in South Asia post-decolonisation; a partition would be a diplomatic failure )

phases.label: + the GREAT DEPRESSION (1929) + WWII (1939–45) ; CMP1946 = THE ONLY PROPOSAL WHERE THE BRITISH

events.label: ATLEE'S ANTI-PARTITION STATEMENT March 1946 — 'a minority won't be allowed veto over majority' ; a DIRECT REVERSAL of the August Offer (1940) + Cripps Mission (1942) + Wavell Plan (1945) — all three of which had, in effect, given ML1906 exactly that veto

CMP1946 — PROPOSALS (goal: peaceful transfer of executive power at the Centre + setting up a CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY (CA) ; a 'ONE STATE, TWO NATION' solution): (i) a WEAK COMMON CENTRE handling only THREE UNION SUBJECTS — DEFENCE + COMMUNICATIONS + FOREIGN AFFAIRS ; all other subjects + residual powers with the PROVINCES = effectively a CONFEDERATION (link Rajaji Formula 1944); (ii) NO two Constituent Assemblies + NO veto to ML1906 — but the British would not accept a constitution not based on INC-ML consensus; (iii) provinces divided into THREE SECTIONS: A = Hindu-majority provinces; B = Muslim-majority provinces of the WEST (NWFP, Punjab, Sindh); C = Muslim-majority provinces of the EAST, i.e. Bengal ( ASSAM placed in Section C though only 31% Muslim — because SYLHET district had a Muslim majority); (iv) each section frames its OWN GROUP CONSTITUTION for all subjects except the three union subjects (*effectively Art. 370 for all 11 provinces, grouped into three sections — meeting Jinnah's 14-Point demands of March 1929 in spirit); (v) the UNION CONSTITUTION framed by a CA of nominees of the Princely States + elected members from the PLAs ; (vi) the CA to be POPULATED BY AUGUST 1946 ; (vii) future changes to constitutions only AFTER 10 YEARS (= a united India guaranteed for at least a decade); (viii) after general elections a province COULD COME OUT of its group ; (ix) FULL INDEPENDENCE once the constitution is drafted; (x) @ Transfer of Power: immediate transfer of executive power to an INTERIM GOVERNMENT at the Centre; (xi) an ADVISORY COMMITTEE on the rights of citizens, Tribals + minorities; (xii) any decision on a major COMMUNAL QUESTION in the Central Legislature needs a majority of BOTH Hindu + Muslim members plus an overall majority. (*CA = Group A + B + C + nominees of Princely States; MAX no. of constitutions = one per Princely State + 3 group + 1 union; MINIMUM = 3 group + 1 union = 4 ); Prelims 1996×2 + 1999 + 2000 + 2002×3 + 2003 + 2004 + 2013

THE DEBATE ON CMP1946 — THE CENTRAL FAULT-LINE: INC thought GROUPING WAS VOLUNTARY; ML1906 thought it was COMPULSORY. (i) ML1906 wanted the right to question the UNION constitution IMMEDIATELY — not after 10 years — since it would establish a united India; (ii) INC argued grouping was NOT compulsory : groups may be created but a province should not be COMPELLED to join a prescribed group (INC was in power in NWFP + ASSAM and did not want them following the constitutions of Group B + Group C); ML1906 argued — and THE BRITISH AGREED — that grouping was COMPULSORY for all Muslim-majority provinces; ML's logic: if grouping is compulsory, PARTITION IS IMPLICIT within the plan (*explicit partition = two separate states; implicit partition = one state, two nations, i.e. a Pakistan WITHIN India in the form of Group B + Group C); the British clarification that grouping was compulsory gave Jinnah the trigger ; (iii) INC also wanted ELECTED representatives from the Princely States in the CA (as it had demanded during Cripps 1942)
INC DECIDES (July 1946) that NWFP + ASSAM will NOT join Group B + Group C respectively; NEHRU further states (July 1946) that the ONLY BINDING decision of the Cabinet Mission is the FORMATION OF A

DIRECT ACTION DAY 16 August 1946 — ML1906 REJECTS CMP1946 , refuses to join the Interim Government + the Constituent Assembly, and gives the call for DIRECT ACTION for the creation of Pakistan; leads to COMMUNAL RIOTS IN CALCUTTA — 5,000 people die in a single week :( ; Prelims 2013

INTERIM GOVERNMENT formed September 1946 with J.L. NEHRU as Prime Minister ; LATER ML1906 DID join the Interim Government — NOT out of agreement, but out of FEAR : it did not want INC holding executive power at the Centre without them; ML1906 got the FINANCE MINISTRY + used it to ensure the government COULD NOT FUNCTION
BRITISH TAKE A STAND FOR TWO CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLIES, 6 December 1946 — stating that if ML1906-ruled provinces did not join the CA, the constitution framed by it would NOT apply to those provinces
CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY CONVENES 9 December 1946 — with DR SACHCHIDANANDA SINHA as its
DR RAJENDRA PRASAD elected PERMANENT PRESIDENT of the Constituent Assembly, 11 December 1946 ; Prelims 2024
ML1906 DEMANDS DISSOLUTION of the Constituent Assembly (February 1947) — on the ground that it is not truly representative

ATLEE STATEMENT February 1947 — in effect a PRO-BALKANISATION statement , very much like the Cripps Mission (1942) before it (*Cripps had given provinces the option to NOT join the Union); Atlee states that BY 30 JUNE 1948 THE BRITISH WILL LEAVE INDIA — WITH OR WITHOUT A CONSTITUTION (= a deliberate THREAT OF ANARCHY designed to force INC + ML1906 into a compromise); THE DETAILS WERE FAR MORE DAMAGING: (6.1) the PRINCELY STATES (all 565) were NOT to be under any future Government of India — PARAMOUNTCY would LAPSE + NOT be transferred to the successor govt = effectively 565 independent countries ; power would be transferred to the Interim Government under Nehru AND to the provincial governments of provinces that had NOT joined the CA (= such provinces could, in effect, become independent); (6.2) MOUNTBATTEN (MTB) would replace Wavell4347 = a VICTORY FOR ML1906 ; widespread communal violence followed + the INC–Akali–Unionist coalition government in PUNJAB was overthrown by direct action led by Muslims under ML1906; Prelims 1998

phases.label: SEC. 7 — PLAN BALKAN / ISMAY PLAN / DICKIE BIRD PLAN (April 1947)

events.label: PLAN BALKAN / ISMAY PLAN / DICKIE BIRD PLAN April 1947 (by Mountbatten — 'Dickie' was MTB's nickname; Ismay was a member of his committee) — proposed a VOLUNTARY UNION on the model of the UNITED STATES : independence to EACH province + EACH Princely State ; PUNJAB + BENGAL given the option of partition; every province + Princely State free to join or not join the CA for a united India; in effect it proposed transferring power to 11 INDIVIDUAL PROVINCES separately ; NEHRU VIOLENTLY OPPOSED it as the 'BALKANIZATION' of India — opposed it immediately; IT WAS NOT DISCUSSED FURTHER ; Prelims 1999

MTB'S BRIEF + CONCLUSION — Mountbatten had been given a deadline of OCTOBER 1947 to explore options for unity + partition; within TWO MONTHS he concluded that CMP1946 + the idea of a united India were DEAD HORSES — entirely due to Jinnah ; British national interest now pointed differently: better to have TWO COUNTRIES FRIENDLY TO BRITAIN than to risk an unfriendly Pakistan created by direct action or civil war; as Atlee later stated, 'Britain wanted a united India, tried but failed' (*1st choice = India as a colony; 2nd = a friendly united India; 3rd + now the only realistic one = a friendly India + a friendly Pakistan); [*the harder point: partition was AVOIDABLE if the British had acted against communal violence rather than playing the passive role of mediator between INC + ML1906 — they chose the passive role, because it served British national interest]

3rd JUNE PLAN / MOUNTBATTEN PLAN — gives DOMINION STATUS to BOTH India + Pakistan , keeping both in the BRITISH COMMONWEALTH , even if temporarily (*the Commonwealth = the network of British colonies with a special economic relationship with Britain; membership translated into trade + business benefits for British firms ; dominion status = a political victory for the British government among the British people ); SINCE INC AGREED TO SMALL AS POSSIBLE , with an informal promise that the 565 Princely States would NOT be given independence ; (ii) a STRONG CENTRE for India (unitary structure — like the Nehru Report 1928 + UNLIKE the Rajaji Formula 1944); (iii) the British would EXIT IN 72 DAYS from 3rd June, i.e. on 15 AUGUST 1947 — ONE YEAR AHEAD of the deadline set in the Atlee Statement

phases.label: PARTITION + DOMINION STATUS, ALL OTHER INC DEMANDS WERE ACCEPTED: (i) PAKISTAN TO BE AS

events.label: THE MECHANICS OF PARTITION — in PUNJAB + BENGAL , a SIMPLE MAJORITY of EITHER the Hindu OR the Muslim members of the PLAs in favour of partition would lead to partition (*the decision on partition was thus taken by the two big Muslim-majority provinces); the remaining question was which areas would join Pakistan: (i) a PLEBISCITE in SINDH ; (ii) a REFERENDUM in NWFP + in the SYLHET district of Assam ; (iii) VOTING BY POLITICAL LEADERS in BALUCHISTAN (*INC had won the Dec 1945 elections in NWFP + Assam — a REFERENDUM was chosen there to get a clear, direct answer from the people: a plebiscite seeks a NON-BINDING opinion; a referendum is BINDING ); if the votes favoured partition, the CA set up by the Cabinet Mission would be SPLIT INTO TWO CAs for two dominions + power transferred to TWO CENTRES by 15 AUGUST 1947 = 'THE APPOINTED DAY' (*this is why India became an 'INDESTRUCTIBLE UNION OF DESTRUCTIBLE STATES' — power was transferred only to the Union at the Centre; the provinces did not separately decide to form a union, as in the USA)

THE VOTES — INC + ML1906 BOTH ACCEPT the Mountbatten Plan; the votes come out IN FAVOUR OF PARTITION in PUNJAB + BENGAL ; NWFP + SINDH + BALUCHISTAN + SYLHET vote to join PAKISTAN ; (* FRONTIER GANDHI — Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan — BOYCOTTED the referendum + passed the BANNU RESOLUTION in JUNE 1947 , demanding an independent PAKHTONISTAN for the Pashtuns; NWFP's vote therefore went in favour of Pakistan — because the followers of Frontier Gandhi did not vote ; Pakistan BANNED the Khudai Khidmatgars in 1948 ; 'Pakhto' = the Pakhtun code of life; some Pashtuns wanted to join Afghanistan; today NWFP is called Khyber Pakhtunwa )

BOUNDARY COMMISSION — TWO commissions set up to demarcate borders in the WEST (Punjab) + the EAST (Bengal) ; BOTH headed by SIR CYRIL RADCLIFFE , a British jurist WHO HAD NEVER BEEN TO INDIA ; each commission had FOUR judges — two nominated by INC + two by ML1906 — completely DEADLOCKED on partisan lines ; the boundary lines were therefore RADCLIFFE'S UNILATERAL DECISION
THE RADCLIFFE LINE ANNOUNCED 17 August 1947 — TWO DAYS AFTER INDEPENDENCE — ensuring MAXIMUM CHAOS during the transfer of power :(

INDIAN INDEPENDENCE ACT, July 1947 — gives LEGAL STATUS to the Mountbatten Plan ; KEY PROVISIONS: (10.1) PARTITION of British India into TWO INDEPENDENT DOMINIONS — independent of each other — on the appointed day, 15 AUGUST 1947 ; (10.2) each dominion headed by a GOVERNOR GENERAL appointed by the King ; the SAME GG would serve BOTH dominions until their respective CAs passed a law for a separate GG ( Pakistan decided JINNAH would be its GG ); (10.3) the CAs of the two dominions could pass constitutions ENDING DOMINION STATUS (the CA of India did so on 26 JANUARY 1950 ); (10.4) END of the jurisdiction of the BRITISH PARLIAMENT over British India + END OF PARAMOUNTCY over the 565 Princely States on the appointed day — Paramountcy NOT to be transferred to any government in the two dominions (= legally, each of the 565 Princely States had the right to independence ); (10.5) ABOLITION of the title 'EMPEROR OF INDIA' + abolition of the office of the SECRETARY OF STATE FOR INDIA (created in 1858); (10.6) until the passage of a new constitution, the GOI ACT 1935 would apply ; (10.7) territories of India + Pakistan to be determined 'BEFORE OR AFTER' the appointed day by a boundary commission appointed by the GG
India was a DOMINION of Britain from 15 AUGUST 1947 until 26 JANUARY 1950 — when our Constitution came into effect

phases.label: SEC. 9 — INTEGRATION OF THE PRINCELY STATES

events.label: 565 officially recognised PRINCELY STATES in the subcontinent — approx 40% of the landmass + about 23% of the population ; the Indian Independence Act (July 1947) ended British PARAMOUNTCY over all 565, legally freeing each to choose independence = one of the gravest challenges facing the new Indian state

PATEL + MENON — SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL , as head of the STATES DEPARTMENT , with V.P. MENON as its Secretary, undertakes the integration; of the 565 states, 552 were geographically CONTIGUOUS to the Dominion of India; through persuasion + pressure + appeals to patriotism , 549 states signed the INSTRUMENT OF ACCESSION by or shortly after 15 August 1947
JAMMU & KASHMIR accedes to India ( October 1947 ) following an invasion by Pakistani-backed tribal militias
JUNAGADH integrated ( February 1948 ) following a public PLEBISCITE in which the overwhelming majority voted to join India — after its Nawab had initially attempted to accede to Pakistan
HYDERABAD integrated ( September 1948 ) following a military operation known as 'OPERATION POLO'

THE FINAL COUNT — all 552 states contiguous to India joined the Indian Union; the remaining 13 Princely States (contiguous to Pakistan's borders) acceded to the Dominion of Pakistan: Bahawalpur (Punjab), Khairpur (Sindh), the Khanate of Kalat + Makran + Las Bela + Kharan (Balochistan), and Swat + Chitral + Hunza + Nagar + Amb + Phulra + Dir (North-West Frontier / Gilgit). 552 + 13 = 565. [* NOTE ON NUMBERS: ' 562 princely states' is one of the most widely repeated factual errors on the internet — the Butler Committee Report (1927) cited 562, but 565 is the final accepted count at the time of British withdrawal. Authoritative source = the WHITE PAPER ON INDIAN STATES (1950) , published by the Ministry of States under Patel + Menon, read with the Indian Independence Act (July 1947): 565 → 552 to India (549 by accession + 3 subsequently integrated) → 13 to Pakistan ]

BRITISH DIVIDE & RULE (i): Hunter's 'INDIAN MUSALMANS' (1871) argued that British neglect of Muslims had contributed to the Faraisi movement (1830–70s) — planting the idea that Muslims were a SEPARATE, NEGLECTED POLITICAL CATEGORY requiring special attention

DnR (ii): CENSUS 1881 — contributed to a sense of HOMOGENEOUS RELIGIOUS IDENTITY among Hindus + Muslims (communities that were in reality internally very heterogeneous); by publishing religion-based statistics + reports , the government brought religious identity into the domain of public policy + governance
DnR (iii): RESERVATION IN GOVERNMENT JOBS FOR MUSLIMS (1897)
DnR (iv): BENGAL PARTITION (1905) — creating a Muslim-majority province + rewarding elite Muslims
DnR (v) + (vi): the positive response of MINTO05-10 to the SIMLA DEPUTATION (1906) → the FORMATION OF ML1906
DnR (vii): SEPARATE ELECTORATES for Muslims under ICA 1909
DnR (viii): in the AUGUST OFFER (1940) and the WAVELL PLAN (1945) , ML1906 was given a VETO on constitutional progress

ROLE OF WEMC MUSLIMS — Muslim organisations led by SYED AHMED KHAN gave the TWO-NATION THEORY , labelled INC a Hindu organisation, demanded reservation + special status for the Muslim Quam , and supported the British in return; the four DELHI PROPOSALS (December 1927) + the three CALCUTTA AMENDMENTS (December 1928) all FAILED → Jinnah issued the 14-POINT DEMANDS (March 1929) , which became the BLUEPRINT for all future ML1906 politics ; ML also opposed CDM (1930–34) + QIM (1942–45) , reducing Muslim participation in the INM
HINDU REVIVALISM (i): the SHUDDHI movement + the COW PROTECTION movement of the ARYA SAMAJ became AGGRESSIVE after the death of SWAMI DAYANAND SARASWATI (1883)

HINDU REVIVALISM (ii): COW-KILLING RIOTS (1893) — INC DID NOT CONDEMN them, because of its 1886 rule that INC would not take up social issues; Muslim participation in INC DECLINED thereafter + INC did not do much to reclaim Muslim leadership

HINDU REVIVALISM (iii): the HINDI-URDU CONTROVERSY in the North-West Provinces + Awadh (set up 1877) — impact = the identification of HINDI with HINDUS + URDU with MUSLIMS = a cultural fault-line that deepened communal identity

SWADESHI hurt Muslim participation — heavy use of HINDU RELIGIOUS SYMBOLISM , depiction of Muslims + the British as partners in Jatras , and a social boycott that hurt poorer communities disproportionately; ML1906 + the ULAMAS actively discouraged Muslim participation ROLE OF INC — (i) Cripps Mission (1942): INC accepted PROVINCIAL AUTONOMY for Muslim-majority provinces (like Art. 370); (ii) MG–Jinnah talks on the Rajaji Formula (1944): INC agreed to a PLEBISCITE for 'partition without independence' — partially conceding the right of self-determination of MMPs ; (iii) CMP1946: INC opposed only COMPULSORY grouping — NOT the idea of grouping itself; (iv) INC first explicitly mentioned PARTITION in MARCH 1947 — stating that Punjab + Bengal would have to be partitioned if the country was divided (months before the 3rd June Plan)

THE VERDICT — per BIPIN CHANDRA , INC failed on TWO counts: it failed to bring Muslims into the INM as a MASS CONSTITUENCY , and it failed to CURB MUSLIM COMMUNAL FORCES — especially from 1937 onwards; the proof is stark: ML1906 won 90% of Muslim seats in the 1945 elections to PLAs ; by June 1947 INC had given up on a united India — defeated by communal violence + the failure of the Interim Government + ML's refusal to join the CA (August 1946) ; even the Bengal government of ML1906 promoted communal riots; TWO FALSE BELIEFS proved costly: (a) that partition would be TEMPORARY (MG told INC: 'don't accept partition in your hearts' — but hearts do not make borders ); (b) that APPEASEMENT of ML1906 would reduce the fear-of-majority complex — instead every concession increased ML's prestige + brought it closer to its goal; Gandhi could not start a movement against partition — communalism had spread too far; he stated that Hindus + Sikhs also desired partition , which made Muslims hate him + made Hindus + Sikhs abandon him; by mid-1947 GANDHI WAS ALONE — MTB later called him a 'ONE-MAN BOUNDARY FORCE' against communal violence; THEREFORE the 3rd June Plan was a COMPULSION, NOT A

anchors: The One Fault-Line That Runs Through Everything — Confederation vs a Strong Centre: Rajaji Formula (1944) offered a
confederation . CMP1946 offered a weak centre with three subjects and compulsory grouping = a One-State, Two-Nation solution
(what Syed Ahmed Khan had hinted at decades earlier). Plan Balkan (April 1947) offered 11 separate provinces . Every one of these was
some version of a weak centre . INC accepted partition in the 3rd June Plan precisely because — having agreed to partition + dominion
status — it finally got what it had wanted throughout: a STRONG UNITARY CENTRE (the Nehru Report 1928 model). Partition was the price
of the strong centre. This is also why India is an 'indestructible union of destructible states' : power was transferred only to the Union at
the Centre — the provinces never separately decided to form a union, as in the USA.
Raising Jinnah's Floor — the Arithmetic of Concession: Each INC concession was not building goodwill. It was setting a new minimum
from which Jinnah would begin the next negotiation. Lucknow Pact (1916) conceded separate electorates. The Rajaji Formula (1944)
conceded a plebiscite on partition — and told Jinnah exactly how far INC would bend. The Desai-Liaqat Pact (1945) conceded 50:50 parity
in the VEC — and Jinnah then denied all knowledge of it, keeping the concession while giving nothing back. The Wavell Plan (1945) and the
August Offer (1940) handed ML1906 an effective veto on constitutional progress . By 1946, ML's floor was so high that the only plan
offering a united India — CMP1946 — could not clear it. Every concession by INC increased the prestige of ML1906 and brought it closer to
its goal.
