chapters.title: Many Voices of the Nation: Workers, Capitalists, Dalits, Women, Peasants

sections.title: The Role of Indian Capitalists in the INM

events.label: SASIPADA BANNERJEE , a Brahmo Samajist reformer, sets up a WORKING MEN'S CLUB + launches the monthly journal BHARAT SHRAMJEEVI (1870) — the earliest sign of organised effort (*the modern Indian worker did not exist in meaningful numbers before the 2nd half of the 19th c.; railways + telegraphs + textile mills brought this class into being)
NARAYAN LOKHANDE starts the Anglo-Marathi weekly DEEN BANDHU (1880)

FACTORY ACTS 1881 + 1891 — reduced working hours; the MODERATES OPPOSED them because reduced hours raised costs for Indian mill owners already under pressure; (*the Acts were pushed by the LANCASHIRE TEXTILE LOBBY in Britain — stricter labour regulation in India raised Indian production costs + reduced the competitiveness of Indian textiles. The British were not regulating Indian factories out of sympathy for Indian workers — but out of fear of Indian competition)

Moderates STRONGLY BACK workers in the ASSAM TEA GARDENS (British-owned) — the ONE consistent exception to their position: where the employer was BRITISH, INC engaged; where the employer was INDIAN, INC stood aside DADABHAI NAOROJI formalises at the 1886 INC session that the Congress will NOT take up issues that could set Indians against one another (*if INC took a strongly pro-peasant stand it risked antagonising the zamindars who were also part of the nationalist coalition — a strategic position, not a moral failing; but it would cost the INC dearly with Dalits + peasants + workers for decades)
Lokhande sets up the BOMBAY MILLS & MILL HANDS ASSOCIATION (1890) — a PHILANTHROPIC body for workers' welfare, NOT a trade union in the modern sense
SIGNALLERS' STRIKE in the GREAT INDIAN PENINSULAR (GIP) RAILWAYS — THE FIRST ORGANISED INDUSTRIAL STRIKE IN INDIA ; the INC SUPPORTED it (the employer was British)

SWADESHI = THE TURNING POINT — Extremists ( Lal + Bal + Pal + Aurobindo Ghosh ) argue INC must take up the issues of ALL workers if the INM is to become a genuine mass movement; important strikes in foreign enterprises led by CR DAS + BC PAL + LIAQUAT HUSSAIN ; the FIRST ATTEMPT at an ALL-INDIA UNION of workers is made (it did not succeed, but reflected a new political awareness); for the first time workers are drawn into the INM (*before Swadeshi a mill worker's political horizon was largely his mill; Swadeshi expanded it to the nation) RUSSIAN REVOLUTION 1905 — the visible role of workers in it impresses the Extremist leadership; they see organised labour as a potential source of strength for the INM = the cautious beginning of SOCIALIST THINKING entering INC circles

TILAK TRIAL 1908 — Tilak tried for sedition for writing in KESARI in support of PRAFULLA CHAKI + KHUDIRAM BOSE (Muzaffarpur Conspiracy Case, 1908); ONE OF THE LARGEST WORKING CLASS DEMONSTRATIONS in India to that point takes place in his support (Bombay textile workers' strike)

REVIVAL DURING WORLD WAR I — wartime INFLATION ERODES THE REAL WAGES of industrial workers; workers already at the lower end find their position worse Workers participate actively in the HOME RULE LEAGUE MOVEMENT (HRL, 1916–18) RUSSIAN REVOLUTION (OCTOBER 1917) — demonstrates that organised workers can be a decisive political force ; prompts the formation of communist parties across the world

AHMEDABAD MILL STRIKE 1918 — led by MAHATMA GANDHI ; mill owners (incl AMBALAL SARABHAI ) resisted; Gandhi sided with the workers on the principle of a LIVING WAGE , but his method of ARBITRATION was specifically designed to PREVENT class conflict from escalating ; produced the TEXTILE LABOUR ASSOCIATION (TLA, 1920) in Ahmedabad — an early working model of Gandhian arbitration between labour + capital
MADRAS LABOUR UNION (1918) , founded by B.P. WADIA — THE FIRST MODERN ORGANISED TRADE UNION IN INDIA
Workers among the main participants in the ROWLATT SATYAGRAHA (1919)

AITUC (ALL INDIA TRADE UNION CONGRESS) FORMED 1920 — the FIRST all-India organisation of workers in Indian history ; leadership of LALA LAJPAT RAI (first president; founder = N.M. JOSHI ); represented India at the ILO of the League of Nations from the outset; LAJPAT RAI = THE FIRST INDIAN LEADER TO EXPLICITLY CONNECT IMPERIALISM WITH CAPITALISM — arguing colonial rule + capitalist exploitation were parts of a single structure (*a colony = a reliable source of cheap raw materials + a captive market for the coloniser's industries; the economic interests of the colonial power + its business class are therefore aligned)
CPI FIRST ESTABLISHED IN TASHKENT (Uzbekistan, USSR) in 1920 by M.N. ROY + ABANI MUKHERJI + others

NCM — strikes spread across multiple sectors; JM SEN GUPTA leads strikes in railways + steamer services + tea plantations in Assam ; workers also strike during the visit of the PRINCE OF WALES (November 1921) INC GAYA SESSION 1922 — THE CHANGE OF POSITION : CR DAS argues that if INC keeps ignoring the grievances of workers + peasants, they will launch INDEPENDENT CLASS-BASED MOVEMENTS (workers vs capitalists, peasants vs landlords) that will FRAGMENT THE NATIONAL COALITION ; the only way to hold the movement together is to bring their demands WITHIN the nationalist programme ; INC ACCEPTS — formally welcomes the AITUC + begins supporting workers' + peasants' issues; GANDHI offers TRUSTEESHIP + ARBITRATION as the middle path (*Gandhi's approach was not anti-capitalist; it was an attempt to make capitalism compatible with a broadly equitable social order)
M. SINGARAVELU CHETTIAR (Madras) = the FIRST to celebrate MAY DAY in India (1923)
KANPUR BOLSHEVIK CONSPIRACY CASE 1924 — S.A. DANGE + MUZAFFAR AHMAD + SHAUKAT USMANI imprisoned

CPI SET UP WITHIN INDIA at the KANPUR CONFERENCE, December 1925 — to unite scattered communist groups into a single legal party ; key leaders S.V. GHATE + M. SINGARAVELU CHETTIAR (presided over the Kanpur session); SATYABHAKTA convened it but wanted a purely 'nationalist' communist party independent of the Comintern — he was OUTVOTED by Ghate + Singaravelu and resigned shortly after; the THREE TALLEST LEADERS of CPI (1925–47) = S.A. DANGE (West/Bombay) + MUZAFFAR AHMAD (East/Bengal) + P.C. JOSHI (organisation)

TRADE UNION ACT 1926 — a landmark: gave LEGAL RECOGNITION to trade unions for the first time , protected union funds from arbitrary seizure, and granted IMMUNITY to members + office-bearers for legitimate strike action; transformed trade unionism from an informal, legally vulnerable activity into a recognised institution with enforceable rights (*the irony: the same colonial govt that sought to suppress labour through the Meerut Case + the Trade Disputes Bill also felt compelled to give it legal standing — partly under ILO pressure, partly to channel agitation into regulated forms)

WORKERS & PEASANTS PARTIES (WPPs) set up within the INC structure from early 1927 , under the communist leader SA DANGE ; by 1928 an ALL-INDIA WPP had been formed — communist influence within the Congress now a visible + growing factor

BOMBAY TEXTILE STRIKES 1928 — S.A. DANGE'S defining moment : a massive SIX-MONTH-LONG strike ; he builds the GIRNI KAMGAR UNION (GKU) into one of the most formidable + militant trade unions in Indian history (*Dange authored 'Gandhi vs. Lenin' (1921) + founded 'The Socialist' , the first communist journal in India)
Substantial working class participation in the ANTI-SIMON COMMISSION AGITATIONS (October 1928)

6th WORLD CONGRESS OF THE COMINTERN (1928) — directs communist parties worldwide to OPPOSE ALL NON-COMMUNIST POLITICAL FORCES → the CPI1925 declares the INC a party of the BOURGEOISIE + describes NEHRU + BOSE as representatives of propertied class interests; THE CPI THEREBY SEVERED ITSELF FROM THE LARGEST MASS MOVEMENT IN INDIA — and made it far easier for the British to suppress it

THE BRITISH COUNTER-OFFENSIVE — the PUBLIC SAFETY BILL (1929) gave the govt powers of DEPORTATION ; the TRADE DISPUTES BILL (1929) imposed significant restrictions on labour action; ( u this was the context for the bomb thrown in the CENTRAL LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY on 8 APRIL 1929 by BHAGAT SINGH + BK DUTT — the Assembly was that day discussing THESE VERY BILLS ; the action was designed to be HEARD, NOT TO KILL )

MEERUT CONSPIRACY CASE (1929–1933) — a large number of communists, incl foreign nationals , arrested under SECTION 121A of the IPC (1860) , charged with conspiracy to deprive the King of sovereignty over British India; immediate triggers = ongoing railway strikes + attempts to establish a COMINTERN branch in India; MUZAFFAR AHMAD was the prime accused — he used the courtroom as a massive PROPAGANDA PLATFORM to broadcast communist ideology + demand complete independence; the trial dragged on for years + significantly weakened the communist + workers' movement organisationally WHITLEY COMMISSION (ROYAL COMMISSION ON LABOUR, 1929) , chaired by JH WHITLEY , with six Indian members incl GD BIRLA + NM JOSHI ; REPORT SUBMITTED 1931 : found POVERTY the root cause of India's industrial problems + was critical of British employers' role; RECOMMENDED legal recognition of trade unions + the right to collective bargaining , standardised wages in cotton + jute, works committees at factory level, conciliation officers , and systematic collection of labour statistics; its recommendations on TRIPARTITE consultative bodies laid the foundation of the INDIAN LABOUR CONFERENCE ; implementation under colonial rule was limited, but the report became the BLUEPRINT for the FACTORIES ACT (1948) + MINIMUM WAGES ACT (1948)

CPI1925 OPPOSES THE CDM — characterises the goal of Swaraj as ILLUSORY + presents the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) as evidence that INC had compromised the national cause; the INC meanwhile declares workers the 'HANDS & FEET' of the movement; workers DID participate — but the CPI's stance meant participation fell well short of its potential; NONETHELESS: after Gandhi's arrest in MAY 1930 , textile workers in SHOLAPUR launch strikes serious enough that the British impose MARTIAL LAW ; GIP railway workers LIE DOWN ON THE TRACKS to stop trains CONGRESS SOCIALIST PARTY (CSP, 1934) formed inside the INC by JAYAPRAKASH NARAYAN + MINOO MASANI + ACHARYA NARENDRA DEV — critical of Gandhi + the INC leadership over the withdrawal of the CDM , but equally rejecting the CPI's decision to work AGAINST the Congress; their response = stay INSIDE the INC + shift it from within ; in the same year, the WPPs inside the INC were wound up by the communists themselves

7th WORLD CONGRESS OF THE COMINTERN (1935) — with the rise of HITLER + the threat of fascism, the Comintern directs communist parties to UNITE WITH ALL ANTI-FASCIST FORCES regardless of ideology ; under P.C. JOSHI (General Secretary of CPI, 1935–47 ) the CPI moves BACK into alignment with the INC + infiltrates the CSP to gain mass cadres; Joshi transforms the CPI from a fringe group into a disciplined pan-India machine + spearheads the IPTA (Indian People's Theatre Association) + the PWA (Progressive Writers' Association) , recruiting Kaifi Azmi + Mulk Raj Anand + Balraj Sahni to carry the anti-imperialist message to the rural masses through plays + songs

Communists build substantial PEASANT MOVEMENTS in KERALA + ANDHRA + BENGAL + PUNJAB — recovering much of the credibility lost in the early 1930s The period of INC PROVINCIAL MINISTRIES (1937–39) gives the working class movement a further lift, with AITUC actively supporting the INC in elections GERMANY ATTACKS THE SOVIET UNION (June 1941) → the CPI1925 declares WWII a 'PEOPLE'S WAR' + swings to SUPPORTING THE BRITISH WAR EFFORT — which meant formally OPPOSING the QIM (1942) ; this damaged the CPI's standing with the broader nationalist public considerably; even so, many individual communists + workers participated in the INM on their own initiative , regardless of the official party line
DECEMBER 1945 PROVINCIAL ELECTIONS confirm a landscape dominated by the INC + ML1906 ; smaller parties, including those of the left, fare POORLY = the CPI's political irrelevance made clear

THE INA VOLTE-FACE — during the war the CPI1925 had denounced Subhas Chandra Bose + the INA in the harshest terms (at one point comparing Netaji to 'TOJO'S DOG' ); the moment the war ended + the INA trials (1945–46) became a flashpoint of nationalist anger, the CPI was among those PARTICIPATING IN THE AGITATIONS in support of the very INA soldiers it had condemned (*after Dec 1945 had exposed its irrelevance, participation was as much about recovering lost standing as about principle) RIN MUTINY (February 1946) — when the ratings of the Royal Indian Navy mutiny in Bombay, the CPI1925 calls on Bombay's workers to STRIKE in solidarity = a moment where the labour movement + a section of the armed forces acted in public alignment (*link Ch 45)

Communists + workers lead popular agitations WITHIN the Princely States of TRAVANCORE + JUNAGARH + HYDERABAD (which declined to sign the Instrument of Accession), demanding democratic rights + integration with India — contributing to the political pressure that brought about accession (*link Ch 46) HIND MAZDOOR SABHA (HMS) founded at HOWRAH, 29 December 1948 by socialists + Forward Bloc unionists —

phases.label: SEC. 2 — THE ROLE OF INDIAN CAPITALISTS IN THE INM

events.label: CORE GRIEVANCES OF INDIAN CAPITAL — (i) British trade + tariff policy systematically favoured British manufacturers; (ii) heavy taxation , incl INCOME TAX introduced in 1868 despite famines ; (iii) restrictions on production of certain goods, incl low-grade steel ; (iv) preference to British firms in contracts + procurement ; (v) no developmental support or institutional credit from the state

THE TARIFF TRAP — for most of the 19th c. British textiles entered India virtually duty-free while Indian goods faced prohibitive duties in Britain ; when a modest IMPORT DUTY on cotton goods was introduced in 1894 , the LANCASHIRE LOBBY forced a matching COUNTERVAILING EXCISE DUTY on Indian mill-produced cloth — so that even domestic production received NO advantage

SWADESHI = THE MOST CAPITALIST-FRIENDLY PHASE OF THE INM (the demand was exactly what business wanted: buy Indian, boycott British) — PC RAY's Bengal Chemical Industries thrives; CHIDAMBARAM PILLAI's Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company challenges the British shipping monopoly on Indian coastal routes; TISCO (Tata Iron & Steel Company) set up by JAMSETJI TATA ; TILAK sets up Bombay Swadeshi Stores ; LALA LAJPAT RAI founds the Indian National Bank , later the Punjab National Bank (PNB) brings meaningful PROTECTIVE TARIFFS = Indian capitalists had, through sustained nationalist pressure, secured a concrete economic gain from the INM

AGAINST WORKER DEMANDS — the AHMEDABAD MILL STRIKE (1918) : mill owners incl AMBALAL SARABHAI resist; Gandhi mediates + sides with workers on a living wage, but his arbitration prevents class conflict from escalating ; the TLA (1920) is explicitly GANDHIAN — non-confrontational, focused on negotiation (*for capitalists, Gandhi's model of labour relations was the most comfortable version available: workers got some rights, but class war was avoided ; trusteeship they could accept — nationalisation or workers' control they could not) FUNDING THE MOVEMENT — JAMNALAL BAJAJ + GD BIRLA were personally close to Gandhi + funded his work consistently; Bajaj provided the land for the SABARMATI ASHRAM ; Birla funded Gandhi's activities + hosted him regularly; VAIDILAL MEHTA + other businessmen contributed to INC funds (*not purely selfless — a free India under INC leadership was likely to be far better for Indian industry than continued British rule)
events.full: 1918-20 1920s — AGAINST WORKER DEMANDS — the AHMEDABAD MILL STRIKE (1918) : mill owners incl AMBALAL SARABHAI resist; Gandhi mediates + sides with workers on a living wage, but his arbitration prevents class conflict from escalating ; the TLA (1920) is explicitly GANDHIAN — non-confrontational, focused on negotiation (*for capitalists, Gandhi's model of labour relations was the most comfortable version available: workers got some rights, but class war was avoided ; trusteeship they could accept — nationalisation or workers' control they could not) FUNDING THE MOVEMENT — JAMNALAL BAJAJ + GD BIRLA were personally close to Gandhi + funded his work consistently; Bajaj provided the land for the SABARMATI ASHRAM ; Birla funded Gandhi's activities + hosted him regularly; VAIDILAL MEHTA + other businessmen contributed to INC funds (*not purely selfless — a free India under INC leadership was likely to be far better for Indian industry than continued British rule)

events.label: THE CURRENCY GRIEVANCE — the high 1s 6d rupee fixed in 1926 (HILTON-YOUNG COMMISSION) suited British exporters but squeezed Indian producers; Indian businessmen pressed for a lower 1s 4d rate + set up a CURRENCY LEAGUE in Bombay (1926) , with the blessings of GANDHI + PATEL

FICCI (FEDERATION OF INDIAN CHAMBERS OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY) set up 1927 ( Purshotamdas Thakurdas + GD Birla ) — the organised voice of Indian business; FICCI REFUSED to negotiate with the British government on constitutional or economic issues WITHOUT the approval or participation of the INC (*India's big business lobby had effectively made the INC its political representative)

GANDHI makes 1s 4d one of his ELEVEN DEMANDS (1930) — the businessmen's demand had become the Congress's own = the base for the capitalists' active part in the CDM; at the 1st ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE (1930) , FICCI BOYCOTTED proceedings in solidarity with the INC

CDM — capitalist participation reaches a new level: for the first time TRADERS ACTIVELY STOPPED IMPORTING BRITISH CLOTH → British cloth imports fell by roughly 50% (*not purely nationalist sentiment — also good business, since Indian mills gained from reduced British competition); capitalists contributed financially; BUT they consistently OPPOSED the escalation of mass civil disobedience beyond a point — FICCI's line: support the INC politically, but do not let the movement threaten capitalism itself 2nd ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE (1931) — when Gandhi attends, FICCI SUPPORTS CONGRESS : a concrete political act — India's organised business community publicly standing with the nationalist negotiating team at a constitutional forum

QIM — even at the INM's most confrontational, individual businessmen acted on nationalist sentiment: during the underground phase businessmen DONATED GENEROUSLY ; SUMATI MORARJEE , a businesswoman, gave ACHYUT PATWARDHAN a different car each day so he could evade detection (*acts of personal courage, not institutional policy)

THE BOMBAY PLAN (January 1944) — formally 'A Plan of Economic Development for India' ; drafted by EIGHT leading industrialists + technocrats: JRD TATA + GD BIRLA + PURUSHOTTAMDAS THAKURDAS + ARDESHIR DALAL + KASTURBHAI LALBHAI + AD SHROFF + LALA SHRI RAM + JOHN MATHAI ; published at the height of the Bengal Famine (1943) + QIM repression; THE FIRST EVER NATIONAL ECONOMIC PLAN FOR INDIA ; proposed a MIXED ECONOMY with heavy STATE investment in basic industries + infrastructure + transportation + power + social welfare (education, housing, healthcare); called for DOUBLING per capita income within 15 YEARS through THREE FIVE-YEAR PLANS ; endorsed by FICCI at its 1944 annual meeting ; direct + acknowledged influence on India's FIRST FIVE YEAR PLAN ( u criticised from all sides: the left said it did not go far enough; the right said it was socialist + dangerous; the Viceroy's office reportedly discussed a 'rival pamphlet' — that it upset everyone roughly equally is the clearest sign it was a genuinely centrist document)

INA TRIALS + THE FINAL PHASE — capitalists + businessmen contributed funds, provided material support, and openly backed the INA men's defence ; the INA DEFENCE COMMITTEE raised funds with GD BIRLA among the major contributors, while BHULABHAI DESAI led the legal defence at the Red Fort ; even before the trials, Indian businessmen in MALAYA + SINGAPORE + BURMA (the diaspora merchant communities) had been a major source of funding for the INA + the IIL during the war itself

phases.note: the FISCAL AUTONOMY CONVENTION after WWI gives India some tariff-setting power ; the post-CDM period finally

events.label: GOPAL BABA WALANGKAR , a Mahar ex-soldier, starts VITAL-VIDHVANSAK ('Destroyer of Ceremonial Pollution') in 1888 — the FIRST monthly journal aimed at the untouchable community , well before Ambedkar's generation

VAIKOM SATYAGRAHA (1924–25) in Travancore — the FIRST major organised TEMPLE-ENTRY movement of the modern period; led by the EZHAVA community, with NARAYAN GURU + K. KESAVA MENON at the forefront; immediate demand = the right to use public roads near the Vaikom temple ; it became an ALL-INDIA movement — PERIYAR (EV Ramaswamy Naicker) joined; the INC formally supported it; Savarnas (upper castes) boycotted Avarnas + pro-Satyagraha Congressmen in response GANDHI VISITS (1925) + meets the QUEEN OF TRAVANCORE → a COMPROMISE : some roads near the temple opened to Avarnas, others remained reserved for Savarnas, and some temple gates remained closed to lower castes (*a partial win — the principle of equality was acknowledged, but not yet enforced)

SELF-RESPECT MOVEMENT (1925) founded by PERIYAR in the Madras Presidency — a direct assault on Brahminical social dominance : rejected caste hierarchy, denounced Brahminical rituals, and promoted SELF-RESPECT MARRIAGES (weddings without Brahmin priests + without Sanskrit mantras) = an assertion that lower-caste communities could define their own dignity, own ceremonies + own social rules ; Prelims 2019 + 2021
ALL INDIA DEPRESSED CLASSES ASSOCIATION (AIDCA, 1926) formed under MC RAJAH of Madras

MAHAD SATYAGRAHA (1927) — AMBEDKAR organises a massive Satyagraha of 15,000 Dalits at MAHAD, Maharashtra , asserting the right to draw water from a PUBLIC TANK (Chavdar Tank) ; the colonial administration had technically granted the right — the upper-caste community had refused to accept it; Ambedkar led the Dalits physically to the tank + drew water ; Prelims 2013

AMBEDKAR PUBLICLY BURNS THE MANUSMRITI at the same Mahad conference ( December 1927 ) — the ancient text that had codified caste hierarchy + the subjugation of Dalits + women ; one of the most powerful symbolic acts of the entire colonial period

AMBEDKAR APPEARS BEFORE THE SIMON COMMISSION (1928) + demands SEPARATE ELECTORATES FOR DALITS — the same mechanism granted to Muslims under the ICA 1909 + accepted by the INC for Muslims in the Lucknow Pact (1916) (*Ambedkar was not asking for anything that had not already been given to others — but when a Dalit asked, the INC's response was very different)

ALL INDIA DEPRESSED CLASSES CONGRESS (AIDCC, 1930) formed by Ambedkar — explicitly ANTI-INC in orientation + designed to negotiate with the British directly as a distinct political voice; at the 1st ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE (1930) — which the INC boycotted — Ambedkar participated + again demanded separate electorates

2nd ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE (1931) — THE DECISIVE CONFRONTATION: GANDHI vs AMBEDKAR on separate electorates for Dalits; GANDHI: Dalits are Hindus + should not be separated from the Hindu electorate — it would permanently divide Hindu society ; AMBEDKAR: without separate electorates Dalits will always be dependent on upper-caste Hindu voters + will never be able to elect genuine Dalit representatives

GURUVAYUR SATYAGRAHA (1931–33) in Malabar (today Thrissur district, Kerala) — K. KELLAPAN leads a march to the temple for temple entry + goes on a FAST UNTO DEATH , breaking it only on Gandhi's personal appeal ; AK GOPALAN (later a major communist leader) walks across Malabar on foot as part of the agitation COMMUNAL AWARD (August 1932) , issued by British PM RAMSAY MACDONALD — SIDES WITH AMBEDKAR , granting Dalits reserved seats through SEPARATE ELECTORATES ; GANDHI responds with a FAST UNTO DEATH from jail (*his objection was to separate electorates , NOT to reservation — which he explicitly supported; but the political effect was enormous moral pressure on Ambedkar to surrender the demand)

POONA PACT (September 1932) — Dalits RETAIN RESERVED SEATS but with JOINT electorates instead of separate ones; the number of reserved seats was actually INCREASED compared to the Communal Award — but the crucial instrument of ELECTORAL INDEPENDENCE was gone ; Ambedkar described signing it as one of the worst days of his life ; the reservation structure was formalised in the GOI ACT 1935 ; post-Pact, Gandhi launches his HARIJAN CAMPAIGN (touring the country, opening wells + temples, raising funds) — sincere, but other INC leaders were largely indifferent

AMBEDKAR'S TURN — 'NO SOLUTION WITHIN HINDUISM' : when temple-entry Satyagrahis agitate at the KALARAM TEMPLE in NASIK (1934) , Ambedkar asks them to STOP + instead BOYCOTT TEMPLES ALTOGETHER ; his reasoning was blunt: seeking entry into the very system that created the injustice is not the path forward; the solution lies in EDUCATION + POLITICAL POWER , and the compensation for centuries of oppression was non-negotiable — RESERVATION in education, government jobs + political representation

INDEPENDENT LABOUR PARTY (ILP, 1936) formed by Ambedkar — designed to bring together poor workers + untouchables , merging the politics of class + caste into a single movement (*the poorest industrial workers + the most oppressed caste group were, in many cases, the same people); the ILP won most reserved seats in BOMBAY in the 1937 elections

KING OF TRAVANCORE ISSUES A ROYAL PROCLAMATION (1936) — opening ALL TEMPLES in Travancore to ALL Hindus regardless of caste , following continued pressure from the Guruvayur agitation (*1936 — the same year as the INC's Faizpur session + the founding of AIKS. One India, many struggles, all running simultaneously)

In the 1937 provincial elections the INC won only HALF of the reserved Dalit seats ; the INC governments (1937–39) did NOT meaningfully work for Dalit interests in the provinces they governed (*Nehru refused to recognise caste as a political problem — seeing it as a social question that would dissolve with modernisation + economic development) AMBEDKAR becomes LABOUR MINISTER in the Viceroy's Executive Council (1942) — working within the colonial administration; in the SAME year, just a few days before the QIM , he forms the ALL INDIA SCHEDULED CASTES FEDERATION (AISCF, 1942) , with the explicit motto that DALITS ARE DISTINCT FROM HINDUS

AISCF MARGINALISED in the 1946 elections — like every minor party — by the dominant INC vs ML1906 contest (the QIM legacy + INA trials + the Pakistan demand consumed all political oxygen); the AISCF had been formed late, had a weak organisational structure, many Dalits were personally followers of Gandhi, and the communists actively eroded its base among poorer Dalits

CO-OPTION + THE CONSTITUTION — after the 1946 elections the INC CO-OPTS AMBEDKAR : member of the CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY → CHAIRMAN of its Constitution Drafting Committee (the man the INC had opposed at the Round Table Conferences now wrote the Constitution of independent India); UNTOUCHABILITY made illegal under ARTICLE 17 ; Ambedkar becomes LAW MINISTER in Nehru's cabinet; Prelims 2025 AMBEDKAR RESIGNS from the cabinet (1951) — the INC refused to support his HINDU CODE BILL , a sweeping reform of Hindu personal law covering inheritance + marriage + divorce + property rights for women (*the party that had spoken for decades about social equality could not pass it when it actually held power)

AMBEDKAR CONVERTS TO BUDDHISM (October 1956) along with 3.8 LAKH followers — just one and a half months before his death ; his final statement that there was no solution within Hinduism, and no political home within the INC

BETHUNE SCHOOL (1849) established by DRINKWATER BETHUNE (Law Member of the Governor-General's Council, with special interest from Dalhousie ) — a landmark in women's formal education (*19th-c. reform talked ABOUT women — it did not talk WITH them; women were the SUBJECT of reform, not its participants)

TARABAI SHINDE publishes 'COMPARISON BETWEEN WOMEN & MEN' (1882) — a fierce argument that men enjoyed all rights while women were reduced to the stereotype of the PATIVRATA , the devoted wife who exists only in service to her husband

HUNTER COMMISSION (1882) provides liberal grants + scholarships for women's education (*the British interest was not altruistic — they wanted English-educated women who would raise pro-Western children + hoped that keeping women in the domestic sphere would prevent them joining the INM ; the bhadralok wanted an educated companion; reformers wanted to counter the British civilisational critique. All male agendas)

PANDITA RAMABAI — a Brahmin woman who refused the new model on offer (the educated but obedient wife): stayed unmarried for years, then married a Sudra man , was widowed, went to England to study medicine , converted to Christianity , went to the United States + raised funds for a WIDOW'S HOME IN BOMBAY ; criticised not just by traditionalists but by the very reformers who claimed to support women

SWADESHI — the focus on 'MOTHER INDIA' kept women's participation in stereotyped domestic activities (keepers of the household, guardians of Swadeshi, boycotters of foreign goods); ONE notable exception: SARALA DEBI CHAUDHRANI , involved in the PHYSICAL CULTURE MOVEMENT for Bengal's youth (*in revolutionary activities too, women's roles were support roles — shelter, couriers, messages: brave + dangerous work, but invisible + uncredited) BHARAT STREE MANDAL (1910) established by SARALA DEBI CHAUDHRANI — branches across India to promote women's education
SAROJINI NAIDU leads a DELEGATION TO THE SECRETARY OF STATE (1917) demanding the RIGHT TO VOTE FOR WOMEN ; ANNIE BESANT already central to the Home Rule League Movement (1916–18)

Naidu demands EQUAL ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA for voting rights within the INC ( 1918 ); the GOI ACT 1919 gives women the RIGHT TO VOTE — though subject to PROPERTY QUALIFICATIONS ; in the ROWLATT SATYAGRAHA (1919) Gandhi gives a specific call to WOMEN to participate for the first time NCM — women join boycotts + Swadeshi activities; agitate against the visit of the PRINCE OF WALES (November 1921) ; BASANTI DEVI (wife of CR Das) courts arrest in December 1921 ; Muslim women join the Khilafat Movement — the most remarkable moment being BI AMMAN , mother of the Ali Brothers (Shaukat + Mohammad Ali), who addressed public crowds for the first time in her life , lifting purdah + addressing the crowds as her children From 1921 to 1930 several PROVINCIAL LEGISLATURES use powers given by the GOI Act 1919 to grant women the right to vote — subject to property qualifications SAROJINI NAIDU elected PRESIDENT OF THE INC (1925) — the FIRST WOMAN to hold the position

ALL INDIA WOMEN'S CONFERENCE (AIWC, 1927) founded under MARGARET COUSINS , an Irish feminist — the most significant women's organisation; UNLIKE the INC it took up women's issues DIRECTLY : women's education + political rights + marriage reforms + rights for women workers; methods MODERATE (lobbying + petitions, not mass agitation); it placed the INM BEFORE women's issues (*women's organisations in this period were nationalist first, feminist second )
SARDA ACT 1929 (formally the CHILD MARRIAGE RESTRAINT ACT ) — minimum age of marriage set at 14 for girls + 18 for males

CDM — THOUSANDS of women joined ; everyone was shocked by the scale; the CHITTAGONG revolutionary group under SURYA SEN also included women participants; BUT a sharp contradiction persisted: the INC NEVER involved women in DECISION-MAKING + never took up women's issues as political demands — SARALA DEBI CHAUDHRANI captured it precisely: 'The INC wants women only to be LAWBREAKERS, NOT LAWMAKERS .' Bills on PROPERTY RIGHTS + INHERITANCE + DIVORCE + DOWRY + PROSTITUTION passed in central + provincial legislatures
events.full: 1930-34 1930s — CDM — THOUSANDS of women joined ; everyone was shocked by the scale; the CHITTAGONG revolutionary group under SURYA SEN also included women participants; BUT a sharp contradiction persisted: the INC NEVER involved women in DECISION-MAKING + never took up women's issues as political demands — SARALA DEBI CHAUDHRANI captured it precisely: 'The INC wants women only to be LAWBREAKERS, NOT LAWMAKERS .' Bills on PROPERTY RIGHTS + INHERITANCE + DIVORCE + DOWRY + PROSTITUTION passed in central + provincial legislatures

events.label: GOI ACT 1935 extends the right to vote to MORE WOMEN + gives them RESERVED SEATS in legislatures; women leaders were NOT satisfied with reservation — they wanted UNIVERSAL ADULT FRANCHISE , which would make reservation unnecessary (*that came only with the Constitution of 1950 )

QIM — GREAT PARTICIPATION by women , especially in RURAL AREAS ; the lifting of the ban on CPI1925 in 1942 also aided women's political participation (many women had been CPI members since the 1920s–30s); in Bengal in 1942 leftist women leaders organise the MAHILA ATMARAKSHA SAMITI (1942) + do famine relief work during the Bengal Famine (1943)
1,500 WOMEN join the RANI JHANSI REGIMENT of the INA + fight in the IMPHAL CAMPAIGN (1944) (*link Ch 45); women also participate in the Muslim League's Pakistan campaign in the 1940s

TEBHAGA MOVEMENT (1946) in Bengal — sharecroppers demanding two-thirds of their produce — sees high participation by DALIT + TRIBAL WOMEN , who fought the British + sacrificed lives in what became a violent resistance (*they were not fighting for abstract nationalism — they were fighting for the rice that fed their children)

THE CONSTITUTION OF 1950 gives women FULL POLITICAL EQUALITY — but the social + economic transformation that Tarabai Shinde + Pandita Ramabai had demanded in the 1880s is still unfinished (*overall, women fought more for nationalism than for their own rights ; the INC took their participation gratefully + gave their issues a low priority in return)

BARDOLI SATYAGRAHA (1928) — the most organised peasant movement of the 1920s, but still WITHIN the Gandhian framework of negotiation + arbitration (*1920s peasant movements = mostly LOCAL : one district, one landlord, one grievance)
SWAMI SAHAJANAND SARASWATI founds the BIHAR PROVINCIAL KISAN SABHA (BPKS) in 1929 — it becomes the most organised + aggressive arm of the peasant movement in Bihar

THE GREAT DEPRESSION — between 1929 + 1933 agricultural prices FELL BY ROUGHLY HALF ; but the rent owed to the zamindar did NOT fall, the land revenue owed to the govt did NOT fall, the debt owed to the moneylender did NOT fall: income fell by half; obligations stayed the same → MASS DEBT + LOSS OF LAND (*global commodity prices collapsed because of events in New York + London — events a farmer in UP or Bihar had no role in, no knowledge of, and no protection against. Yet he paid the full price) KARACHI SESSION (March 1931) — presided by SARDAR PATEL , resolution drafted by NEHRU : for the FIRST time INC defines what Swaraj would actually mean for the masses — political freedom must include REAL ECONOMIC FREEDOM : substantial reduction of land revenue + rent , relief for uneconomic holdings, cancellation of agricultural debt , a living wage for workers, and STATE OWNERSHIP of key industries (*the colonial govt was alarmed enough by its near-socialist content to spread rumours that communist money had secretly reached Karachi )

CDM pulls the peasantry into ACTIVE POLITICS — no-tax campaigns + no-rent campaigns + refusal to pay land revenue = not just economic acts but political ones; when the CDM is withdrawn in 1934 , peasants are POLITICALLY CONSCIOUS BUT ORGANISATIONALLY HOMELESS — a gap waiting to be filled THE LEFT MOVES IN — the CSP (1934) + the CPI both invest heavily in rural organisation ; they give the peasant movement an IDEOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK (not just 'reduce my rent' but 'the zamindari system itself must go' ) + the organisational skill to build at scale

ALL INDIA KISAN SABHA (AIKS) founded at LUCKNOW, 11 April 1936 — timed to coincide with the INC session that year; SWAMI SAHAJANAND SARASWATI of Bihar = first PRESIDENT ; NG RANGA = first GENERAL SECRETARY

THE KISAN MANIFESTO (August 1936) — demands: ABOLISH THE ZAMINDARI SYSTEM + tax agricultural wealth on a GRADUATED SCALE + CANCEL the hereditary debts of peasants + grant OCCUPANCY RIGHTS to tenants (*occupancy right = the legal right to stay on + till a piece of land; without it a tenant could be evicted at the zamindar's will at any time ); these demands went well beyond what the INC was ready to adopt as official policy

KRISHAK PRAJA PARTY (KPP) founded by AK FAZLUL HUQ in Bengal ( 1936 ) — NOT part of the AIKS structure ; an independent party of East Bengal , representing Muslim peasants against largely Hindu zamindars + moneylenders; demanded abolition of zamindari + debt relief + an end to the PERMANENT SETTLEMENT ; won 36 SEATS in the 1937 Bengal assembly elections, but later formed a coalition with the Muslim League , not the INC

FAIZPUR SESSION (1936) — the FIRST EVER INC session held IN A VILLAGE (a deliberate symbolic act); AIKS + INC hold a JOINT MEETING there, and Kisan demands substantially shape the INC's manifesto for the 1937 provincial elections → a strong INC performance (though short of majorities in Bengal, Punjab, Assam, Sindh + NWFP)

CONGRESS MINISTRIES (28 months) — FROM AGITATION TO ADMINISTRATION : the INC was a coalition of many classes (peasants + workers + lawyers + professionals + merchants + industrialists + zamindars who were themselves part of the nationalist movement); all had voted INC; all now expected something in return; in Bihar + UP the ministries passed INCREMENTAL agrarian laws (relief for tenants in arrears + protection against arbitrary eviction + reduction in rent burdens) — they did NOT abolish zamindari (*abolishing it overnight would extinguish millions of legal property rights at once, without a replacement system ready — the risk of agrarian chaos was real) THE BAKASHT AGITATION, BIHAR (* Bakasht lands = tenant plots that zamindars had seized during the Depression when tenants fell into debt + could not pay rent) — under the BPKS , peasants launch Satyagrahas, physically entering disputed fields + harvesting crops ; the Congress Ministry under SRI KRISHNA SINHA works out a NEGOTIATED SETTLEMENT (partial restoration of seized land to tenants + legal stability for zamindars over remaining claims); when the Kisan Sabha's agitation turns volatile, the ministry USES THE POLICE ; by AUGUST 1939 , concessions + legislation + the arrest of ~600 activists bring it under control; RAHUL SANKRITYAYAN among those arrested (*his more famous 2-year Hazaribagh imprisonment came in 1940 , under BRITISH authority, after the ministries had resigned in Oct 1939) HARIPURA SESSION (1938) , presided by SUBHAS CHANDRA BOSE — the INC passes a formal resolution on Kisan Sabhas: it REAFFIRMS the right of peasants to organise , BUT states that the Congress cannot associate itself with any activities incompatible with its basic principles + would NOT permit Congressmen who were Kisan Sabha members to create an atmosphere hostile to Congress policy ; PCCs directed to take suitable action (*the resolution was rushed through with very little discussion — the INC had drawn its line, quietly but firmly)

THE SPLIT — peasant activists now had a choice: stay within the constitutional, moderate framework of the INC , or pursue the militant, class-based path of the AIKS ; many chose the AIKS — and the CPI moved steadily into the organisational space the INC had vacated ; despite Haripura, the AIKS reached a membership of over 800,000 by 1939

FLOUD COMMISSION (1940) — formally the Bengal Land Revenue Commission ; recommended the ABOLITION OF THE PERMANENT SETTLEMENT + a restructuring of the landlord-tenant revenue share; the Bengal govt NEVER IMPLEMENTED IT — which is precisely why the peasants had to fight for it six years later through TEBHAGA

WAR, THE CPI, AND THE PEASANTRY — after 1941, SAHAJANAND SARASWATI + NG RANGA eventually LEAVE the AIKS , finding it impossible to address peasants while following the CPI's pro-British 'PEOPLE'S WAR' line; the AIKS changes from a broad peasant front allied with the INC into, in practical terms, a MASS ORGANISATION OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY ; meanwhile wartime requisitioning of grain + forced procurement below market prices + rampant inflation + severe food shortages push the peasantry to the edge → the BENGAL FAMINE OF 1943 is the most catastrophic expression of this crisis (*link Ch 45) QIM — PEASANTS WERE THE SOUL OF THE MOVEMENT : with the entire INC leadership arrested within hours of the 8 August resolution , the movement was carried forward by the masses; peasants cut telegraph lines + disrupted rail communications + attacked police stations + in several districts established PARALLEL GOVERNMENTS (the Satara Prati Sarkar + the Ballia + Midnapore uprisings the most famous); for the rural poor QIM was simultaneously a NATIONALIST outburst + a CLASS struggle — the colonial revenue machinery, the zamindar's rent collector + the moneylender's account book were all part of the same oppressive system ; the two impulses fused (*link Ch 44)

THE WORLI UPRISING (Maharashtra, 1945–1947) — the Worlis , an impoverished tribal community in THANE district of Bombay Presidency, were treated by landlords + moneylenders + forest contractors virtually as bonded labour ; the central grievance was VETH BEGAR — forced, unpaid labour , accompanied by physical abuse + starvation wages; in 1945 , finding a voice through organisers like GODAVARI PARULEKAR , they launch a massive, unified STRIKE refusing to perform forced labour ; despite brutal police crackdowns, their unprecedented solidarity FORCES THE

THE BAKASHT LAND RE-OCCUPATIONS (Bihar, 1946–1947) — the second, more intense phase (roots in the 1930s agitation); as famine loomed + wartime distress deepened, starving evicted peasants demanded immediate restoration of hereditary tenancy rights ; led again by SWAMI SAHAJANAND SARASWATI , they bypass petitions + resort to DIRECT ACTION — marching onto the Bakasht lands to plant their own crops, facing the lathi-wielding private armies of zamindars + British police ; the agitation forces the provincial government to pass the BIHAR BAKASHT

THE PUNNAPRA-VAYALAR UPRISING (Kerala, October 1946) — in the Princely State of TRAVANCORE , where the autocratic Dewan SIR C.P. RAMASWAMI IYER had a plan to declare Travancore an INDEPENDENT state allied directly with the British Crown — refusing to join the Indian Union; amid wartime food hoarding + brutal feudal exploitation, CPI + CSP cadres mobilise coir-factory workers + fishermen + agricultural labourers, armed with little more than SHARPENED BAMBOO STICKS , fighting both their economic oppressors + the Dewan's separatist agenda; they establish SELF-RULE CAMPS in the villages of Punnapra + Vayalar ; the Dewan sends the state military with BRITISH MACHINE GUNS — an estimated 1,000 peasants + workers KILLED over a few days; but the sacrifice SHATTERS the Dewan's authority → he flees, permanently ending his separatist ambitions + ensuring Travancore's integration into the Indian Republic (*a crucial instance where the Left's radical agrarian agitation directly served the vital national interest of preventing India's balkanisation)

THE TEBHAGA MOVEMENT (Bengal, 1946–1947) — a PRE-INDEPENDENCE peasant struggle confronting the Bengal provincial government while India was still under British rule ; 'TEBHAGA' = THREE PARTS : peasants demanded the landlord's share be reduced from HALF (1/2) to ONE-THIRD (1/3) , with the tenant keeping TWO-THIRDS ; the intellectual basis had been laid by the FLOUD COMMISSION (1940) , which the Bengal govt never implemented; Prelims 2013 THE TELANGANA ARMED STRUGGLE (1946–1951) — born of the horrific exploitation of the rural poor by the Nizam of Hyderabad's feudal landlords (DESHMUKHS) through forced labour ( VETTI ) + violent evictions; the peasants' initial armed resistance against the Nizam's RAZAKAR militia heroically aided India's national integration ; BUT after Hyderabad's liberation by the Indian Army in 1948 (OPERATION POLO) , the CPI leadership directed the peasants to REFUSE DISARMAMENT + turn their weapons against the newly independent democratic Indian Republic — transforming a just anti-feudal rebellion into a misguided ideological war that the Indian state SUPPRESSED BY 1951 (*Tebhaga + Telangana both operated ENTIRELY OUTSIDE the Gandhian framework )

anchors: Gandhi vs Ambedkar on Varna — the Fundamental Divide (Mains 2015): GANDHI = REFORM FROM WITHIN. The varna system was
fundamentally sound — a division of labour that, in its ideal form, assigned dignity to all occupations without hierarchy. What had gone wrong
was its corruption into caste : untouchability, pollution norms, hereditary exclusion — none of it sanctioned by the original scriptures.
Remedy = moral persuasion : upper-caste Hindus must do penance, open temples + wells, treat Dalits as equals — because their own
religion demands it. AMBEDKAR = ANNIHILATION. Caste was not a corruption of varna but its logical consequence : hierarchy, the bans
on inter-dining + inter-marriage, and untouchability were built into the structure of the Shastras . There was no 'pure varna' to return to.
Remedy = destroy the authority of the Shastras , enact statutory safeguards (reservation, legal prohibition, constitutional rights), and if
Hinduism cannot accommodate equality, exit Hinduism . Moral persuasion is useless against a system sustained not by individual cruelty
but by scriptural authority + institutional power . u Gandhi said: change the heart. Ambedkar said: change the law, because the
heart will not change on its own. Independent India, through the Constitution, largely adopted Ambedkar's institutional approach
(Article 17, reservation, the SC order) while continuing to invoke Gandhi's moral language . The tension remains alive.
Historiography of the Peasant Upsurge — Two Readings (essential for Mains): BIPAN CHANDRA (Nationalist): the peasant
movement was an integral part of the anti-colonial struggle . The INC provided the initial political awakening; its left wing pushed the party
toward real agrarian reform. Even in the great upsurges of the 1940s — above all the QIM — the peasants' primary target was the colonial
state . Even the radical Left-led post-war movements (Tebhaga, Punnapra-Vayalar) struck at the feudal pillars of the British Empire ,
thereby aiding national liberation. The tensions with Congress ministries (1937–39) + the CPI's Telangana deviation are secondary to this
overarching anti-imperialist reality. SEKHAR BANDYOPADHYAY (Subaltern/Critical): 'freedom' meant vastly different things to
different social groups . When the Congress ministries accommodated zamindar interests in 1937–39, it revealed the class limits of the
INC's bourgeois leadership . The explosion of the post-war movements (Worli, Tebhaga, Telangana) confirms his thesis: frustrated by the
INC's protection of propertied interests, the rural masses broke free of the Congress umbrella and fought a parallel class war entirely
outside the Gandhian framework . u SYNTHESIS: both catch something true. The INC was genuinely anti-colonial AND a multi-class
coalition that could not govern without managing propertied interests. The peasantry's journey — from Gandhi's CDM (1930) → AIKS (1936)
→ armed communist rebellion (1946) — illustrates that unresolved tension. The national movement threw out the British, but left the
class struggle in the countryside to be fought out in the early years of the Republic.
n Prelims Cluster — Ch 47 (1995–2025): WORKERS + CAPITALISTS (17 PYQs, 1995–2019). Anchors: AITUC 1920 (founder = N.M.
Joshi; first president = Lala Lajpat Rai); Bombay textile workers' strike 1908 (Tilak's sedition trial); Trade Union Act 1926 ; Royal
Commission on Labour 1929 (Whitley); Industrial Disputes Act 1947 ; FICCI 1927 (Purshotamdas Thakurdas + GD Birla); Bombay Plan
1944 (Tata, Birla, Dalmia — the capitalist statement of post-independence economic policy); capitalist support to the INM through indirect
funding , while capitalists like Walchand Hirachand and others opposed Gandhi's anti-modernist Khadi line. DALITS: 2013 — Ambedkar's
Mahad Satyagraha 1927 (public water access at Chavdar Tank); 2019 + 2021 — Periyar E.V. Ramasamy + the Self-Respect Movement
(Tamil Nadu, 1925); 2025 — Ambedkar's constitutional contributions + Depressed Classes representation at the Round Table Conferences.
PEASANTS: 2013 — Tebhaga (landlord's share from 1/2 to 1/3). MAINS 2015 — Gandhi vs Ambedkar on varna + caste .
FIVE VOICES, ONE NATION. The INM was never a single voice. Beneath it ran five distinct streams — WORKERS

Sur clan (Pashtun tribe) migrates from Sur region of Afghanistan to India during Lodi Sultanate period; Sher Shah's grandfather receives small Jagir in Sasaram (present-day Bihar)

Trade between Europe & Asia = most profitable business in known world; Arab traders dominate Arabian Sea leg; Italian merchants (Genoa & Venice) carry goods across Mediterranean into Europe; both earn enormous profits at each handoff

Guru Nanak Dev Ji — founder of Sikhism; contemporary of Babur26-30; Sikhism rises from 1500 onwards; 4 core principles: (i) One supreme & formless God; (ii) direct access to God without rituals/priests; (iii) rejection of caste system; (iv) honest living & selfless service

1st Battle of Panipat — Babur defeats & kills Ibrahim Lodi → Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526) ENDS; Mughal Kingdom BORN
~20 major Rajput clans control Rajputana — multi-polar; no single dominant power
Akbar's reign — builds Mansabdari system; Zabti LR system; practically abolishes Ijaradari/Muqatai

EIC founded — Royal Charter of Queen Elizabeth I58-03 (1558–1603); 4th joint-stock company in England; 215 London merchant adventurers; stated goal: trade (NOT empire); Charter gives: (i) 15-year monopoly over trade with East Indies; (ii) right to carry gold out of England; (iii) management by Governor, Deputy Governor & 24 members (later Board/Court of Directors)
Jahangir's reign — Ijaradari re-emerges marginally; control over Jagirdar-Mansabdars loosens
