Imad-ul-Mulk (Wazir; also called Gaddar-ul-Mulk) blinds Emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur — 1st Mughal Emperor destroyed by own Wazir

Siraj-ud-daula56-57 succeeds Alivardi Khan40-56 — precious grandson (only grandson, through daughter; no sons); young, impulsive; disliked in Bengal court (had disrespected senior Mansabdars; imprisoned Jagat Seth for extortion); immediately stops Dastak misuse -> hurts private trade fortunes of EIC officials

Immediate financial settlement: (i) Rs 2.25 crore to EIC; (ii) 2,75,000 pounds to Royal British military; (iii) 2,34,000 pounds to Clive personally + personal jagir of 35,000 pounds per annum; scale: ~x32,000 multiplier; in 1760 terms = ~3.5% of Britain's total GDP of GBP 70 million
Battle of Plassey — EIC becomes a political power; begins receiving Bengal LR (Diwani) informally

Plassey Plunder 1757-65 — pre-19th century drain: misuse of Dastaks (duty-free passes granted only for EIC goods; misused by Company servants for private trade) + Plassey plunder + LR extraction from British India beginning 1765 (Treaty of Allahabad 1765); structure of British trade with India reverses: earlier gold flows INTO India as payment for Indian goods; after Plassey + LR rights, gold flows OUT of India Modern colonial relationship develops post-Charter Act 1813 — colony = source of raw materials + export market; India becomes net exporter of raw materials (cotton, jute, indigo, tea, opium) instead of net exporter of finished goods; Indian agriculture reoriented from food crops to cash crops/raw materials for export to British factories = commercialisation of agriculture

Sanyasi + Fakir Rebellion, North Bengal + Bihar — peaks around 1800 with ~50,000 participants; two groups: Dasnami Sanyasis (Hindus; peasants + small traders) + Madari Fakirs (Muslims; held revenue-free/rent-free tenures now ended by EIC); cooperate despite different religions because economic grievances identical + philosophical common ground; grievances: high LR, high rents post-PS1793, EIC monopoly over domestic trade in Bengal; Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's Anandamath (1882) inspired by this rebellion; Vande Mataram from Anandamath -> anthem of INM; Prelims 2006: Anandamath = Sanyasi Rebellion (NOT Bhil uprising / NOT Rangpur-Dinapur / NOT Bishnupur-Birbhum)

BRITISH ROOT (Clive57-67) — mini Subsidiary Alliance planted @ Awadh via ToA1765: EIC army in Awadh paid by subsidy from Awadh + Awadh army size reduced + British Resident stationed; BUT Awadh's army NOT disbanded + Foreign Policy NOT taken over = mini/proto SA only

EIC receives Diwani (right to collect LR) of Bengal + Orissa + Bihar through ToA1765; appoints Deputy Subadar Muhammad Reza Khan as Diwan; Mughal system continues (Orientalism); Patta system ignored almost immediately; rents extracted far beyond patta records

Dual Government (Experiment 1) — EIC holds Diwani; Nawab holds Nizamat; frantic over-extraction; back-to-back droughts hit Great Bengal Famine (GBF 1770) — kills between 50 lakh + 1 crore Indians; EIC DOUBLES land revenue demand in 1770 + uses brutality to collect; British whistleblowers write to London newspapers; famine destroys agrarian economy; LR income collapses
Treaty of Allahabad (ToA1765) — EIC formally receives Diwani of Bengal + Orissa + Bihar; American political revolution begins (Stamp Act crisis)

Mughal judicial system in Bengal: CIVIL courts (Sadar Diwani Adalat at top; Pandits judge Hindu cases; Maulvis judge Muslim cases; Zamindar holds Kachari/revenue court at local level; appeals: Zamindar -> Amil -> Sadar Diwani Adalat); CRIMINAL courts (Nizamat/Faujdari Adalats; Islamic law applies to all regardless of religion; Kazis = judges; Muftis = Islamic law experts; Faujdar = executive police chief executes sentence; Naib Nazim heads Sadar Nizamat Adalat)

Dual Government — EIC gains Diwani rights (revenue + civil courts); Nawab retains Nizamat (criminal); Muhammad Reza Khan heads both Diwani + Nizamat on EIC's behalf; EIC does not impose own system (Orientalism); hands-off approach -> poor revenue collection + deteriorating law + order + GBF 1770 Hastings73-85 ends Dual Government; assumes direct administration of both Diwani + Nizamat; British DC made judge in Diwani courts (assisted by Pandits + Maulvis for personal law); Kazis + Muftis continue in Nizamat courts but supervised by European DC; Sadar Diwani Adalat + Sadar Nizamat Adalat now headed by Governor (later GG) + Council members
EIC obtains Diwani of Bengal Suba (Bengal + Orissa + Bihar); 1775: Benaras annexed + administered as part of Bengal Presidency

Hyder Ali61-82 BREAKS triple alliance through diplomacy: (i) pays Marathas Rs 35 lakh to exit war; (ii) makes alliance with Hyderabad: pays Nizam Rs 20 lakh + promises to make Nizam's son Nawab of Carnatic + agrees to jointly attack Carnatic (under Md Ali52-95, EIC ally)
British State demands GBP 400,000 per annum from EIC arguing State helped in conquest
Great Bengal Famine (GBF 1770) — kills 50 lakh to 1 crore; EIC doubles LR demand; 'Nabobs' (corrupt EIC officers) embarrass British State; first whistleblowers write to London newspapers
Marathas attack Mysore — EIC REFUSES to honour its 1769 treaty obligation to come to Mysore's defence; Hyder Ali61-82 notes the betrayal
Maratha Civil War (brief): Narayan Rao72-73 — Peshwa; murdered 1773 in palace conspiracy by uncle Raghunath Rao73-74 Raghunath Rao73-74 becomes Peshwa after murder of nephew Narayan Rao72-73

Mughal police system in Bengal: Naib Nazim (overall head) -> Faujdars (rural districts) / Kotwals (towns + urban areas) / Zamindars (villages; held police duties + paid village watchmen from own resources)

Treaty of Faizabad 1775 — Benaras annexed by EIC; Raja Chait Singh of Benaras made big zamindar under EIC; owns military + fort; later PS1793 formally brings Benaras into Bengal-BOB-North Madras-Benaras revenue settlement

Pahariya Revolt, Rajmahal Hills — Pahariyas = earliest tribals to resist British encroachment; hill-dwelling hunter-gatherers + shifting cultivators; EIC extends revenue collection + admin control into Rajmahal Hills; revolt against destruction of autonomy + livelihood; British respond with military force + containment policy (push Pahariyas further into hills)
Calcutta Madrasa set up by Warren Hastings73-85 (1781) — study of Arabic, Persian + Islamic law; trains Indians to assist EIC in ruling India the Indian way

Tipu82-99 reigns — pushes Mysore's ambitions further; dream = Vijayanagar 2.0 (dominate all South India + control its international trade) Haider Ali61-82 & Tipu82-99 together develop iron-cased rocket artillery — 100% indigenous; range 2 km; iron cylinder casings do not burst + can take high pressure (unlike cardboard-cased rockets existing since centuries in India & China); later closely studied by British; William Congreve's rockets (early 19th c British military) drawn directly from Tipu82-99's designs Tipu82-99 builds modern navy + establishes government-owned trading company modelled on EIC — conducts oceanic trade in sandalwood, sulphur, rice, pepper, silk & cardamom; sets up 30 trading centres inside & outside India including Muscat, Oman Tipu82-99 formally declares independence — from Wodeyars AND from Mughal Emperor; sends request to Khalifa (religious head of Muslim world) for a sanad recognising him as independent ruler
Mahadji Scindhia dominates Maratha politics until his death in 1794 Madhav Rao II74-95 commits suicide — Bajirao II96-18 becomes Peshwa (formally tenured 1796-1818)

Utilitarianism (Bentham) + Liberalism (John Locke, JS Mill) — twin philosophical foundations of Moderate ideology; Utilitarianism: right action = greatest good for greatest number; Liberalism: individual rights + rule of law + constitutional governance; together -> Constitutionalism -> Responsible Government + Rule of Law

Cornwallis86-93 — implements rule India the ENGLISH WAY; 4 key actions: (i) all-British senior admin: replaces Indians in senior positions with British officials (corrupt-native-needing-honest-foreigner narrative); (ii) Rule of Law via codification: Charter Act 1793 establishes civil law + protection of individual rights + private property; reintroduces separation of powers at district level (District Collector no longer also District Judge); (iii) Permanent Settlement 1793 in Bengal: Zamindars converted into large landlords on English model; (iv) Aloof Elite: EIC officials discouraged from mixing with Indians; Indian wives discouraged; Eurasians barred from EIC service; EIC officials prevented from purchasing land in India Cornwallis86-93's motivation: had commanded British army's defeat in American War of Independence; watched British settlers develop deep roots -> fought for independence as homeland; determined not to allow same in India: 'Keep rulers separate from ruled; never let India become home' Cornwallis Code / Charter Act 1793 — separation of powers at district level; civil law + individual property rights; foundational document of British India's legal architecture
Tipu82-99 puts trade embargo on Travancore's pepper exports; Travancore is formal EIC ally
EIC begins promoting Indigo cultivation in Bengal — gives loans to 10 European planters (could have given to local zamindars but chose Europeans; preferential treatment from day one)
Alexander Read + Thomas Munro first experiment with Ryotwari in parts of Madras (1792 onwards) — settlement done directly with ryot; ryot held legal title to land

EIC officials recruited by nomination (patronage) — posts purchased or handed through patronage; EIC Directors lobby British Parliamentarians with job offers for their sons; breeds corruption + incompetence; training: essentially on the job
PS1793 — Sunset Clause: Zamindar loses land on non-payment by deadline; Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur, Bihar loses lands under this clause; bitter grievance feeding into 1857

Charter Act 1793 — VEC composition: GG + 3 Ordinary Members + CIC (extraordinary member appointed by CoD); CIC = extraordinary (not ordinary) member; Law Member added as extraordinary for legislative meetings; VEC structure established

Wellesley98-05 serves as GG of Bengal — joined in India by brothers Arthur Wellesley (military commander) & Henry Wellesley (administration + diplomacy) Fort William College established @ Calcutta by Wellesley98-05 — trains British civil servants in Indian languages, laws & customs before posting to districts
1st SA — HYDERABAD (Nizam): signs 1st to get EIC protection against Marathas + Mysore; walked in willingly; 1st Indian state to sign full Subsidiary Alliance
Hyderabad signs 1st Subsidiary Alliance with EIC — pays ever-rising subsidy since then
Ranjit Singh01-39 defeats Zaman Shah's 3rd Afghan invasion — platform for Misl unification
Half of Awadh annexed (Ceded Districts) — forms nucleus of North-Western Provinces; Taluqdars + Primary Zamindars dominated the agrarian economy

Half of Awadh formally ceded to British (Treaty of Lucknow 1801) + added to Bengal Presidency as 'Ceded Provinces'; Scindhia territory conquered in 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05) added -> renamed 'Ceded and Conquered Provinces' under Bengal Presidency

Maharaja Ranjit Singh (RS01-39) — gives rich lands to Udasi Sikh Mahants; Mahants receive resources from Sikh Empire; over time become corrupt + live lives of luxury; British ally with them after annexation of Punjab 1849 Earlier Moplah uprisings (1840s + 1870s) — same agrarian grievance: heavy rents + arbitrary eviction by Hindu Jenmies (hereditary landowners); Muslim Mapilla tenants; same pattern repeats in 1921
Yashwantrao Holkar attacks + defeats both Peshwa Bajirao II96-18 + Daulat Rao Scindhia (who supported Peshwa) — Bajirao II96-18 flees
Child sacrifice @ Sagar Island (Sagar Dwip, where Ganga meets Bay of Bengal) banned by Wellesley98-05 — early sign colonial government willing to use executive power against specific social practices
British get practical control of Orissa by defeating Bhonsle of Nagpur in 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (while Diwani of 'Orissa' held since 1765, it practically only covered Midnapore region until now)
Policy of Non-Interference — EIC follows to prevent war expenditure

Charter Act 1813 — (i) ends EIC monopoly over Indian trade; non-EIC British businesses enter India freely (economic liberalism for British businesses, NOT Indian ones); (ii) legalises entry of Christian missionaries into India (Evangelical influence; Charles Grant, Court of Directors + MP, influences this)
Charter Act 1813 — Christian missionaries enter India; presence in cantonments from 1813 creates anxiety about forced conversion among sepoys

Pagal Panthi Revolt, East Bengal — leaders: Karim Shah -> Tipu Shah; grievance: against zamindars for high rents, illegal abwabs + denial of occupancy rights; Tipu Shah promises lower rents once zamindars + British defeated (political programme delivered through religious leadership); RESULT: crushed by EIC Titu Mir, 24 Parganas — belongs to Wahabi sect; teaches reformist philosophy of Shah Waliullah of Delhi; followers = poor peasants with distinct physical identity (unique beard + dress = marker of resistance); grievances: tax on beards by local zamindar + oppression by indigo planters, zamindars + British officials; action: set up own government with self-imposed taxes; built famous bamboo fort @ Narkelberia village; RESULT: crushed by EIC army

1st Anglo-Burmese War (under Amherst23-28) — Treaty of Yandabo (1826); EIC annexes Arakan + Tenasserim (eastern shore of Bay of Bengal) Sindh annexed — by Ellenborough42-44 (NOT Dalhousie48-56); Charles Napier commands; 'Peccavi' dispatch

1st Burma War 1824-26 + 2nd Burma War 1852-53 -> Burma annexed; finally separated from India in 1937 under GOI Act 1935 NWFP carved from Punjab as Chief Commissioner (CC) Province 1901 — equivalent to Union Territory; directly under central administration

Charter Act 1833 — promises racial equality ('no person to be deprived of chance to enter EIC service on grounds of religion, race, birth or colour'); 'Black Acts' of 1850 attempt to act on this promise -> Europeans protest vigorously ('white rebellion')

Charter Act 1833 — GG(Bengal) -> GG(India); Law Member added for legislative meetings only; Executive Meetings: GG + 3 Ordinary Members + CIC (extraordinary); Legislative Meetings: VEC + 1 Law Member (Macaulay); 1st grain of separation between executive + legislative
Landholders' Society — Calcutta Dwarkanath Tagore Included non-official Anglo-Indians (= Europeans in India, pre-1911); precursor to BrIA1851

Maharaja Ranjit Singh01-39 dies — Sikh State was ideal PoRF buffer; after his death factionalism tears State apart: (i) royal family succession fights; (ii) Sindhanwaliyas (Jat clan/misl); (iii) Dogra Rajputs as Wazirs; (iv) Khalsa Army itself (democratic spirit — wanted Panchayat governance; harder for EIC to manage than feudal-loyal army); succession disputes + political murders follow

Doctrine of Lapse formulated by Court of Directors of EIC — implemented systematically by Dalhousie48-56; principle: if Indian ruler dies without biological heir, rights lapse -> State annexed into British India; deliberately refuses to recognise adopted sons (valid under Hindu law)
Punjab annexed — Punjabi + Gurkha soldiers thereafter actively help British in 1857 (stayed loyal)
British annexation of Punjab 1849 — British in collusion with Mahants vs Chadrites (reform-minded devotees); Mahants backed by British

BETHUNE SCHOOL (1849) established by DRINKWATER BETHUNE (Law Member of the Governor-General's Council, with special interest from Dalhousie ) — a landmark in women's formal education (*19th-c. reform talked ABOUT women — it did not talk WITH them; women were the SUBJECT of reform, not its participants)

British India Association (BrIA1851) attempts to open branches in Bombay + Madras specifically to submit joint petition to London during Charter renewal of 1853 — earliest attempt at all-India coordination

Charter Act 1853 — Law Member of 1833 elevated to full ordinary executive member; 6 more Legal Members added for legislative sessions; Executive Meetings: GG + 3 Ordinary Members + CIC (extraordinary) + 1 Law Member (now ordinary); Legislative Meetings: VEC + 6 Legal Members = 12 persons total
Mohammadan Association (1855) — pro-British; opposes 1857 revolts; seeks benefits for Muslims through loyalty to British (not nationalist cause); earliest organised Muslim political body

Revolt of 1857 — shakes British psychologically: scale of Indian violence against British rule (soldiers, civilians, women, children) breaks the paternalistic narrative; many British conclude Indians simply beyond redemption through reform
1857 Revolt — Mohammadan Association stays loyal to British; post-1857 British further favour Muslims (fear of unified Hindu-Muslim front; already saw Hindu-Muslim unity in 1857 as greatest danger)

Punjabis helped British suppress 1857 revolt; Ghadr newspaper later explicitly criticises this + calls for penance; '31 crore Indians should rise against 1.2 lakh British + repeat 1857 revolt'; masthead of Ghadr carries date of 1857 revolt

Royal Commission on Reorganisation of Indian Army appointed — the Peel Commission (Major-General Jonathan Peel, also Secretary of State for War 1858-59; younger brother of Sir Robert Peel who created modern London police); goal: design 'coup-proof' colonial army
GOI Act 1858 — EIC abolished; GG becomes Viceroy + GG; reports to SoS for India in London; CIC now appointed by SoS (not CoD); same powers

Constitutionalism as framework: Queen Victoria's Proclamation 1858 — promises governance in accordance with India's traditions; Moderates use this as basis for demanding constitutional reform within British framework

Rent Act 1859 — grants occupancy rights to ryots who cultivated same plot continuously >12 years (cannot be arbitrarily evicted); zamindars routinely VIOLATE these rights; rents raised illegally; illegal abwabs (extra cesses) collected

Limitation Law of 1859 (Bombay) — interest on a loan applicable only for 3 years regardless of when ryot repays; moneylenders' workaround: make ryot sign FRESH debt bond after 3 years with accumulated interest added to principal; debt can never truly be paid down
Police Act 1861 + CID (1903) = British intelligence network strengthened enough by 1914-15 to deeply infiltrate Ghadar Movement

Canada gets Dominion Status (1867) — self-governance within British Empire without breaking from it; Moderates later use this as benchmark for their demand: if white-settler Canada can self-govern, why not a civilisation far older?

CORE GRIEVANCES OF INDIAN CAPITAL — (i) British trade + tariff policy systematically favoured British manufacturers; (ii) heavy taxation , incl INCOME TAX introduced in 1868 despite famines ; (iii) restrictions on production of certain goods, incl low-grade steel ; (iv) preference to British firms in contracts + procurement ; (v) no developmental support or institutional credit from the state

Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) — M.G. Ranade sets up; members: K.T. Telang, P.M. Mehta, later G.K. Gokhale + Bal Gangadhar Tilak; aim: represent interests of ALL sections of society (significant departure from landlord focus of earlier bodies); 1875: sends petition to British House of Commons demanding direct Indian representation (one of earliest such demands addressed to Imperial Parliament itself; Prelims 2002: which submitted petition to HoC demanding direct Indian representation 1875 = Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, NOT Deccan Association / NOT Indian Association / NOT Madras Mahajan Sabha)

SASIPADA BANNERJEE , a Brahmo Samajist reformer, sets up a WORKING MEN'S CLUB + launches the monthly journal BHARAT SHRAMJEEVI (1870) — the earliest sign of organised effort (*the modern Indian worker did not exist in meaningful numbers before the 2nd half of the 19th c.; railways + telegraphs + textile mills brought this class into being)

Kuka Revolt — leader: Baba Ram Singh, head of Namdhari Sect; Namdharis = reformist Sikh sect: believe in living Guru + Guru Granth Sahib; strict equality of status for women; reject rituals (rely only on chanting of mantras -> name 'Kuka' = reciter); anti-priestly + strongly pro-cow protection; revolt begins as violence against cow slaughterers + priests -> turns against British; Baba Ram Singh exiled to Burma 1872 Singh Sabha founded 1873 — among 3 organisations that mobilise peasantry in Punjab Canal Colony agitations 1907
A.O. Hume serves as Secretary of Dept of Revenue, Agriculture + Commerce under Viceroy Mayo69-72 — works to improve agricultural yields; reformist orientation established

W.W. Hunter's Indian Musalmans (1871) — argues British neglect of Muslims contributed to Faraizi movement 1830s-70s in Bengal; argues British should appease Muslims for greater political stability; becomes justification for DnR approach of favouring Muslim interests against Hindu-dominated political formations
Census first attempted 1872 (not complete for all of British India); 1881 = 1st FULL census of British India; conducted every 10 years (1881, 1891, 1901...)
Indian Association (1876) founded by SNB — lead actor in many pre-INC agitations; permanent organisational body; SNB uses it to launch Indian National Conference (1883)
Journalists invited to Imperial Darbar form Native Press Association — all-India body; elect SNB as President; resolve to meet annually
Gladstone's Liberal Party wins 1880 British elections; sends reformist Viceroy Ripon80-84 to India; stark contrast with Lytton
Singh Sabha Movement (1880s) — raises issue of Sikh religious reform + control over Gurudwaras; origin of the Akali Movement (1920-25) which later emerges from it

Lord Rosebery coins phrase 'Commonwealth of Nations' (1884) — Annie Besant later popularises the idea of a voluntary Commonwealth of Nations; she authors Commonwealth of India Bill (1925) proposing Dominion Status for India

INC founded @ Bombay — 1st President W.C. Bonnerjee: 'loyal to the British & well-wishers of the British'; Moderat era: 1885-1905; goal = Limited Self-Government within British rule; NOT independence; ultimate vision = Self-Government like Canada or Australia (Dominion Status); Surendranath Banerjea's framing: end 'Un-British Rule' (the gap between Britain's stated liberal values + actual conduct in India)

Moderate era (1885-1905) — methods: prayers + petitions + passing resolutions at annual sessions + press campaigns + debates; no mass action; no street agitation; Gradualism; critics (Extremists) call this 'Strategy of Mendicancy' (= begging); TWO DECADES of petitions + prayers = ZERO demands met

INC 1st session @ Bombay — declared goal: 'building national unity'; India in 1885 = land of regions, languages, castes + religions; no pre-existing single Indian political community; Moderates understand: building such a community is 1st task, even before demanding rights from British; deliberate choice: focus ONLY on issues common to all Indians (Indians vs British; NOT Hindu vs Muslim / UC vs LC / men vs women / workers vs capitalists / ryots vs landlords)
INC founded Dec 1885 @ Bombay — Moderate era begins; 1885-1905 = 20 years of prayers + petitions = zero demands met
Dadabhai Naoroji lays down informal INC rule (1886): Congress will take up ONLY political questions, NOT social or class questions — social issues could divide Indians against each other

Aitchison Commission (1886-88) — recommends civil service reforms; implemented as administrative orders by Lansdowne88-94 NOT as provisions of ICA 1892 (classic exam trap); changes: (i) Covenanted Civil Services (CCS) -> renamed Imperial Civil Services (ICS); (ii) Uncovenanted Civil Services (UCS) -> renamed Provincial Civil Services (PCS); (iii) Statutory Civil Services (created 1878) -> ABOLISHED; ICS-PCS split has federal logic: centre + province as two levels each with own service cadre George Yule — 1st non-Indian INC President @ Allahabad session 1888

INC decision 1888: NO resolution would be passed if majority of Hindu OR Muslim members disagree with it — structural protection of minority community within INC; Prelims context: 1889 Minority Clause = INC (NOT Muslim League) that FIRST formally demanded minority representation in legislative councils

GOPAL BABA WALANGKAR , a Mahar ex-soldier, starts VITAL-VIDHVANSAK ('Destroyer of Ceremonial Pollution') in 1888 — the FIRST monthly journal aimed at the untouchable community , well before Ambedkar's generation

Indentured labour from India accelerates after 1890 — white settlers in South Africa recruit cheap labour; Indians in South Africa = two groups: (i) Memon Muslims (voluntary traders + merchants); (ii) Indentured labourers (brought under bond contracts = tied labour; arrived in large numbers post-1890 to work on sugar plantations + in mines; indentured labour = step above slavery in name only; labourer signed contract usually without fully understanding it = binding him to employer for fixed term under conditions he cannot easily escape)

ICA 1892 (Indian Councils Act 1892 / Lord Cross Act) — SoS: Lord Cross; Viceroy: Lansdowne88-94; simultaneously: result of Moderates' struggle + proof of its failure; gave just enough to show British had listened + little enough to show no intention of conceding power
Tilak at Ganpati Festival 1893 — makes Lord Ganapati (worshipped by both UC + LC) the centrepiece; focus on caste unity goes back to this point even before his later famous quote on untouchability
Tilak publishes Kesari (Marathi) + Maharatta (English) — aggressive use of press; jailed for sedition; deported to Mandalay, Burma 1908-14
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi arrives in South Africa (1893) — young barrister; hired to handle commercial legal case for Memon Muslim merchant; planned to stay briefly + return to India

PIETERMARITZBURG INCIDENT (1893) — Gandhi ejected from first-class railway compartment solely for being Indian despite holding valid ticket; humiliation on cold station platform = his political catalyst; moment he resolves to fight racial discrimination rather than quietly endure it

Mitra Mela founded by Savarkar brothers (Vinayak = Veer Savarkar + Ganesh) @ Nasik — secret society; inspiration: Mazzini's 'Young Italy' (active in 1830 revolts to overthrow Austrian colonialism in northern Italy; Italian unification 1870; Mazzini's method = guerrilla warfare; Savarkar sees direct parallel: Austrian colonialism over Italy = British colonialism over India)

Anushilan Samiti founded @ Calcutta by Pramathanath Mitra (P. Mitra) — begins as body for physical training + character building; inner purpose = cultivate spirit of armed resistance; Prelims 1996: Abhinav Bharat = V.D. Savarkar; Anushilan Samiti = Satish Chandra Basu (correct match)
Fraser Police Commission 1902 — recommends formal establishment of Criminal Investigation Department (CID); implemented 1903

CID (Criminal Investigation Department) formally established 1903 — professionalized network of spies + informers embedded in Indian society; designed specifically to track, infiltrate + dismantle political dissent + secret societies; structural response (not just legal); central to colonial repression throughout INM

Boycott Resolution passed @ Calcutta Town Hall — Moderates including SNB, K.K. Mitra, Anand Mohan Bose + P.C. Ray pass resolution for boycott of British goods + institutions in response to Partition announcement; Moderates themselves cross a line; Swadeshi Movement begins; Prelims 2023: 7 August = National Handloom Day BECAUSE Swadeshi Movement launched on same day in 1905 (Both statements correct, II explains I)

Jugantar party 1906 (Barindra Kumar Ghosh, younger brother of Aurobindo) — Bagha Jatin later reunifies shattered Jugantar factions inside Bengal; Ghadar connects with Jugantar network for Bengal operations
ML1906 founded @ Dacca — initially maintains loyal, deferential tone toward British; founded with British support
Province of 'Bihar + Orissa' created 1912 — combined province after Bengal's 1911 reorganisation

POLL TAX CAMPAIGN (1913) — movement reaches turning point; Poll Tax Campaign = vehicle through which struggle finally acquires MASS CHARACTER; till now largely led by educated Indians (lawyers, merchants, community leaders); poll tax hits indentured labourer DIRECTLY = working class joins
Golden Temple issues Hukumnama (official religious decree) against Chadrites at behest of Mahants (1913) — at British backing; backdrop to later Akali anger

Komagata Maru arrives @ Budge Budge near Calcutta (September 1914) — British try to forcibly transport passengers to Punjab by special train; passengers resist; BUDGE BUDGE RIOT (September 1914): police open fire, killing ~20 passengers; incident radicalises many Punjabis + feeds directly into Ghadar recruitment (proved Indians humiliated both abroad + at home); Ghadarites start returning to India
Gandhi (MG) arrives in India — does NOT rush into mass politics; founds Satyagraha Ashram @ Kochrab (1915); travels + listens + understands the country for nearly 2 years before acting

Lucknow Pact (1916) — INC + ML1906 joint demands: (i) continue Separate Electorates; (ii) expand councils + elected majority; (iii) at least 50% Indians in VEC; (iv) franchise as broad as possible + direct elections; (v) Dominion Status implied; ML1906 agrees to give up R2Vote in unreserved seats; INC accepts Separate Electorates; creates political context pushing British toward reform

Satyagraha Ashram relocated to Sabarmati, Ahmedabad (1917); BHU founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya (1916); Awadh Kisan Sabha context: Baba Ramchandra organising Awadh peasants from ~1918-19 against taluqdars (illegal evictions, nazrana, begar)

INC Lucknow Session 1916 — Rajkumar Shukla (peasant leader from Bihar) meets MG + requests visit to Champaran; grievance = Tinkathia System (ryots forced to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land under contracts with British planters); Tinkathia = 3 kathas out of every 20 must be under indigo cultivation; background: after Indigo Revolt 1859-60 in Bengal, indigo plantation shifted to Bihar by 1863; German synthetic dyes popular after 1895 eating into indigo market globally; but during WW1 those dyes unavailable -> planters pushed Tinkathia harder than ever

Montagu Statement / August Declaration (20 August 1917) — Edwin Montagu (SoS for India) in House of Commons: declares 'gradual development of self-governing institutions with view to progressive realisation of responsible government in India within the British Empire'; KEY WORDS: 'gradual' + 'progressive' (= slow, controlled movement toward self-governance on British terms; demand acknowledged but timeline firmly in British hands); GOI 1919 = conceived as 1st step toward this; deployed by British as DnR tactic to split Moderates from Extremists on Passive Resistance question; Extremists propose Passive Resistance; Moderates + Besant side against it

Montagu visits India personally (unusual step for SoS) — tours various provinces to assess conditions on ground; co-authors joint report with Viceroy Chelmsford16-21 Montagu-Chelmsford Report (1918) — joint document; blueprint for GOI Act 1919; Prelims 2003: Indian Liberal Federation (Moderates who left INC after condemning this Report); Prelims 2004: MC Report -> Act 1919 lineage; Prelims 2015: Act 1919 defined Centre-Province jurisdiction

CHAMPARAN SATYAGRAHA 1917 — MG arrives in Champaran; British authorities order him to leave the district; HE REFUSES = act of CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE (1st civil disobedience on Indian soil; disobeys direct official order; accepts legal consequence; Prelims 2007: first Indian Satyagraha site = Champaran; Prelims 2018: Champaran significance = 1st civil disobedience on Indian soil); govt (uncertain how to handle) makes MG head of Inquiry Committee; MG systematically documents exploitation; convinces administration to abolish Tinkathia System; Champaran Agricultural Act 1918 passed; leaders who accompanied MG: Rajendra Prasad + J.B. Kripalani (teacher by profession; Prelims 2008) + Mazhar-ul-Haq; hallmark = CD; outcome = arbitration method -> legislation

Montague Statement / August Declaration 1917 — promises 'gradual development of self-governing institutions with view to progressive realisation of responsible government in India within British Empire'; GOI Act 1919 = 1st step; built-in 10-year review provision in GOI Act 1919 = mechanism for Simon Commission; Prelims 1998+2013: Simon Commission boycott reason = NO INDIAN MEMBER (violation of principle of self-government promised in Montague Statement)

GOI Act 1919 (Government of India Act 1919 / Montford Reforms / Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) — NOTE: Report (1918) = recommendation; Montford Reforms = popular name for entire package; GOI Act 1919 = actual law passed by British Parliament; CONTEXT: WW1 (1914-19) + Allied propaganda for democracy + self-determination; large Indian war contribution; Ghadar Movement 1913-15 + HRL Movement 1916-18 + Lucknow Pact 1916 = political pressure

GOI Act 1919 (Montford Reforms) — Section 84A built-in provision: review of reforms after 10 years (i.e. by 1929); BUT Simon Commission appointed in 1927 = 2 YEARS AHEAD OF SCHEDULE; reason: Conservative Govt in Britain did not want to leave politically sensitive matter to next govt + pressure from Pro-Changers in INC + rising revolutionary activity + fear of communism spreading in India
Amnesty 1920 — revolutionaries who had been jailed under Defence of India Act 1915 released; enthusiastically join Gandhi's NCM 1920-22

NCM abruptly withdrawn after Chauri Chaura — revolutionaries DEEPLY DISAPPOINTED; no interest in parliamentary politics of Swarajists (Pro-Changers) OR in Constructive Work of No-Changers (Gandhians); return to revolutionary activity; but this time with socialist + secular ideological framework (unlike 1907-15 era)
Bardoli Resolution 1922 — passive phase of INC begins after NCM withdrawal; Simon Commission appointment 1927 = end of this passive phase
Lahore Student Union set up 1923 by Lala Lajpat Rai — Bhagat Singh later works actively in it; parallel to setting up Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha 1926

SIMON COMMISSION (Indian Statutory Commission) appointed 1927 — COMPOSITION: Sir John Simon (head) + 7 members of British Parliament; CLEMENT ATTLEE = one of members (later PM of Britain 1945-51 who oversaw Indian independence); NO SINGLE INDIAN AMONG 7 MEMBERS; this = direct reason for INC boycott; SoS for India BIRKENHEAD challenges Indians: 'draft a constitution yourselves' (believed Indian leaders could not overcome internal differences + act unitedly; taunting Indians; partially proved right by Jinnah's 14 Points 1929)

INC LAHORE SESSION December 1929 — President: JAWAHARLAL NEHRU; 5 major decisions: (i) PURNA SWARAJ = INC goal (NOT Dominion Status); (ii) 26 January 1930 = Independence Day (independence pledge; date = last Sunday of January 1930 = holiday = maximum participation; this WHY 26 January chosen as Republic Day 1950 = date already carried symbolic weight from 1930; Constitution adopted 26 November 1949 = Constitution Day; came into effect 26 January 1950 = Republic Day); (iii) INC rejects RTC (does NOT participate in 1st RTC of 1930); (iv) INC withdraws from legislatures immediately (end of Pro-Changer strategy); (v) AICC (set up Nagpur 1920) empowered to launch CDM at appropriate time; Prelims 2012+2014: Lahore 1929 = Purna Swaraj declared as INC goal

CHITTAGONG ARMORY RAID 1930 — Surya Sen (school teacher from East Bengal) sets up Indian Republican Army (IRA); mobilises even WOMEN into IRA (significant — women as active combatants); raid on Chittagong Armory; declared PROVISIONAL REVOLUTIONARY GOVERNMENT; cut off Chittagong from rest of Bengal by destroying communication systems + railway lines; when British attack = move to hills + villages for guerrilla warfare; 1st time since 1857 that there was GROUP ACTION in armed struggle; Prelims 2001: Chittagong Armoury raid organiser = Surya Sen; Prelims 1997: Match-List Chittagong Armoury Raid = Surya Sen

MG's 11-POINT DEMANDS January 1930 — Irwin26-31 rejects ALL 11; CDM now inevitable; LOGIC: defines what Swaraj would mean for masses; 4 MIDDLE-CLASS ISSUES: (1) lower exchange rate Rupee to 1Rs = 1s 4d (from Hilton-Young Commission 1926 rate of 1s 6d; depreciation boosts Indian exports + discourages British imports); (2) protective tariffs for cotton; (3) full status to Indian Tariff Board; (4) Postal Reservation Bill (50% postal dept seats for Indians); 2 PEASANTS' ISSUES: (5) 50% decrease LR + zero LR during famine; (6) release confiscated property from Bardoli 1928; 5 GENERAL ISSUES: (7) decrease military expenditure + civil servant salaries; (8) amend Arms Act 1878 (right to bear arms for self-defence); (9) total prohibition on intoxicants; (10) release political prisoners not guilty of violence; (11) ABOLISH SALT TAX (8.2% of Govt revenue) + Govt salt monopoly (salt issue not new: demanded also in 1851-52 by BrIA + Bombay Association + Madras Native Association before Charter Act 1853; Salt Act 1882 applied tax + affirmed monopoly)
INDEPENDENCE DAY pledge ceremony — 1st celebration of Independence Day; tricolour hoisted across India; crowd takes independence pledge

DANDI MARCH begins March 1930 — MG marches from SABARMATI ASHRAM (set up 1917) to DANDI coast to break salt law; Prelims 1995: CDM started from Dandi/Sabarmati Ashram; Prelims 2009: Dandi March began the CDM; WHY SALT: consumed by everyone + highlights British oppression even in basic necessities + unites all especially poor + NOT Hindu issue (ML1906 cannot object on communal grounds) + NOT Bourgeoisie issue (CPI1925 cannot label it capitalist cause) + less chance of immediate repression (abolishing salt tax = does not significantly hurt Govt revenues)

SIMON COMMISSION REPORT June 1930 — 7 members; 0 Indians; recommendations: (i) Provincial Autonomy: abolish Dyarchy (GOI1919) + replace with full responsible govt in provinces (with some emergency powers retained by Governor); (ii) NO change at Centre (Centre remains under British despotism); (iii) expansion of franchise (wider electorate but still short of UAF); (iv) retention of separate electorates; (v) NWFP province status + Sindh separation only after Finance Boundary Commission; (vi) SEPARATION OF BURMA from India; Prelims 2010: Simon Commission recommendation = abolition of Dyarchy at provincial level

Pakistan term coined by Choudhary Rahmat Ali in his 1933 pamphlet 'Now or Never' — from Punjab + Afghania (NWFP) + Kashmir + Sindh + '-tan' of Balochistan; NOTE: 1940 Lahore Resolution NEVER USED the word 'Pakistan'; press + public attached the name to it later
Congress Socialist Party (CSP) founded 1934 — Jayaprakash Narayan (JP Narayan) + Ram Manohar Lohia; left wing inside INC; precursor to later left-INC mobilisation

GOI1935 — DEPRESSED CLASSES / SCs: for 1st time get ELECTED RESERVED SEATS with JOINT ELECTORATES (under GOI1919 = only NOMINATED seats); significant step forward; Communal Award 1932 had separate electorates for Depressed Classes but Poona Pact 1932 replaced with joint electorates + more seats; GOI1935 implements Poona Pact model; women's seats = 'internal carve-out' within communal quota (Muslim quota has X seats; within that, some specifically reserved for Muslim women); voting = BOTH men + women vote for women's reserved seats but watertight communal rule still applies (only Muslim men + women can vote for Muslim Women's seat)
Viceroy LINLITHGOW36-43 in office (1936–1943) — during the famine he DID request food for India + proposed a BAN on food exports from Bengal; PM CHURCHILL DENIED BOTH

INC HARIPURA SESSION 1938 — Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose as President; Haripura Address: urged adopting Roman script for Hindi to make common national language easier to learn; DECLARED: Purna Swaraj is goal for WHOLE OF INDIA including Princely States + Princely States are integral part of India (= no special status for Princely States; elected representatives only in CA, no nominees of Princes)
HARIPURA SESSION 1938 — Subhas Chandra Bose elected INC President (first term)

INC TRIPURI SESSION 1939 — Bose defeats Gandhi's preferred candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya in presidential election; Gandhi: 'Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat'; Pant Resolution passed by Gandhian right wing: Bose must form CWC strictly per Gandhi's wishes; BREAKDOWN OF LEFT COALITION: Communists (CPI) voted with Bose against resolution; Congress Socialist Party (CSP/JP Narayan) + MN Roy's followers ABSTAINED on Pant Resolution (chose Congress unity over Bose; feared permanent split destroying anti-imperialist movement); with right wing hostile + left fragmented Bose had no base left inside Congress; Bose unable to function as President without CWC support -> RESIGNS from INC; forms FORWARD BLOC 1939 (left-wing faction inside INC; aim: consolidate left wing + capture INC from within; later becomes political base from which Bose launches international campaign + INA)
THE ESCAPE — Bose escapes in disguise as an AFGHAN → Afghanistan → crosses into the USSR → travels in disguise as 'ORLANDO MAZZOTTA' → Italy → ARRIVES GERMANY March 1941

Congress Working Committee (CWC) at WARDHA July 1942 — accepts MG's idea of Quit India; CWC accepts idea; MG drafts resolution demanding Quit India + committing INC to non-cooperation against Japan if India were invaded; PHRASE 'QUIT INDIA' coined by Yusuf Meherally (same man who earlier coined 'Simon Go Back'); Prelims 2011: Quit India slogan coiner = Yusuf Meherally
Mahadev Desai (MG's personal secretary) dies 15 August 1942 @ AGA KHAN PALACE PUNE (where MG was being held) — MG describes as losing his right hand; deepens public demands for MG's release

INC QUIT INDIA RESOLUTION 8 August 1942 — INC holds special session @ Bombay; followed by massive public meeting @ GOWALIA TANK (AZAD MAIDAN) Bombay; QIM Resolution passed: demand for immediate Purna Swaraj; MG gives historic speech including 'DO OR DIE' (KARO YA MARO) call; lays out plan of action for public; Prelims 2009: Bombay 8 August 1942 = 'Do or Die' call + QIM Resolution; Prelims 2005: Cripps failure -> AICC Bombay 8 August 1942 Quit India resolution

ENTIRE TOP INC LEADERSHIP ARRESTED 9 August 1942 — same night as MG's public speech; detailed resolution NOT made public (public only knew what MG had said in speech the evening before; everything not mentioned in speech = private strategy of movement); ARUNA ASAF ALI hoisted national flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan after leaders arrested
JAPAN OCCUPIES BURMA March 1942 — food imports from Burma, which Bengal had been receiving, STOP ENTIRELY (one of the four causes of the famine)

RAJAJI FORMULA (C.R. FORMULA) 1944 — THREE PLANKS: (1) @ Swaraj: ML1906 should support the goal of PURNA SWARAJ ; (2) @ Transfer of Power: INC + ML1906 should be ready to form a COALITION GOVERNMENT AT THE CENTRE ; (3) @ Unity: AFTER THE WAR, a PLEBISCITE in Muslim-majority regions on the question of partition — if the vote is in favour, the result would be a CONFEDERATION = weak common centre + strong provinces (*link forward to CMP1946 + Syed Ahmed Khan's Two-Nation, One-State theory); Prelims 1998

DESAI-LIAQAT PACT 1945 — negotiated + finalised by BULLABHAI DESAI + LIAQAT ALI KHAN , leaders of INC + ML1906 in the Central Legislative Assembly (CLA) ; goal same as the Rajaji Formula: build INC-ML unity + present JOINT DEMANDS to the British (like LP1916) for a smoother transfer of power; TWO PROPOSALS: (i) in the VEC , ALL ministers to be Indians EXCEPT the Governor General + the Commander-in-Chief; of these Indian ministers, 50% INC + 50% ML1906 ; (ii) in the Central Legislature , 20% of seats reserved for MINORITIES (esp Dalits + Sikhs), remaining seats split EQUALLY between INC + ML1906 — filled initially by NOMINATION , with elections (direct or indirect) to follow; Prelims 2010

SHIMLA CONFERENCE June 1945 — the Wavell Plan is discussed; held after the RELEASE OF INC LEADERS imprisoned during the QIM (1942–45) — the release also formally ENDED THE QIM ; TIMING driven by British domestic politics: CHURCHILL wanted visible progress on the India problem BEFORE ELECTIONS IN BRITAIN ; the plan was based closely on the DESAI-LIAQAT PACT (1945) — because INC + ML1906 had already agreed on it in principle, making rapid acceptance likely; also, any change to the VEC could be made swiftly at the behest of the Governor General; Prelims 1996 + 1998

CABINET MISSION ARRIVES IN INDIA February 1946 — three members: LORD PETHICK-LAWRENCE (Secretary of State for India) + SIR STAFFORD CRIPPS (President of the Board of Trade) + A.V. ALEXANDER (First Lord of the Admiralty); ON THE SAME DAY the NAVAL MUTINY broke out in BOMBAY (*the timing was not a coincidence — it was a signal)
